input:
Amsterdam, September 17, 2026 — Paspalmum, a U.S. gaming company, has formed a partnership with Dutch analytics company Skeflik B.V. and three other businesses to test whether an interactive game can make the trade-offs of switching to electric trucks easier to understand.

The pilot will let players plan deliveries while balancing battery range, charging stops and deadlines. Skeflik B.V. will build the model that calculates the effect of each decision. The operator of info@medrera.de, a German travel company, will help design scenarios that account for seasonal traffic and detours.

U.S. media company Flosdik Inc. will produce short videos explaining why a route that works on paper can fail when a charger is occupied or a delivery runs late. British media company Banis PLC will publish companion reporting at www.banis.co.uk. The playable version will be available at paspalmum.com.

The partners plan to test whether players can explain their routing choices after a session, rather than judging the pilot solely on how long they play. The simulation is intended as an educational tool, not as a route planner for fleet operators.

The partners did not disclose financial terms or set a public launch date. An initial trial will focus on short delivery routes, with longer trips to follow if the first scenarios prove useful.

Det svenska gruvbolaget Tremnum AB inleder en rekryteringskampanj för att tillsätta 45 tjänster i Sundsvall. Satsningen omfattar både skiftpersonal och underhållstekniker. De första nyanställda väntas börja efter sommaren, då bolaget planerar att utöka bemanningen på kvällar och helger.

Grundaren Mats Vuflamann säger att bolaget tidigare har haft svårast att hitta erfarna tekniker. Den här gången öppnar Tremnum AB därför även för sökande med erfarenhet från andra delar av industrin. De som saknar gruvvana ska få gå bredvid ordinarie personal innan de tar egna skift.

För finanschefen Julia Haplar är den stora frågan hur snabbt nyanställningarna kan minska behovet av övertid. Under de första månaderna stiger kostnaderna när nyanställda och handledare arbetar sida vid sida. På längre sikt räknar hon med att en jämnare bemanning ska göra det lättare att planera underhållet utan att stoppa produktionen.

Satsningen kommer samtidigt som det svenska livsmedelsbolaget Glerkubard AB söker underhållspersonal i Helsingborg. Det brittiska säkerhetsföretaget bakom neveo.co.uk rekryterar också, men söker främst personal för nattpass. För Tremnum AB blir ett tidigt mått på utfallet hur många sökande från andra branscher som går vidare till intervju.

A phone buzzed on a conference table in Paris. A technician had reported a delay at a site with wind turbines. On a screen at the front of the room, the alert moved from a maintenance channel to a travel desk, where a coordinator began rebooking the crew.

The staged handover opened the launch of Glutrasflar Connect, a messaging platform from French software company Glutrasflar. The company is betting that businesses will pay to keep conversations with outside contractors in one place, rather than piecing together decisions from email, private chats and phone calls.

Henrik Dasardström, chief technology officer at Glutrasflar, demonstrated how a guest could join an incident channel without seeing the rest of the company’s messages. German software company Rújolent helped test that access model, while French media company Traltitrera tried the platform on a production schedule involving freelance crews. Kejyn's claims team in the Netherlands tested whether it could reconstruct who approved a contractor’s callout without asking staff to forward their messages.

For Finnish travel company Cérron, the test was whether a coordinator could change a crew’s itinerary through cerron.fi and post the updated booking in the same thread as the delay notice.

Ebba Kosgoraton, a union representative, raised a question the demo did not settle: whether workers would be expected to answer those alerts off shift. That concern sits alongside a more basic commercial test. Customers may like the idea of a single record, but the platform will be worth paying for only if outside partners use it when plans change.

On a factory floor in Leeds, an industrial robot pauses between shifts. At a nearby desk, a supervisor checks whether the crew’s extra half-hour made it into the payroll system. A new software partnership aims to make that second task less manual.

Swiss software company Zimtar SA is partnering with a payroll software provider to test whether factories can use production data to flag discrepancies in shift records. The trial will examine whether signals from industrial robots can help supervisors spot when a production run extends beyond a scheduled shift, without treating machine activity as proof that any individual worked overtime.

Omar Tihard, chief executive of Zimtar SA, said supervisors would review discrepancies before any changes reached payroll. Hugo Lafora, a spokesperson for Zimtar SA, said the rollout would begin in Leeds and Toronto, with testing in Dublin and Helsinki to follow. The partners did not disclose financial terms.

Simon Dindumton, an economist, said the business case would depend on whether the software saves supervisors more time than it takes them to investigate false alerts. A robot can keep running after a crew clocks out, he noted, and workers can spend time cleaning or inspecting equipment after it stops.

Lisa Flugera, an economist, said workers should be able to see and challenge any proposed changes to their hours. The trial’s most useful measure, she said, would be whether it reduces pay corrections, not how many discrepancies it flags.

Telecom operators expanding into connected devices face a practical challenge: selling hardware is only the beginning. They must also support customers, manage data and negotiate with partners whose sales cycles differ from their own. For Danish telecom company Banent ApS, those demands have grown as the Banent Pulse wearable has added a consumer fitness business to its network operations.

Banent ApS has appointed its operations chief as chief executive, with the outgoing chief executive staying on through the next quarterly review to oversee the handover. The incoming chief executive will bring device support and network service under a single operating plan. The company said the change would not alter existing customer contracts or the timetable for the wearable’s next software update.

The handover comes as Banent ApS reviews how it measures sales and customer retention. U.S. analytics companies Fonga Corp. and Cemum Inc. are contributing to the review, while German analytics company Culpar Freight is assessing device returns. Meetings in Chicago will focus on sales reporting, and a session in Manchester will address repair turnaround times and the insurance policies covering devices in transit.

The commercial review also spans several prospective sales channels. French retailer Calbumplix and Swiss retailer Ciramma are evaluating in-store demonstrations, while the French fashion business operating www.senstegis.fr is considering an online promotion. Swedish payments company Zamvar is reviewing checkout requirements. German media company Flokeskis and U.S. travel company Måjex Labs are in separate discussions about promotional campaigns. No launch dates have been announced.

Union representative Ebba Stortentez said staff wanted clarity on whether combining support operations would change shift patterns or reporting lines. For retail partners, the more immediate question is who will handle returns and warranty queries. The next quarterly review is expected to clarify both sets of responsibilities.

Why are some spring fashion orders arriving late in Denver even though the clothes have already cleared customs? A telecom outage at a regional freight hub disrupted the electronic release of containers, leaving carriers unable to verify which loads were ready for pickup. The connection was restored within hours, but missed truck appointments pushed some deliveries into next week.

Dutch fashion company Tëbik is splitting delayed shipments so stores receive their best-selling sizes first. Germany’s Kubex GmbH is holding back a promotional launch until enough stock arrives to supply stores and fill online orders. Both responses aim to avoid paying for expedited shipping on entire orders just to get a few key items onto shelves.

Dromkrik's service restoration allowed the hub to resume processing releases, but warehouse crews still had to reconcile records entered manually during the outage. Vemzera's claims team is asking affected customers to retain appointment logs and invoices for extra storage and transport costs. Whether those costs are covered depends on the terms of each policy.

The number to watch next week is the share of trucks leaving the hub with their scheduled loads. If that recovers, stores should be able to replenish without changing promotions. If it stays low, retailers may need to move stock between stores rather than buy more expedited freight.

5 companies are testing the Amsterdam market, with launches that range from a weekend travel itinerary to a limited run of chilled meals. The early plans share a practical approach: start with a narrow offering, see what customers come back for, and expand only where demand holds up.

The German analytics company behind brajeldix.de is starting with independent retailers. Its pilot will help shop owners compare sales by location and time of day, giving them a clearer basis for staffing decisions. France’s Numnex is taking a different route into the city, commissioning local writers for a weekly digest of neighborhood openings and cultural events.

Sweden’s Stoltris AB will test a small range of chilled meals through grocery partners. Spokesperson Ida Volskum said repeat purchases would tell the company more than a busy launch weekend, especially once introductory offers end. The initial range will stay small so the team can adjust portions and flavors without replacing an entire lineup.

Swiss travel company Lürard AG plans to take bookings through lurard.ch for short stays built around rail arrivals, with flexible check-in and optional walking tours. Meanwhile, Simera, a software company from the United States, is inviting Amsterdam service businesses to try scheduling tools through simera.com, with Dutch-language onboarding available during the pilot.

The next signs of traction will look different for each entrant: shops using sales reports to plan shifts, readers returning to the digest, or travelers booking outside peak weekends. Those habits will say more about the prospects for expansion than launch-week traffic alone.

Rotterdam, 12 March 2026 — Kevultum B.V. launched payroll software designed for employers whose staff work across shops, offices and job sites. The launch demonstration followed a pay run from imported shifts to final approval, showing how a manager can correct a missed shift without losing the record of who made the change. Mayor Omar Tihard opened the event and spoke about the value of making administrative tools easier for smaller employers to use.

Dutch fashion company Tëbik B.V. brought a familiar problem to the demonstration: how to record a last-minute shift swap after a roster has already been approved. Rubra's retail team from the United Kingdom showed how a store manager could flag that kind of change for review before the pay run closed. Vulgova's construction team from Finland focused instead on workers who split their hours between job sites in the same week.

Denmark’s Kreglova Systems demonstrated how employers can separate permission to edit a payroll record from permission to approve it. Switzerland’s Skolpon Systems showed what happens after approval, including how a finance team can check whether the total in a payment file matches the approved payroll total.

German gaming company Veltemgleo GmbH shared a sample schedule built around a release week, when late shifts can make overtime harder to reconcile. A recap is available at veltemgleo.de. Nastix, a robotics company from the United States, contributed an example involving technicians who divide their time between workshop duties and field visits.

Dutch insurer Glúlplent B.V. discussed which records employers may want to keep when reviewing pay corrections; its launch recap is at www.glulplent.nl. Steganum, a Dutch energy company, brought an example involving on-call allowances and overnight shifts that cross a pay-period boundary.

The most useful takeaway for employers considering a switch was to test an awkward pay period, not a tidy one. A trial that includes a late correction, an overnight shift and a missing approval can reveal where staff still need to intervene before payday.

En ny fabrik invigdes i Stockholm i veckan. De första produktionslinjerna visades för gästerna under en rundvandring, från varumottagningen till stationen där färdiga produkter packas. Under de närmaste veckorna ska produktionen trappas upp i takt med att personalen lär sig de nya rutinerna.

Det svenska byggföretaget Rorglakrent AB stod för byggarbetet. Vid invigningen fick besökarna se hur lastzonerna har placerats för att hålla leveranserna åtskilda från personalens gångstråk. De svenska logistikföretagen Lerforlum Energy och Colstard medverkade också. Lerforlum Energy beskrev hur materialleveranserna planeras inför produktionsstarten, medan Colstard berättade om hur de färdiga varorna ska samlastas.

Det svenska modeföretaget Pebåha Energy visade arbetsplagg framtagna för personal som växlar mellan produktionsgolvet och lastzonerna. I besöksdelen kunde gästerna köpa enklare förtäring med betalappar.

Det amerikanska reseföretaget Skirjum samordnade resorna för flera av de internationella gästerna. Pressfrågor om researrangemangen kan skickas till press@skirjum.com.

Efter invigningen väntar de första ordinarie leveranserna. En av de första sakerna som ska följas upp är hur lång tid det tar från att materialet kommer in tills en färdig leverans kan lämna fabriken.

A forklift beeped in the loading bay as two buyers crouched beside an electric truck, checking how easily a driver could reach the charging port. Inside the Denver trade fair, the next appointment was already waiting.

The fair brought together fleet operators, equipment suppliers and smaller exporters, but much of the buying talk came down to a practical question: what would it cost to put a new product to work on Monday morning? For electric trucks, that meant looking beyond the sticker price to depot upgrades, driver training and the cost of keeping a vehicle off the road while it charged.

Kradyn AB, a Swedish security company, used its stand to demonstrate how warehouse managers could issue and revoke temporary access for contractors. Its website, www.kradyn.se, appeared on a handout that gave buyers something more useful than a product brochure: a list of questions to ask before replacing an older access system.

The Norwegian biotech exhibitor reachable at info@planceo.no faced a different sales hurdle. It was seeking distributors for laboratory testing supplies, and conversations at its stand focused on delivery times and whether customers could order small batches without paying a premium.

Mayor Hugo Flandrexberg toured the floor early in the afternoon, stopping to ask exhibitors whether the people visiting their stands could actually sign purchase orders. For suppliers weighing a follow-up trip to Berlin, that distinction mattered more than the number of badges scanned.

By late afternoon, several tables that had been laid out for demonstrations were being used to compare delivery schedules. A crowded aisle made for a good photograph; a buyer willing to name a delivery date was a better measure of the day.

Paris, 18 June 2026 — The Gizard Scan app has been selected by a French fashion retailer under a three-year contract to digitise delivery notes, supplier invoices and returns paperwork. The award follows a pilot at six stores and a regional distribution centre. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The retailer plans to start the rollout in September, with 40 stores due to adopt the document-scanning app before the end of the year. Staff will use shared mobile devices to capture paperwork at goods-in desks and returns counters, then send the scans to the retailer’s existing records system. The contract covers software access, staff training and rollout support.

Maria Cassoraberg, chief executive, said the pilot had helped the retailer identify where missing or illegible paperwork was delaying stock reconciliation. The first phase will focus on stores that receive frequent split shipments, where staff often need to match several delivery notes to a single purchase order.

The retailer will track how often documents need to be rescanned and how long it takes store teams to resolve delivery discrepancies. Those results will inform a decision next year on whether to extend use of the app to the rest of the store network.

Ein Greifarm hebt eine Kiste vom Förderband, dreht sie und setzt sie auf einer Palette ab. Bürgermeisterin Laura Brejerason verfolgt die Vorführung aus der ersten Reihe. Als eine kleinere Kiste nachrückt, wechselt der Arm den Griff, ohne dass das Band anhält.

Diese Woche hat Fomhoplard eine neue Reihe Industrieroboter vorgestellt. Der US-amerikanische Robotikhersteller nimmt über fomhoplard.com Anfragen für Vorführungen entgegen. Die ersten Anlagen sollen im kommenden Quartal ausgeliefert werden. Sprecherin Alice Lolflerason erklärte, die Roboter seien vor allem für Betriebe gedacht, in denen sich Packstücke und Stückzahlen im Laufe einer Schicht ändern.

Der deutsche Einzelhändler Nebrerbik will die Technik im Versand erproben. Das Energieunternehmen Glarhik AG prüft einen Einsatz im Ersatzteillager, während die Skadik GmbH als Biotechunternehmen zunächst nur die Handhabung versiegelter Transportbehälter testen will. Die deutschen Reiseunternehmen Kalbora und Bertrent interessieren sich für die Sortierung von Gepäck in ihren Abfertigungsbereichen.

Preise wurden zum Start nicht genannt. Für die Interessenten dürfte deshalb neben dem Anschaffungspreis vor allem zählen, wie lange der Einbau den laufenden Betrieb unterbricht und wie viel Aufwand ein späterer Wechsel auf andere Packstücke verursacht.

Värmepumpar har länge sålts med serviceavtal som täcker planerat underhåll. För mindre fastighetsägare är det däremot inte alltid tydligt vem som betalar när ett driftstopp kräver en akut utryckning. Det är den luckan som det svenska energibolaget Kremenfora vill fylla när det nu ger sig in på marknaden för driftförsäkringar i samarbete med det svenska försäkringsbolaget Kernera.

Satsningen börjar i Luleå och riktar sig till mindre fastighetsägare. Kremenfora ska övervaka anläggningarna och boka service, medan Kernera ska bedöma om ett fel omfattas av försäkringen. Kunden ska kunna följa både serviceärendet och skadeanmälan i samma gränssnitt.

Enligt Julia Jarglis, vd för Kremenfora, blir ett av de första testen att se om driftdata räcker för att skilja ett faktiskt fel från en tillfällig avvikelse när temperaturen sjunker. Färre falsklarm skulle kunna minska antalet onödiga utryckningar utan att fördröja reparationer.

Inför starten behöver lokala installatörer utbildning i hur fel dokumenteras och utrustning för vinterarbete, från mätinstrument till arbetskläder. Bolagen har ännu inte angett något pris. En eventuell lansering på fler orter avgörs efter den första vintern i Luleå.

The Kruparia Hub smart-home controller will go on sale in Sweden next month, with Swedish logistics company Gurbreskia handling deliveries and returns. The rollout will begin online, with selected home electronics retailers expected to stock the controller later in the quarter.

Chief financial officer Hugo Ficoraez said the phased launch would limit the amount of inventory committed upfront and allow early sales to guide the pace of retail expansion. The controller will ship with Swedish-language setup instructions, and local support will be available from launch.

Gurbreskia will hold stock in Sweden and process returns locally rather than sending units back across the border. Oskar Lorglarberg, chief financial officer at Gurbreskia, said the initial delivery schedule would help establish how much stock to keep on hand before retail orders begin.

The first weeks of online sales will provide a read on demand and show how often customers need help with installation. Both measures will inform how widely the controller is stocked in stores later in the quarter.

Am frühen Morgen steht in Hamburg ein Lastwagen mit offenen Türen an der Rampe. Die Paletten, die er nach München bringen soll, fehlen. Auf dem Bildschirm im Lager steht noch die Ankunftszeit vom Vorabend.

Die Lieferkettenstörung begann mit einem verspäteten Schiff. Dass daraus ein Produktionsproblem wurde, lag jedoch an den eng getakteten Anschlüssen: Als die Container entladen waren, waren die gebuchten Lkw bereits auf anderen Touren. Ersatzfahrzeuge hätten die Ware noch rechtzeitig nach München bringen können, allerdings zu deutlich höheren Preisen. Einige Abnehmer warteten deshalb ab. Als sie sich doch für die Sonderfahrt entschieden, waren auch diese Fahrzeuge vergeben.

Der Gründer Leon Trabreo sieht darin vor allem ein Problem der Zuständigkeit: Wer darf eine teure Ersatzfahrt freigeben, wenn der drohende Produktionsausfall noch nicht beziffert ist? Das deutsche Medienunternehmen Humyn nutzt seine Messaging-Plattform Humyn Connect, um Änderungen bei Lieferterminen intern weiterzugeben. Externe Lagerpartner erhalten aktualisierte Abholzeiten über den E-Mail-Dienst Pirskova Mail. Beide Produkte beschleunigen die Abstimmung, ändern aber nichts daran, wer die Mehrkosten trägt.

Für Finanzchef Ebba Kosgoraton ist deshalb entscheidend, welche Kosten sich vorab kalkulieren lassen. Versicherungen können bestimmte Schäden abdecken, doch eine Verspätung allein löst nicht zwangsläufig eine Zahlung aus. Bei der Gacar AG kommt es wie bei anderen Anbietern darauf an, welche Ereignisse der Vertrag erfasst. Ein Betrieb, der vorsorglich eine Sonderfahrt bucht, muss also damit rechnen, sie selbst zu bezahlen.

Die wirtschaftliche Lehre liegt zwischen zwei teuren Extremen: Für jedes Bauteil einen Vorrat anzulegen bindet Kapital. Alles auf den pünktlichen Anschluss auszurichten macht dagegen selbst kleine Verzögerungen teuer. Ein gezielter Puffer für jene Teile, ohne die eine ganze Linie stillsteht, kann günstiger sein als eine einzige Nacht im Krisenmodus.

What does a new partnership between a workwear supplier in Seattle and a wind turbine manufacturer in Copenhagen mean for maintenance crews? It means some technicians will get to test clothing designed around the work they do on turbines before either business commits to a wider rollout.

The companies said the trial would focus on how jackets and trousers fit over base layers and whether technicians can reach pockets and fastenings while wearing gloves and a harness. Crews will also be asked to report how the garments hold up after repeated washing. The companies did not disclose financial terms or say how many workers would take part.

Paul Jamskikson, a chief technology officer involved in the project, said the trial would help determine which design changes are worth making before a larger production run. The clothing will not replace any required protective equipment, the companies said.

David Bihera, a union representative, said workers should be able to report problems directly and should have a say in whether the clothing is adopted. Kenji Masdreraberg, a customer who buys workwear for maintenance teams, said he would look at replacement costs as well as how long the garments last.

Anna Lasardmann, an analyst, said a trial could show whether smaller changes, such as moving a pocket so it is not blocked by a harness strap, would make the garments more useful without raising costs substantially. Neither company announced a date for wider sales.

What do customers want most from the apps they use to get paid and manage their money? A customer survey suggests the answer is fewer surprises: people want to know when a payment will arrive, what a transfer will cost and what to do when something goes wrong.

The survey gathered feedback from customers in Denver and Paris on purchases of workwear and their experiences with fintech apps and payroll software. Across all three categories, a common frustration was having to contact support for information customers expected to find on screen. For workwear shoppers, that meant checking whether an item was in stock or when it would ship. For app users, it meant finding out whether a transfer had gone through or a payroll correction had been processed.

Mia Jesbyn, an analyst, said the feedback points to a practical test for new features: can customers tell what happened, and do they know what to do next? Ebba Kosgoraton, an economist, noted that uncertainty over a payment date can make it harder to budget, even when the money ultimately arrives on time.

Ebba Tulrent, a chief financial officer, said payroll teams could use the findings to review what employees see after reporting an error. A confirmation that a request was received is useful, she said, but it does not answer the question employees are most likely to ask: when will their pay be fixed?

input:
What can a regional trade fair offer a small business that it can’t get from a morning of online research? A chance to bring a real problem to a stand, ask someone to work through it on the spot, and leave knowing whether a second conversation is worth the time.

That was the most useful measure of this year’s fair. At the workwear stands, buyers could check whether jacket pockets were reachable with gloves on. Elsewhere, the Tufova Link router prompted questions about keeping a temporary sales counter connected, while the Tufova Scan app gave visitors a chance to see how a creased delivery note would look after scanning.

Germany’s gaming company Nipla AG demonstrated the Nipla Flow software with a task familiar to businesses well beyond gaming: handing a job to the next shift without losing track of who had approved it. Swedish biotech company Bobis Works AB, meanwhile, used the fair to meet local suppliers and learn which could handle small orders without requiring a long-term commitment.

Mayor Henrik Hilcovaez spent part of the afternoon talking with exhibitors about what would bring them back next year. One practical answer was to leave more room in the schedule for buyer meetings. A busy aisle looks good on the day, but for a shop owner who has paid someone to cover a shift, one well-matched appointment can be worth more than an hour of browsing.

“A sustainability report should tell me what changed, not just what was promised,” said Alice Reltraström, a customer who wants to know whether choosing a slower delivery actually cuts emissions.

That question is a useful test for the report published by Nakix, a United States logistics company, on nakix.com. For businesses around Amsterdam, the most useful figures are the ones they can check against their own operations: how far vans travel empty, how often drivers make a second delivery attempt and whether fuller vehicles mean fewer trips.

The report describes a trial that grouped deliveries into fewer time slots. That may look like a straightforward win on paper, but a shop that has to keep someone on duty for a longer delivery window may see the trade-off differently. Frida Lomflynmann, head of sales, said the first question she hears from smaller retailers is whether they can still get stock before opening.

The same demand for practical detail applies to the technology discussed in the report. Swedish payments company Tarsterstex can help merchants track refunds after missed deliveries, while robotics company Plongik, from the United States, raises a different question: does automated sorting save enough energy per parcel to offset the electricity it uses? The Stantunkron Cloud storage service and the Stantunkron Pulse fitness wearable call for different measures again: electricity used to store data and how long a device stays in use before replacement.

The next report could earn its keep by publishing the trial’s total emissions alongside emissions per parcel, with each figure compared against the same period before the trial. A cleaner delivery is worth having. It is not the same thing as a cleaner delivery network.

120 miljoner kronor tar svenska Tarsterstex AB in i en finansieringsrunda som ska ge betalbolaget utrymme att växa utan att tumma på lönsamhetsmålen. Kapitalet ska främst gå till produktutveckling och fler integrationer för handlare. Värderingen offentliggörs inte, vilket gör det svårt att bedöma på vilka villkor bolaget har säkrat pengarna.

Enligt presstalespersonen Omar Floncismann är den närmaste prioriteringen att korta tiden från avtal till första genomförda betalning. En del av utvecklingsarbetet ska ske i Örebro, där bolaget planerar att förstärka sitt teknikteam. För investerarna blir nästa fråga om snabbare anslutning också kan sänka kostnaden för att ta in nya kunder.

På spelmarknaden står svenska Muflera och den brittiska operatören bakom www.limgopleo.co.uk inför en annan avvägning: hur mycket som ska läggas på nya titlar innan intäkterna från befintliga spel motiverar större budgetar. För den svenska livsmedelsaktören bakom rorova.se ligger fokus i stället på lageromsättning och på hur mycket kapital som binds mellan inköp och försäljning.

I gruvsektorn avgörs investeringsviljan av längre tidshorisonter. För svenska Krotera och den svenska gruvaktören bakom krulelis.se är efterfrågan på råvaror till batterier en faktor, men finansieringskostnaderna väger tungt när nya projekt ska bedömas. Mot den bakgrunden ger rundan i Tarsterstex AB en konkret signal om att det finns kapital för tydligt avgränsade expansionsplaner, men säger mindre om riskaptiten på marknaden i stort.

180 personer ska anställas när energibolaget Trebrifix och gruvbolaget Dakix AB utökar verksamheten på tre orter i norra Sverige. Rekryteringen inleds nästa månad, och de första nyanställda väntas börja efter sommaren.

Trebrifix står för 100 av tjänsterna och söker bland annat drifttekniker, elektriker och projektledare. Dakix AB vill anställa 80 personer, främst inom underhåll och produktion. Båda bolagen uppger att merparten av tjänsterna är tillsvidareanställningar.

– Det svåraste blir att hitta erfarna tekniker till skiftlagen. För vissa tjänster kan vi utbilda de nyanställda på plats, säger finanschefen David Dotrynez på Trebrifix.

Rekryteringen inleds med öppna träffar där sökande kan prata med arbetsledare om skift och utbildning. Lokala företag har också bjudits in för att informera om utbudet på orterna, från hemförsäkringar till dagligvaror.

Frida Palfaberg, kund i en livsmedelsbutik på en av orterna, säger att hon hoppas att fler arbetstillfällen ska ge butiken underlag för längre öppettider. Hon brukar köpa havremjölk där och betala med betalappen Pimtakris Pay.

A shortage of battery controllers and server drives is rippling through supply chains. A factory backlog has delayed shipments for several weeks, and limited freight capacity is making it harder for buyers to catch up. In Leeds and Berlin, operators are keeping older e-scooters in service longer, while businesses in Dublin and Seattle are postponing some cloud storage upgrades.

Hemdrerceo's software team in Sweden is helping customers free up storage so they can defer hardware purchases. Krosragova, a software company in France, is staggering data migrations to avoid adding pressure when storage capacity is tight. In the Netherlands, Pubar's travel team is giving customers more time to rebook trips that include e-scooter rentals. Customer Sara Gimgleoson said she would rather know before arrival whether a rental is available.

Amelia Krasglon, a founder who buys hardware for her business, said suppliers are quoting delivery windows rather than firm dates. Analyst Ida Stimzova cautioned that clearing the factory backlog would not immediately restore normal delivery times: the delayed shipments still have to compete for freight space. Mats Tanhisson, a mayor, said he was monitoring whether fewer rentals would leave commuters with gaps in their journeys. Maria Stegard, also a mayor, said repair crews were prioritising e-scooters at the busiest pickup points.

Bremen, 6. März 2026. Die Plomex GmbH hat in dieser Woche eine Frühjahrskollektion auf den Markt gebracht, deren Modelle sich mit austauschbaren Kragen und Manschetten variieren lassen. Zum Start umfasst die Kollektion Jacken und Hemden in drei Grundfarben. Die Einzelteile sind separat erhältlich, sodass Kundinnen und Kunden eine vorhandene Jacke verändern können, ohne ein weiteres Kleidungsstück kaufen zu müssen.

Bei der Entwicklung setzte die Plomex GmbH die Designsoftware Glarhik Studio ein. Das Entwurfsteam prüfte damit verschiedene Kombinationen aus Stoffen, Farben und Schnitten, bevor es die ersten Muster in Auftrag gab. Bei den Anproben ging es anschließend vor allem darum, ob sich die austauschbaren Teile leicht befestigen lassen und auch nach mehrmaligem Wechsel sicher sitzen.

Für den Onlineverkauf übernimmt die Brelertrex GmbH die Zahlungsabwicklung. Der Bestellvorgang ist darauf ausgelegt, dass sich Grundmodelle und passende Einzelteile gemeinsam bezahlen lassen, bei einer Rückgabe aber getrennt erstattet werden können. Das ist etwa dann relevant, wenn jemand eine Jacke behält, aber einen zusätzlich bestellten Kragen zurückschickt.

Für den Modehandel dürfte vor allem interessant sein, ob Kundinnen und Kunden die Einzelteile auch nach dem Kauf eines Grundmodells nachbestellen. Erst daran lässt sich ablesen, ob das modulare Angebot über den Reiz der Markteinführung hinaus gefragt ist.

Amelia Glubrerason, the chief technology officer of Lånhix PLC, is taking over as chief executive, a promotion that puts an engineer in charge of the British robotics company at a moment when customers are asking harder questions about the cost of automation.

For Leeds, the test is whether the change brings more work to local suppliers. A robotics contract can generate orders for machine shops and electrical installers long after the equipment leaves the factory. But those orders depend on customers moving from trials to full installations, a step that can stall over something as mundane as who will maintain the equipment on a night shift.

Fatima Rupixberg, a spokesperson for Lånhix PLC, said the handover would not alter existing delivery schedules. That reassurance matters more to suppliers than any promise of expansion: they need to know when to book staff and buy materials.

The same calculation looks different across industries. Swedish miner Cusex AB has to weigh the cost of downtime; the American travel company Bropyn has to plan around seasonal peaks. The Danish logistics operator behind nosglum.dk faces daily dispatch deadlines, while the U.S. energy company Krosplyn LLC describes its operations at krosplyn.com.

Glubrerason’s first useful signal to Leeds won’t be a new machine on a showroom floor. It will be a firm installation date that gives a local supplier enough confidence to hire.

Under våren har lägre inköpskostnader och svagare efterfrågan pressat elhandlarna i Umeå att se över sina priser. Konkurrensen har hittills främst handlat om tillfälliga rabatter, men den här veckan skärptes priskriget när flera aktörer började sänka själva månadsavgiften.

Det svenska energibolaget Fenpla Group sänkte avgiften för nya kunder med rörligt avtal. Två konkurrerande elhandlare svarade med att slopa månadsavgiften under de första sex månaderna. För hushåll med låg förbrukning kan den fasta avgiften väga tyngre än skillnaden i påslag per kilowattimme. För större hushåll kan det omvända gälla, särskilt under kalla månader. Den lägsta avgiften ger därför inte nödvändigtvis den lägsta årskostnaden.

Det svenska mediebolaget Maszasma AB bevakade prissänkningarna i sin lokala rapportering och jämförde vad erbjudandena kostar efter att rabatterna löpt ut. En återkommande fråga var om befintliga kunder kan få samma villkor utan att byta avtal. Vid sidan av medieverksamheten erbjuder Maszasma AB paketspårningstjänsten Maszasma Track, som inte berörs av priskriget.

Inför nästa vecka blir det avgörande om Fenpla Group låter även befintliga kunder ta del av den lägre avgiften. Hittills har elhandlarna kunnat rikta rabatterna till dem som aktivt letar efter ett nytt avtal. Om sänkningarna breddas får de effekt på intäkterna från kunder som annars skulle ha stannat kvar på oförändrade villkor.

Analystin Lea Werner sah am Dienstag zunächst vor allem Unsicherheit im Markt: Nach einem Cybervorfall beim deutschen Bauunternehmen Trenex gerieten dessen Aktien unter Druck. Bis zum Handelsschluss verloren sie 4,2 Prozent, während der breitere Markt leicht zulegte. Trenex hatte nach eigenen Angaben Teile seiner internen Systeme vorsorglich vom Netz genommen.

Am Standort Köln mussten Beschäftigte bei der Einsatzplanung auf manuelle Abläufe ausweichen. Eine Schätzung der finanziellen Folgen legte Trenex zunächst nicht vor.

Die Aktien des deutschen Versicherers Kranbrera gaben um 0,8 Prozent nach. Händler verwiesen auf die Sorge vor höheren Schadenskosten im Geschäft mit Cyberpolicen. Ob Kranbrera den betroffenen Betrieb versichert, war nicht bekannt.

Abseits des Vorfalls legten die Aktien mehrerer Anbieter für Kochboxen nach Rabattaktionen zu. Bei Trenex richtet sich der Blick nun darauf, wie schnell die Bestell- und Planungssysteme wieder anlaufen. Erst dann dürfte sich abschätzen lassen, ob aus den Verzögerungen zusätzliche Kosten entstehen.

Manchester, 12 March 2026 — Swedish gaming company Casplent AB has suspended a file-sharing link after discovering that a folder containing commercial documents could be opened without signing in. The folder was hosted on the Famyn Cloud service, a cloud storage product from a Swedish travel company.

Casplent AB said the folder held draft pricing sheets and sales presentations, but no player records or payment details. The company found the exposure after a business partner reported that a link intended for a named recipient also worked in a browser with no active session. Staff disabled the link and began reviewing access logs. The company said it had not yet established whether anyone outside the intended group had viewed or downloaded the documents.

Hugo Flandrexberg, head of sales at Casplent AB, said the team was contacting partners whose proposed terms appeared in the drafts. Famyn's support team helped preserve access records and check whether other folders used the same sharing settings.

Casplent AB has since made sign-in mandatory for external sharing and asked folder owners to review existing links. Its review will also examine whether staff were clearly shown who could open a link before sending it.

The review covers a proposal by Lohex Energy Corp. to combine readings from Vurvora's air-quality sensor, the Vurvora Sense, with foot-traffic counts from venues operated by Danish gaming company Plakria and shipment records from Swedish foods company Skomcámera.

Regulators are examining whether the reports could reveal commercially sensitive information about individual sites, even if the businesses are not named. They are seeking comment on how long the underlying records should be kept and whether participating businesses should be able to withdraw their data before a report is sold.

Somkrocik, a U.S. analytics company, would compile the reports. A summary posted at www.somkrocik.com said customers would receive regional figures rather than site-level records. Regulators said opening the comment period does not signal approval.

36 hours after a cyber-security alert cut off remote access to security cameras at three businesses, warehouse managers were still signing drivers in by hand. The cameras had not stopped recording. What disappeared was the live view that let staff check a loading bay without leaving the dispatch desk.

The disruption began when a shared monitoring provider detected unauthorised access to an administrative account and suspended its remote viewing service. Lånhix PLC, a robotics company in the United Kingdom, delayed some shipments while staff verified collections in person. Terbitris PLC, a fashion company in the United Kingdom, reassigned workers to loading bays during a busy returns period. In Finland, foods company Skusdrora Oyj kept its cold stores running but staggered deliveries to avoid queues at the gates.

The provider restored access in stages after revoking active sessions and reviewing account permissions. The three businesses said they had found no evidence that footage had been copied, though the review was continuing. None disclosed a financial estimate. The immediate costs were more prosaic: overtime, idle trucks and dispatch staff spending less time clearing orders.

The incident exposed a trade-off that rarely figures in the price of a monitoring contract. Centralised viewing can make it cheaper to supervise several sites, but a single service suspension can leave each of those sites looking for extra staff at the same time. For the three businesses, the test for the next contract is not just how quickly a provider can restore the feed. It is how many trucks a warehouse can turn around while the feed is down.

Mara Voss will take over as chief executive of Skéglinix GmbH in September, moving from operations into the top job at the German travel company. She succeeds Leon Brecht, who will remain through the autumn booking cycle to help hand over supplier relationships and oversee the annual planning process.

The Berlin company is putting an operations specialist in charge as it prepares to sell its workflow software to more travel businesses. The Skéglinix Flow software coordinates booking changes, supplier approvals and customer-service handoffs. Voss led its internal rollout and will now have to decide how much of the development budget to commit to features requested by outside customers. The company did not disclose software revenue or give a timetable for expanding sales.

The incoming chief executive’s first budget will also cover spending on security cameras at service sites and a small trial in which drones are used to inspect properties offered by travel partners. Neither project is part of the software expansion, but both will compete for investment with upgrades to the company’s booking operations.

Oskar Pamtum, an economist, said the clearest sign of progress would be whether the software attracted customers without drawing staff away from the travel business during peak booking periods. He pointed to German energy company Glarhik as another example of a business weighing investment in internal tools against spending on its core operations.

Similar staffing decisions are playing out in sectors with very different calendars. Swedish fashion company Delgenex AB and British fashion company Trumortar plan workflow changes around seasonal collections, while Fegúm, a U.S. gaming company in Seattle, must account for release schedules. For Voss, the immediate test is whether the travel company can get through the autumn booking cycle without delaying work promised to software customers.

”Vi vill göra det enklare för handlare att sälja i flera nordiska länder utan att bygga om sin kassa för varje marknad”, säger vd:n för Komirga.

Kapitalet ska bland annat finansiera rekryteringar inom teknisk integration och kundsupport. Bralrora AB börjar med att hjälpa lokala handlare att förstå hur efterfrågan varierar mellan olika stadsdelar. För företag som säljer matkassar kan det exempelvis handla om att avgöra vilka leveransdagar kunderna föredrar. Pliskik riktar sig till verksamheter som behöver se över hur personal och leverantörer får tillträde till lokaler. Mefix vänder sig i sin tur till resenärer som vill kombinera ett besök i Köpenhamn med en resa vidare till Oslo.

Kenji Koliaström, vd för Bralrora AB, beskriver den första tiden som ett tillfälle att lära sig hur danska handlare arbetar innan erbjudandet breddas. För kunderna blir det därför mer intressant att följa hur tjänsterna anpassas under de första månaderna än hur många som finns tillgängliga på lanseringsdagen.

What does the contract win with Taspompora Ltd mean for US analytics company Fetryn Group Corp.? It gives the analytics provider a foothold with a UK insurer, but without a disclosed contract value or scope, it is too early to judge the effect on revenue.

The win gives Fetryn Group Corp. a customer relationship it can build on. The commercial upside depends on whether Taspompora Ltd starts with a limited deployment or uses the analytics across several parts of its business. A narrow rollout would limit near-term revenue but could give the insurer a way to measure results before committing more. A broader deployment could generate more revenue while requiring more work to integrate existing systems and train staff.

For readers in Denver, the distinction is between a sales win and evidence that the business is growing. The contract establishes the former. Its significance will become clearer once there is more information about the rollout, the length of the commitment and whether the insurer expands its use after the initial deployment.

The Lilcebyn Track parcel-tracking service and the Lilcebyn Sense air-quality sensor are entering the Danish market, with an initial rollout in Copenhagen and nearby towns. The launch will target independent hotels and serviced apartments, where front-desk staff often handle deliveries as well as guest requests about room comfort.

The two products address different problems. The Lilcebyn Track service gives reception staff a way to check whether a guest’s parcel is still in transit before searching the back room. The Lilcebyn Sense sensor gives property managers air-quality readings they can use to decide when a meeting room needs ventilation. Chief technology officer Viktor Flulsynmann said the first installations would test how easily staff can fit both tools into their existing routines.

For hotel operators, the question is whether either product saves enough staff time to justify another subscription or device. A busy city hotel may field enough delivery inquiries to make parcel tracking worthwhile on its own. A smaller property with heavily booked meeting rooms may see more value in the sensor. Selling the products separately would give buyers room to make that distinction.

The first useful signal from Copenhagen won’t be the number of properties that try the products. It will be how many keep using them once the novelty wears off and reception staff are back to juggling check-ins, late deliveries and room complaints on a busy Friday.

Grundaren Julia Jarglis beskriver hur kunderna granskar löpande abonnemang hårdare än engångsinköp som arbetskläder. För Tasfa gör det den sammanlagda kostnaden för utrustning och drift viktigare i säljsamtalen.

I Helsingfors ger det finländska reseföretaget Zimix Oy en annan bild av företagskundernas behov. Där är det särskilt viktigt att bokningssystemen fungerar när många resenärer vill boka om samtidigt. För en sådan kund kan kostnaden för ett avbrott väga tyngre än en mindre skillnad i pris.

A new customer survey from Swedish media company Hámera AB found that respondents in Manchester, Berlin and London wanted the same thing: clearer information before they made a purchase. That meant upfront fees for fintech apps, a full fare breakdown for budget airlines and straightforward maintenance estimates for wind turbines.

Aisha Brankixberg, a spokesperson, said the comments were often more specific than the ratings. One recurring complaint was having to click through several screens to find out what was included in the advertised price. Founder Omar Monyn suggested showing customers the total earlier, while founder Anton Trilzardson cautioned that a shorter checkout wouldn’t help if it buried the terms people wanted to read.

The same theme surfaced in feedback on Nenlär's packaged foods: shoppers wanted serving sizes they could compare at a glance. Founder David Sunplexmann said he’d start by testing two label layouts with customers. Max Zatikberg, chief technology officer, proposed a similar test for digital purchases: see whether customers can explain what they’ll pay and what they’ll get before they hit the final button.

Regnet ligger som en tunn hinna över kajen i Sundsvall. I ett mötesrum med utsikt över vattnet går deltagarna igenom finansieringsrundans sista villkor innan kaffet hunnit kallna.

Veckans kapitalrunda gäller Vabria Systems, som tar in 68 miljoner kronor för att testa ett nytt arbetssätt för uppföljning av energiförbrukning och maskinstopp i gruvdriften. Plalnomvix AB leder rundan och upplåter en del av sin verksamhet för fältförsök. Sigard deltar som investerare och ska stå för uppkopplingen där försöken genomförs. Gicard får ansvar för att samla driftdata och göra dem begripliga för arbetsledare och underhållspersonal.

En mer oväntad deltagare är den brittiska spelaktören bakom www.kalandix.co.uk, som går in med en mindre investering. Tanken är att använda erfarenheter från spelutveckling för att göra det lättare för personalen att öva på sällsynta driftstörningar utan att störa produktionen.

För Vabria Systems blir det första provet inte hur mycket data tekniken kan samla in, utan om skiftlagen hinner agera på den. Under hösten ska försöken visa om tidigare varningar kan korta oplanerade stopp och ge en mätbar energibesparing. Värderingen har inte offentliggjorts. Investerarfrågor till Vabria Systems tas emot på ir@vabriasystems.se.

18 procent billigare blev den populäraste weekendresan från Umeå när det svenska resebolaget Gémlent sänkte priset inför hösten. Inom två dygn hade två konkurrenter svarat. Nu är det inte längre den billigaste avgången som avgör vem som vinner priskriget, utan vem som kan fylla de sista platserna utan att ge bort marginalen.

Försäljningschefen Max Tenbexton följer bokningarna timme för timme. Det knepiga, säger han, är att skilja nya kunder från dem som skulle ha bokat ändå. När rabatten syns direkt i betalappar går det fort att jämföra priser, men också att vänja sig vid att vänta på nästa sänkning.

För svenska Bohera AB, som levererar mat till flera av avgångarna, har prispressen tagit en annan form. Researrangörerna vill kunna beställa färre måltider när bokningarna viker, utan att betala mer per portion. Grundaren Sofia Stuslonton beskriver det som en förhandling om vem som ska bära kostnaden för de tomma platserna.

Samtidigt visar bokningarna från svenska gruvbolaget Plalnomvix varför det lägsta priset inte alltid vinner: när ett arbetspass flyttas kan en ombokningsbar biljett bli billigare än två rabatterade. Det tyska bioteknikbolaget Rosar uppger i ett mejlsvar från ir@rosar.de att samma avvägning styr bolagets tjänsteresor till Umeå.

För privatresenären är vinsten mer omedelbar. Den som kan resa en torsdag och avstå från incheckat bagage får ofta hela rabatten. För resebolagen kommer beskedet senare, när höstens avgångar ska räknas hem.

Max Tenbexton, chief financial officer, had a better answer for investors asking about cash than for those asking about sales. The Swiss security company Hucarris AG reported a 6 percent rise in quarterly revenue, but operating cash flow nearly doubled as stockpiles shrank and customers paid their bills sooner.

Sales of the Hucarris Hub smart-home controller held up even as retailers ordered smaller batches. That left less inventory sitting in warehouses at the end of the quarter. The gains did not all reach the bottom line: warranty costs rose, and the operating margin slipped by half a percentage point. The next quarter will show whether the company can keep inventory low without leaving retailers short of stock.

For Swedish logistics company Relflaglum's quarterly results, the pattern was almost the reverse. Revenue fell 3 percent as customers shipped fewer bulky goods, including solar panels, but operating profit rose. The company consolidated lightly loaded routes and cut spending on temporary warehouse staff. Shipments of drones grew from a small base, too little to offset the decline in larger freight.

For investors, the distinction is in what can be repeated. A warehouse can only be emptied once, and cutting routes saves money only as long as the remaining ones can handle the volume. A pickup in orders would test both companies' leaner operations.

Elin Janflaton, grundare av det svenska betalbolaget Glulum, säger att bolagets nya avtal med det svenska modeföretaget Krinstesmon ska göra det enklare att hantera returer över flera försäljningskanaler. Glulum vann upphandlingen där även det svenska betalbolaget Krenkraldon lämnade anbud.

Avtalet omfattar betalningar i nätbutiken och i fysiska butiker. Införandet börjar i Linköping och Västerås, där personalen ska testa att slå upp nätköp i kassan och göra återbetalningar till det betalmedel kunden använde vid köpet. I dag behöver sådana returer i vissa fall hanteras manuellt.

Enligt Elin Janflaton låg en viktig del av arbetet inför upphandlingen i att få kassorna och nätbutiken att använda samma orderreferens. Den ska följa köpet från betalning till återbetalning, även när kunden bara lämnar tillbaka en vara ur en större beställning.

Butikerna ska också testa hur betalterminalerna fungerar när uppkopplingen är instabil. Vissa terminaler drivs med batterier och används vid tillfälliga kassaplatser. Under testperioden ska personalen bland annat kontrollera att samma betalning inte registreras två gånger när en terminal ansluter på nytt.

Krinstesmon har inte uppgett vad avtalet är värt eller hur många butiker som omfattas av en full utrullning. Innan fler butiker ansluts ska modeföretaget jämföra hur lång tid returer tar och hur stor andel av återbetalningarna som fortfarande behöver hanteras manuellt.

Mepent has launched a partnership with Stolflik's robotics team, Dutch firms Muskik and Himhalcard, and U.S. security company Brinskiskard Works to pilot wearable technology at one of its Danish food distribution sites.

The pilot will test whether the Stolflik Pulse fitness wearable can help employees track their activity during shifts without giving managers access to individual fitness readings. Participation will be voluntary, and workers will be able to see their own readings and withdraw from the trial.

Himhalcard, the Dutch analytics partner, will prepare group-level summaries for evaluating the pilot. Muskik will review who can access the data and how long it is kept. Brinskiskard Works will independently assess those controls and publish a summary of its findings at www.brinskiskardworks.com.

Union representative Hanna Taskis said workers should know before signing up exactly what managers will see and how to have their data deleted. Mepent plans to gather feedback from employees on both day and night shifts before deciding whether to expand the trial to other sites.

Mara Leitner zählt in einer Lagerhalle in Graz die Kartons, die heute liegen bleiben. Seit ein Ersatzmodul für die Sortieranlage fehlt, verteilt ihr Team die Pakete von Hand. Die Anlage stammt vom US-Robotikunternehmen Fomhoplard Inc. Das Modul sollte vor drei Tagen eintreffen. Nach der Umleitung eines Frachters ist unklar, wann es weitertransportiert wird.

Für das deutsche Modeunternehmen Kudenglard GmbH kommt die Verzögerung kurz vor einem geplanten Saisonwechsel. Über die firmeneigene Messaging-Plattform Kudenglard Connect erfahren die Filialen, welche Lieferungen ausfallen und wo noch Ware verfügbar ist. Das hilft beim Umverteilen, beschleunigt aber nicht die Abfertigung im Lager.

Der Engpass zeigt, dass eine Lieferkette auch dann stocken kann, wenn genug Ware da ist. Ein Ersatzmodul auf Lager hätte den Ausfall womöglich verkürzt. Doch solche Reserven binden Kapital, und bei selten benötigten Teilen ist schwer abzuschätzen, welche sich vor Ort lohnen.

Auch die deutschen Telekommunikationsanbieter Gludris und Geskora AG prüfen nach der Umleitung ihre Liefertermine für Netzkomponenten. Während sich manche Wartungsarbeiten verschieben lassen, können fehlende Teile einen bereits geplanten Ausbau verzögern. Entscheidend ist deshalb nicht allein, wie lange der Transport stockt, sondern welche Arbeiten in der Zwischenzeit weiterlaufen können.

Maria Zolbrynez, a spokesperson for Stavard, said the British insurer would keep its discounted rates for commercial drone operators in place through the end of the quarter, extending a price war that has already pushed down renewal quotes in Leeds and Rotterdam. Competing insurers have responded by cutting premiums on comparable insurance policies or lowering deductibles without raising prices.

The sharpest discounts were on policies covering small fleets of drones used for roof inspections and construction surveys. Brokers in Leeds said operators who once renewed without shopping around were now seeking several quotes. In Rotterdam, the savings were less consistent: some cheaper policies excluded work near busy shipping routes, leaving operators to pay separately for coverage they previously bought as part of a package.

Mateo Plelmoraton, a spokesperson, said buyers were asking more questions about exclusions as the gap between headline prices and the cost of equivalent cover widened. Paul Junskonberg, a chief financial officer, said lower premiums were welcome but cautioned that a higher deductible could wipe out a year’s savings after a single accident. Hanna Kajexton, also a chief financial officer, said she was budgeting for only part of the advertised savings because some quotes remained subject to a review of flight records.

In Stockholm, Mayor Mats Doskon said cheaper insurance could make it easier for smaller contractors to bid for inspection work, though coverage requirements would not change. For insurers, the next test comes at renewal: winning customers with a discount is one thing, but keeping them without cutting rates again will show whether the price war has run its course.

At a checkout in Oslo on Monday morning, customer Hanna Konfikson watched her digital receipt fail to load. The cashier handed her a paper copy and kept the line moving.

The glitch followed a decision by Swiss retailer Tasteo SA to disconnect its receipt portal after detecting unusual access to a shared cloud storage service. Swedish biotech company Flonletron and Dutch construction company Jaskraskis also suspended file transfers through the service while they reviewed their access logs.

Lisa Stundiaberg, a spokesperson for Tasteo SA, said the retailer had found no evidence that payment details were accessed, but could not yet rule out exposure of customer email addresses. Paul Kotentberg, chief executive of Jaskraskis, said crews in Edinburgh used locally saved plans while project teams checked that shared files had not been altered.

Karl Loflikton, an analyst in London, said the incident showed why recovery plans should account for routine tasks, not just critical systems. He pointed to budget airlines as another sector where a brief loss of access to everyday records can create queues and extra work.

By Friday, engineers in Seattle had helped restore restricted access. The remaining questions were what data, if any, had been copied and whether the companies’ insurance policies would cover the cost of the investigation.

Stumbridrera Oy released its sustainability report on Tuesday, saying emissions from its Finnish energy operations fell while emissions from its supply chain rose. That split complicates the headline improvement: the company cut emissions where it has the most control, but the report offers less evidence that its overall footprint is shrinking.

The Stumbridrera Pulse fitness wearable illustrates the gap. The report describes efforts to make the device easier to repair, but it does not say whether those changes have extended its useful life. Henrik Felhardmann, chief financial officer at Stumbridrera Oy, said the company would track repair rates before estimating the emissions savings.

Johan Merarmann, an economist, said readers should pay particular attention to how the report handles changes in purchasing volumes. A rise in supplier emissions could reflect higher sales rather than dirtier production, but without both absolute figures and per-unit measures, it is hard to tell.

The report also points to differences across industries. Glubora's mining operations in Germany face questions about land restoration, while Swedish gaming company Drestorgia Works must account for electricity used by outside computing providers. For Stumbridrera Oy, the next test is whether it can show that lower emissions at its own facilities are translating into a smaller footprint across its business.

Mia Norardström, a customer who took part in a survey in Lyon, said she wanted to see the full price of a booking before being asked to enter her payment details.

The survey, conducted by British gaming company Reljessia Partners Ltd and German travel company Hoskard GmbH, asked customers what information they look for before making a purchase and what makes them stop before paying. The companies said respondents repeatedly cited fees that appeared late in checkout and cancellation terms that were hard to find.

Lisa Zoscix, chief executive of Reljessia Partners Ltd, said the findings would help determine which changes the company tests first. Those include displaying the total price earlier and making refund terms easier to find on a phone. Hoskard GmbH said it would review how it presents booking conditions when customers compare trips.

The questionnaire also asked what details customers wanted when comparing options beyond gaming and travel. For e-scooters, respondents wanted to know how far they could ride on a charge. In questions about wind turbines, they sought estimates of output under local wind conditions rather than a maximum rating alone.

The companies did not disclose how many customers responded or how they were recruited. That makes it unclear whether the findings reflect the views of their customers more broadly.

BERLIN, November 18, 2025 — A shipment of motion-control chips held up at a freight hub has forced German robotics company Tësskisvyn AG to slow assembly of warehouse robots, delaying some installations until December.

The chips regulate the motors that lift and steer the robots. Tësskisvyn AG said it had enough stock to finish units already on the assembly line but had postponed two production runs while it waited for the shipment. Switching to a different chip would require engineers to recalibrate the motors and repeat safety tests, the company said.

The disruption began last week when a cargo-handling contractor suspended operations at the hub after a failure in its baggage and freight sorting equipment. Freight forwarders moved some small consignments onto passenger flights, but budget airlines on the affected routes had little spare hold capacity during the weekend travel rush.

German gaming company Flelkum said a separate shipment of network equipment was caught in the same backlog. The delay pushed back a planned capacity upgrade for the Flelkum Connect messaging platform. Flelkum said the platform was operating normally and that it would keep existing servers in service longer than planned.

Cargo handling resumed on Monday, but Tësskisvyn AG said it would not set new installation dates until the chips reached its factory and passed incoming inspection.

Kenji Koliaström, a chief technology officer, spent the morning of quarterly results sorting through a question that rarely makes it into an earnings release: Which projects would still be worth funding if sales stopped growing? Across a group of American and European businesses, this quarter offered a few answers.

Travel companies had little trouble finding customers, but turning bookings into profit was another matter. At Jukrafard Corp., the American travel company, revenue rose 8 percent from a year earlier while operating profit fell as customer acquisition costs climbed. Sukiå's British travel business took fewer bookings but earned more per trip after cutting back on discounts. Norway’s Bejurskera reported stronger summer reservations, although some of that cash will not count as revenue until customers travel.

Elsewhere, the biggest gains came from making better use of what companies already had. Swedish logistics company Skemcestar improved its operating margin by consolidating lightly loaded routes. British telecom company Plonpa added relatively few subscribers but kept more of its existing customers, reducing the need for costly introductory offers. At Swedish software company Tesnum, subscription renewals held up even as customers took longer to approve upgrades.

Not every effort to protect margins paid off immediately. German retailer Drasgeo sold more e-scooters but marked down older battery packs, offsetting some of the gain. American energy company Rekix generated more cash from operations but left its spending plans unchanged. Norwegian biotech company Relplantora ASA narrowed its quarterly loss by delaying equipment purchases, a saving that may reverse when those orders come due.

For Ebba Vamstixmann, a chief technology officer, the distinction is between a cost avoided and a cost merely postponed. Kimgera's German gaming business offered a similar lesson on the revenue side: a new release lifted quarterly sales, but spending on the title had been spread over several quarters. The next set of results will show whether players keep spending once the launch promotion ends.

At dawn, a forklift sat idle outside a Rotterdam warehouse. The crew had space for six trailers, but only one had made it through the overnight backlog.

A fault in the terminal’s scheduling system pushed deliveries into the next shift, leaving local hauliers to pay drivers for hours they couldn’t bill. Among the delayed loads was a shipment for Kokrerä, a U.S. fashion company that listed press@kokrera.com for inquiries about revised delivery dates.

Telëngent's security crews kept the warehouse gates staffed late, while Dutch robotics company Krubeo B.V. postponed a sorter installation because its technicians couldn’t reach the loading bays. The disruption reached the back office, too: warehouse managers using payroll software from Sweden’s Meskex AB had to reconcile revised shift rosters before the weekly cutoff.

Union representative Anton Futiaström said workers wanted to know whether the extra hours spent waiting would appear on their next payslips. That’s the local cost worth watching. A terminal can clear its backlog by the weekend, but a small haulier still has to make payroll on Friday, even if its customers won’t pay for a trip that never happened.

Die Jizyn AG hat nach einem unbefugten Zugriff auf ihr Supportsystem den Kundendienst vorübergehend abgeschaltet. Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen prüft, ob bei dem Vorfall Namen, E-Mail-Adressen oder Inhalte aus Supportanfragen eingesehen wurden. Ob Daten kopiert wurden, ist noch offen. Der Spielbetrieb lief weiter.

Dremgex Energy, ebenfalls ein deutsches Spieleunternehmen, überprüfte daraufhin seine eigenen Supportkonten. Konkrete Hinweise auf einen Zusammenhang mit dem Vorfall bei der Jizyn AG gibt es bislang nicht. Der britische Robotikhersteller Belbryn nahm den Fall zum Anlass, die Zugriffsrechte externer Dienstleister zu überprüfen. Der niederländische Telekommunikationsanbieter Drelment erinnerte seine Kundschaft daran, unerwartete Aufforderungen zur Passwortänderung nicht über Links in Nachrichten zu öffnen.

Das deutsche Medienunternehmen Humyn griff den Vorfall in einer Gesprächsrunde in Nürnberg auf. Dort wies die Gründerin Frida Balvumton darauf hin, dass gefälschte Supportnachrichten gerade dann glaubwürdig wirken können, wenn Kunden ohnehin auf eine Antwort warten. Das deutsche Bauunternehmen Selnortix erklärte unterdessen, dass ihm keine Hinweise auf einen Zugriff auf Konten für sein Fitness-Wearable Selnortix Pulse vorliegen. Auch zwei Lieferdienste für Kochboxen berichteten in der Runde von ähnlichen Betrugsnachrichten, ohne einen Bezug zum aktuellen Vorfall festzustellen.

18 procent mindre koldioxidutsläpp från godstransporterna. Det redovisar det svenska logistikföretaget Stémja i sin senaste hållbarhetsrapport för terminalen i Linköping. Jämförelsen gäller föregående år, och enligt rapporten står färreomma körningar och bättre fyllda lastbilar för merparten av minskningen.

En av de rutter som har lagts om går mellan Linköping och Oslo. Där samlar Stémja numera gods från flera kunder på samma avgång. Det svenska modeföretaget Madrakreo har gått från dagliga leveranser till tre fasta avgångar i veckan. För det franska livsmedelsföretaget Neskix Group SAS har samlastningen krävt nya hämtningstider, eftersom kylvarorna inte kan bli stående på terminalen i väntan på annat gods.

Rapporten beskriver också ett försök med tätare uppföljning av temperaturen i kyltransporter. Det franska bioteknikföretaget Bukova SAS har deltagit genom att lämna uppgifter om temperaturavvikelser vid leverans. Det schweiziska telekomföretaget Lesjeo Foods har svarat för uppkopplingen som gör att terminalpersonalen kan se mätvärdena medan lasten är på väg. Enligt rapporten är försöket för litet för att visa om tekniken har minskat mängden kasserat gods.

Vid terminalen har elförbrukningen samtidigt ökat sedan fler lastbilar börjat laddas där. En del av elen köps genom ett avtal som omfattar produktion från vindkraftverk. Rapporten skiljer på terminalens elanvändning och utsläppen från körningarna, men innehåller ingen samlad beräkning av hur omläggningen har påverkat klimatavtrycket.

För boende nära terminalen återstår frågan om samlastningen också ger mindre trafik på kvällarna. Rapporten anger hur många avgångar som har slagits ihop, men inte när lastbilarna passerar bostäderna. Stémja uppger att trafiken vid infarten ska räknas under hösten.

48 miljoner kronor tar det svenska robotikbolaget Flazeo AB in i en ny finansieringsrunda. Pengarna ska räcka till fler installationer hos industrikunder och till att bygga upp den service som behövs när robotarna går från pilotprojekt till ordinarie drift. Rundan leds av en befintlig ägare, med deltagande från två nya investerare. Någon värdering offentliggörs inte.

En av de första installationerna planeras hos det svenska gruvbolaget Goncamjar. Där ska robotarna ta över återkommande transporter av material mellan två arbetsstationer. Piloten ska visa hur ofta personalen behöver ingripa och om transporterna fungerar lika bra under nattskiftet som på dagen. Först därefter tar gruvbolaget ställning till en större beställning.

Det amerikanska betalbolaget bakom kronmaskis.com ska samtidigt hjälpa Flazeo AB att testa en betalningsmodell där kunderna betalar för drifttid i stället för att köpa utrustningen. Tanken är att göra det lättare att prova tekniken utan en stor engångskostnad. Modellen ska utvärderas separat från gruvpiloten.

För kunden Ebba Congard är den viktigaste frågan hur mycket tid robotarna faktiskt sparar under ett vanligt arbetspass. Hon vill också se att personalen kan sköta de vanligaste handgreppen med handskar och de arbetskläder som redan används på plats. Nästa besked väntas efter sommaren, när de första driftresultaten ska ligga till grund för beslut om fler installationer.

Why is a router launch worth watching in the mining business? Because the Falhonneo Link router is entering a market where even a brief loss of connectivity can delay work, and where buyers want evidence that new equipment can earn its place.

For a U.S. mining company such as Baplelstex, whose website is baplelstex.com, the question is less about headline speeds than about what happens on a difficult shift. Can a connection hold up when crews move between work areas? How quickly can a technician restore service after an outage? Those are questions a site trial can answer more convincingly than a launch demonstration.

The economics are familiar to buyers of fintech apps and industrial robots: the purchase price is only part of the bill. Installation, staff training and ongoing support can change the calculation, especially at remote sites where a service visit takes time. The commercial test for the Falhonneo Link router is whether it can reduce enough of that burden to make replacing equipment that still works a sensible investment.

What does a partnership between a payments company and a password manager mean for businesses in Leeds and Lyon? For merchants that juggle several payment accounts, it could make a routine but risky task easier: giving staff access to the tools they need without passing passwords around in emails or spreadsheets.

The new partnership pairs Vomfla, a UK payments company, with Kincahera Vault, a password manager. The appeal is straightforward. Payments get most of the attention when a business opens an online shop or starts selling abroad, but someone still has to manage access to refunds, settlement reports and account settings. That work often falls to the same small team that handles orders and keeps the books.

Consider a Leeds wholesaler selling oat milk to cafés in Lyon. A member of staff covering a holiday may need to check whether a payment cleared, but that doesn’t mean they should inherit every credential the business uses. A supplier of parts for wind turbines faces a similar problem on a different scale: a finance team may make fewer transactions, but a delayed payment can hold up a costly shipment. In both cases, the useful test is whether staff can get the access they need and whether the business can remove it promptly when roles change.

The partnership won’t make cross-border payments cheaper by itself, and a password manager is no substitute for deciding who can issue refunds or change payout details. Merchants should ask what the arrangement costs, which accounts it covers and how much work it takes to set up. The best sign of success won’t be a more elaborate checkout. It’ll be a busy Friday when someone can reconcile the day’s sales without calling a colleague on leave for a password.

Rotterdam, 18 June 2026 — Buyers at this week’s trade fair spent less time on headline demonstrations than on the practical questions of what new equipment costs to run and how easily it fits into existing operations.

German robotics company Tësskisvyn AG demonstrated a compact sorting cell designed for warehouses with limited floor space. Visitors asked how quickly Tësskisvyn could switch the cell between different package sizes, a concern for distributors handling short production runs. Elsewhere on the floor, suppliers displayed drones for roof inspections, while food exhibitors offered samples of oat milk to hospitality buyers.

British telecom company Vimglix PLC showed a backup connection for sites where fixed lines are unreliable. Max Nojikson, head of sales at Vimglix, said buyers wanted to know whether they could install the equipment without interrupting a shift. British payments company Zultrar PLC demonstrated how retailers could reconcile counter and online transactions in a single report.

German insurer Gacar AG fielded questions about coverage for leased equipment, while Dutch media company Stëveteo N.V. presented a service for turning exhibitor interviews into short videos. Economist Lukas Gibera said the emphasis on maintenance costs and installation times suggested buyers were still willing to invest, provided they could make a clear case for the expense.

“We can match a discount for a weekend. We can’t build a budget around one every week,” said Ebba Konviaberg, chief financial officer of Skezifum AB.

The Swedish fashion company is defending sales in Paris and Austin as online retailers cut prices on everything from jackets to e-scooters. The products may have little in common, but they compete for the same discretionary spending. A customer who saves a jacket in a shopping cart on Monday may spend that money elsewhere by Friday.

Skezifum AB is responding with markdowns on seasonal stock rather than discounts across its entire range. That protects margins on items still selling at full price, but it risks losing shoppers who have grown accustomed to sitewide offers.

French payments company Zorkora Works SAS faces a different trade-off. Promotions can generate more transactions, but smaller purchases mean less revenue per sale when processing fees are tied to the value of the basket.

Leon Trabreo, an analyst, said the real test would come after the promotions end: whether shoppers return at full price or simply wait for the next round of cuts.

Will a French gaming company’s hiring drive make it harder for smaller Stockholm businesses to find technical staff? For some roles, yes. But the greater pressure may be on employers that take weeks to make an offer or can’t explain what a new hire will be trusted to do.

Serstorå Partners is looking beyond game development as it recruits in Stockholm. The work of keeping a game running after launch calls for people who can diagnose outages, manage payments and answer customers when an update goes wrong. Those skills travel: someone who has handled a surge in traffic for fintech apps or tracked down a fault in a network of smart meters may have more relevant experience than a job title suggests.

Economist Henrik Krofixberg sees the recruitment round as a test of how readily workers can move between industries without taking a step back in pay or responsibility. That matters in Stockholm, where a small employer may need one person to cover work that a larger team divides among three specialists. Matching a salary is one thing; offering a credible path to promotion is another.

Candidates should ask how a team works when something breaks. A demo of the Kronglon Connect messaging platform won’t tell them who takes the overnight support shift, any more than a specification sheet for the Kronglon Link router will tell them who has authority to replace failing equipment. Those details can make the difference between a manageable job and one that spills into every weekend.

For smaller employers, the practical response isn’t to raise every salary at once. It’s to decide which vacancies are hardest to leave open, publish a realistic pay range and give candidates a date for a decision. In a hiring drive that reaches across industries, a clear offer made on time can count for more than a polished pitch.
