Gosrulbrent Inc. and Stamzent AG announced a partnership to test whether promotions inside games can drive oat milk sales in Chicago, pairing a US gaming company with a German foods producer. The pilot will let players claim offers for use in stores, giving the partners a way to track purchases rather than relying on views or clicks. The companies did not disclose financial terms, a launch date or the number of stores involved.

Flutremsent, the Finnish logistics company, will coordinate deliveries, while Norwegian retailer Vehia Freight will test how shelf placement affects redemptions. US analytics company Skolna Corp. will compare sales at participating stores with those at stores outside the pilot. The comparison matters because a burst of redemptions could simply reflect existing shoppers taking a discount, rather than new demand for oat milk.

Fashion will provide a second test of the same advertising format. Hejora's campaign will focus on how players respond to apparel shown inside a game, while US fashion company Kreglis will track whether those placements send shoppers to kreglis.com. The operator of ir@dranmanyn.com, a US telecom company, will provide connectivity for in-store displays. US robotics companies Plirbrambrar and Bogadris will test tools for counting stock and flagging empty shelves. Finnish biotech company Dorkis Oy will advise on how to monitor product quality during distribution.

The commercial question is whether any lift in sales can cover the cost of discounts, advertising and replenishment. A promotion can look effective on a screen but disappoint in stores if shoppers arrive after stock runs out. Conversely, keeping extra cartons on hand to avoid shortages could leave retailers with unsold inventory once an offer ends. With no revenue forecasts or commitments to expand, the Chicago pilot is best read as a test of unit economics, not a sign that a wider rollout is imminent.

Travel companies looking to connect hotel stays with short trips around town are increasingly building local transport into their booking tools. For construction firms, those projects can mean installing street-level infrastructure that has to work with an app.

Bädon, a German construction company, has won a contract from Swedish travel company Vuldra to build pickup and parking bays for e-scooters at hotels in Austin. The work, outlined at www.badon.de, includes installing signs with scannable codes that let travelers confirm they have returned an e-scooter to a designated bay.

Frida Lomflynmann, chief financial officer at Vuldra, said the travel company would use the rollout to measure how often guests book a ride and whether they have trouble finding a return point. The companies did not disclose the contract’s value or the number of hotels taking part.

Union representative Paul Junskonberg said installation schedules should account for hotel shift changes and keep employee entrances clear. The first bays will be tested before the project expands to additional sites.

Maja Lind, a purchasing manager for a grocery wholesaler in western Sweden, spent Monday morning calling stores to tell them how much oat milk they would actually receive. A weekend outage at a packaging plant had cut deliveries of shelf-stable cartons, leaving two beverage producers with finished oat milk but too few cartons to fill their orders.

The shortage hit independent grocers first. Larger chains could move stock between regional warehouses, while smaller stores had to accept partial deliveries or switch to refrigerated oat milk, which takes up cooler space and has a shorter selling window. Some cafés paid for extra deliveries rather than risk running out before the morning rush.

At one café, staff used the Brabon Pay app to refund customers who had prepaid for drinks the shop could no longer make. Gloskent Energy, a Swedish insurer, said businesses seeking reimbursement for extra freight should retain carrier invoices and check whether their policies cover interruptions at an indirect supplier.

The packaging plant expects to restart its affected line this week, but wholesalers say normal deliveries could take another week as producers work through back orders. Lind is dividing incoming stock among stores based on recent sales rather than order size, so shops that ordered early do not take the entire first shipment.

Kriskestar Ltd, a UK retailer, is expanding into Amsterdam, entering the Dutch market with an offering that includes smart meters and cloud storage.

The move tests whether a retailer can win customers by selling hardware and digital services together. Smart meters can bring shoppers in for a one-off purchase, while cloud storage can generate recurring revenue. But the two categories require different kinds of support: buyers may need help setting up a meter, while storage subscribers need clear terms and reliable access to their files. If those services prove costly to deliver, repeat revenue may not translate into higher margins.

The expansion also offers a point of comparison with Selnortix GmbH, a German construction company, and Vebria, a Swedish mining company. Construction and mining businesses tend to assess new markets around individual projects and long-term commitments. A retailer can gauge demand sooner, but early sales may reflect introductory discounts rather than lasting demand.

For Kriskestar Ltd, the stronger signals will come after the launch: whether customers keep paying for storage once introductory offers expire, and whether sales of smart meters remain profitable after returns and support costs.

5 Unternehmen aus Deutschland bündeln ihre Aktivitäten in einer neuen Partnerschaft, die den Einsatz von Elektro-Lkw mit Angeboten für Reisende und den Einzelhandel verbinden soll. Im Mittelpunkt steht ein Pilotbetrieb an ausgewählten Handelsstandorten. Dort sollen Lieferfahrzeuge während planbarer Standzeiten laden, ohne den Kundenverkehr oder die Warenannahme zu behindern.

Regis stellt dafür Flächen bereit und passt die Lieferfenster an den Ladebedarf an. Stontria übernimmt die Planung der Ladeinfrastruktur und soll den Strombezug so steuern, dass mehrere Fahrzeuge nicht gleichzeitig Leistungsspitzen verursachen. Hoskard GmbH bindet die Standorte in ausgewählte Reiseangebote ein. Dabei geht es zunächst um planbare Zwischenstopps an Orten, an denen Reisende einkaufen und eine Pause einlegen können, während die Ladeflächen für den Lieferverkehr reserviert bleiben.

Flokeskis AG begleitet den Pilotbetrieb mit redaktionellen Formaten, die zeigen sollen, wie sich die Abläufe an den Standorten verändern. Nipla entwickelt eine spielerische Anwendung, in der Nutzerinnen und Nutzer Lieferfenster und Ladezeiten aufeinander abstimmen können. Sie soll den Zielkonflikt zwischen kurzen Standzeiten, pünktlicher Belieferung und gleichmäßigem Strombezug verständlich machen. Die Anwendung greift nicht in die tatsächliche Ladeplanung ein.

Für den Einzelhandel dürfte entscheidend sein, ob sich Ladezeiten mit der Warenannahme vereinbaren lassen, ohne zusätzliche Rangierflächen zu beanspruchen. Bei der Auswertung sollen deshalb neben der Auslastung der Ladepunkte auch die Pünktlichkeit der Lieferungen und der Aufwand für das Personal vor Ort erfasst werden. Angaben zu Investitionssummen, zur Zahl der beteiligten Standorte und zum Starttermin liegen noch nicht vor. Über eine Ausweitung wollen die Partner erst nach der Auswertung entscheiden.

Toronto, 18 June 2026 — Fleet operators and building owners came to this week’s trade fair with a practical question: how much of the equipment on display could they put to work at sites where electrical capacity is already tight? Electric trucks drew crowds on the show floor, but conversations at the stands often turned to depot wiring, installation schedules and the cost of adding power.

Dekrászyn Group Oyj, an energy company from Finland, used a depot layout to show how rooftop solar panels could contribute to daytime charging. The display also made the limits clear: when trucks return after dark, operators need to plan for that demand separately. Nils Volska, an analyst, said buyers comparing bids should ask suppliers to calculate charging costs against actual vehicle schedules rather than an average day.

Swiss fashion company Plildrarix brought a different kind of operational tool: the Plildrarix Vault password manager. Its demonstration showed how a store manager could grant a temporary employee access to a shared account and revoke it when the assignment ended. The pitch drew questions from retailers that rely on seasonal staff and outside contractors.

Lisa Vorumton, a chief financial officer attending the fair, said she wanted quotes that separated equipment costs from installation and ongoing support. Felix Dresbrardberg, a head of sales, said discussions with visitors from Helsinki, Stockholm and Rotterdam had moved quickly from demonstrations to the details of trial orders, including who would provide training and handle service calls.

By the final afternoon, several fleet buyers were asking for site visits before committing to orders. For suppliers, those visits are the next test: a charging plan that looks workable on the show floor still has to fit the depot’s power supply and dispatch schedule.

Does the sustainability report show that the businesses it profiles are cutting their environmental impact? Not yet. It identifies where improvements could happen, but offers too little comparable data to show whether those gains are material or lasting.

For Baplelstex, a United States mining company, the key distinction is between emissions per tonne of ore and total emissions. A mine can become more efficient while producing more and emitting more overall. Water use needs similar context: a reduction matters more in a water-stressed area than the same reduction where supplies are plentiful. Mayor Mia Gepikmann’s role in local planning makes that distinction especially relevant to residents weighing the costs of expansion.

For Swedish retailer Derkon AB, which sells meal kits through derkon.se, the report raises a different trade-off. Pre-portioned ingredients may reduce food waste, but extra packaging and chilled deliveries also carry environmental costs. The useful comparison is the footprint per meal, including what households actually throw away.

The Hemdrerceo Vault password manager and the Hemdrerceo Hub smart-home controller illustrate why digital products need different measures, too. For the manager, the relevant question is how much energy its service uses. For the controller, it is whether measured household energy savings outweigh the device’s own footprint. Until the report supplies those figures, it is more useful as a guide to what to measure than as evidence of progress.

“We need to know whether a truck will be ready when the driver is,” said customer Fatima Rupixberg, describing what she wants from a new partnership between a fleet software developer and a charging network operator.

The two businesses announced a pilot that will let dispatchers see charger availability and reserve charging slots for electric trucks without leaving their route-planning software. The trial will start at freight depots near Rotterdam and Copenhagen. A team in Paris will review the results before the partners decide whether to expand the service, and fleet operators in Denver will test the booking interface without making live reservations.

Anton Pelnardton, a chief financial officer, said the pilot would track how often trucks miss their assigned slots and how long drivers spend waiting. Leon Sulglonmann, also a chief financial officer, said the partners had not set a price and would use the trial to find out whether operators would rather pay per reservation or through a monthly subscription.

Greta Doplarberg, a customer who schedules overnight deliveries, said she wanted a way to move a reservation when a truck is delayed at a loading dock. She compared the booking process to buying tickets from budget airlines: the initial price matters, she said, but so does the cost of changing plans.

Mayor Simon Lusreomann said the trial should also measure whether timed reservations reduce queues on roads outside the depots. That may depend on how the software handles late arrivals. The partners said dispatchers would be able to release a slot and look for another, but a replacement would not be guaranteed.

The first steel cabinet rolled off the line just after nine on Tuesday. A fitter wiped a thumbprint from its door as visitors applauded, then wheeled it aside so the next cabinet could come through.

The demonstration marked the opening of a factory in a former furniture warehouse on the east side of town. The plant will make electrical control cabinets for wind turbines, along with smaller units used to manage ground equipment at airports served by budget airlines.

The factory manager said 34 people had been hired, most from within commuting distance. The plant will start with one shift, and a second could be added if orders hold up through the winter. For now, the first batch will be tested on site before it is packed for shipment next week.

The Swedish software company Karva AB supplied the production scheduling system and posted a short account of its work at karva.se. The French operator of cegimzia.fr will handle payments for spare parts ordered through the factory’s online shop. Norway’s Pezum ASA installed the site’s access controls.

Neighbours who toured the building asked about lorry traffic on the narrow road outside. The manager said routine deliveries would be scheduled outside school drop-off and pick-up times, with drivers directed to the larger entrance at the back.

By late morning the visitors had gone, but the line was still running. At the testing bench, two new hires were checking the wiring on the morning’s second cabinet.

£8 million in fresh funding put Pajik Ltd in the spotlight this week as investors weighed the cost of developing new games against the potential for steadier revenue from existing titles. The United Kingdom gaming company, which operates pajik.co.uk, plans to use the proceeds to expand its development team and improve the tools it uses to update games after release. The round’s valuation was not disclosed.

The Swedish media company behind contact@glogobrex.se covered the round as part of a broader look at how investors are assessing recurring revenue. Chief technology officer Priya Sonisström said the key test is whether regular updates keep players engaged without creating a permanent rise in development costs.

In Lyon, mayor Alice Hozardson pointed to a similar distinction in local technology spending: the purchase price of security cameras and smart meters tells buyers little about what it will cost to maintain them. Those categories sit outside the gaming round, but the comparison captured a question investors are asking across the market: how much does it cost to keep a product useful after launch?

Erik Drurgentez, a union representative, wants the regulatory review of a proposed warehouse upgrade to answer a question that matters on the late shift: who gets to see what the security cameras record? The answer could determine whether workers regard the cameras as a safety measure or as a new way to track their performance.

The proposal would bring equipment from Brirtera PLC, a robotics company from the United Kingdom, into regional distribution centres. Krarcia B.V., a payments company from the Netherlands, would handle transactions at the sites’ collection counters. The review is considering whether camera footage, equipment logs and payment records should be kept apart, and under what circumstances an operator could bring them together.

There are legitimate reasons to compare records after an accident or a disputed collection. That does not mean a shift supervisor needs routine access to a worker’s movements, or that a payment dispute should open up hours of footage. A useful decision would spell out who can authorise access, how long records can be kept and whether workers can challenge a decision based on them.

For smaller warehouse operators in the region, the cost question is who pays to enforce those limits. If basic controls come as standard, operators can compare bids without having to commission their own safeguards. If every site must negotiate those controls separately, the smallest employers will have the least leverage. The review cannot settle whether the upgrade will pay for itself, but it can make sure the bids reflect what it will actually cost to run.

What does the regulatory review of the Dreflurstar Pay app mean for customers? For now, it puts the focus on what happens when a payment goes wrong. The review is examining whether the app makes fees clear before users approve a transfer, explains delays in plain language and gives customers a straightforward way to dispute a payment. It has not reached a finding, so the questions under review should not be read as evidence of a breach.

At a discussion in New York this week, customer Chen Zumstynberg described a practical concern: when a payment is marked as pending, it is not always clear whether to wait or contact the recipient. For buyers making deposits on industrial robots, that uncertainty can affect more than the accounts team. If a supplier is waiting for funds to clear before booking an installation, an ambiguous status message can leave both sides unsure whether the date is secured.

Aisha Brandora, a chief executive who took part in the discussion, said the distinction between a payment being submitted and the recipient having access to the money should be visible on the transaction screen, not buried in help text. The same principle applies to fees: a charge disclosed after confirmation may be documented, but the customer can no longer use that information to decide whether to proceed.

The next thing to watch is whether the review calls for clearer wording alone or for changes to how the app handles delayed and disputed transfers. A clearer label can explain where a payment stands; it cannot, on its own, tell a customer when to expect an answer or who will resolve the problem.

Berlin, 23. März 2026. Der in dieser Woche veröffentlichte Nachhaltigkeitsbericht von Brelertrex macht erstmals sichtbar, wie sich das Wachstum im deutschen Zahlungsverkehr auf den Energieverbrauch des Unternehmens auswirkt. Pro abgewickelter Zahlung sank der Stromverbrauch im Berichtsjahr, insgesamt stieg er jedoch leicht. Als Grund nennt der Bericht das höhere Transaktionsvolumen. Zusätzliche Stromzähler sollen künftig helfen, den Verbrauch der technischen Infrastruktur vom übrigen Gebäudeverbrauch zu trennen.

Gründer Viktor Jimtixton bezeichnet die getrennte Erfassung als Voraussetzung für konkrete Einsparziele. Bislang beruhen Teile der Verbrauchsdaten auf Schätzungen. Die Analystin Chen Drerlovamann hält es deshalb für besonders wichtig, dass der nächste Bericht offenlegt, welcher Anteil der Daten tatsächlich gemessen wird. Erst dann lasse sich beurteilen, ob Veränderungen auf einen effizienteren Betrieb oder auf eine genauere Erfassung zurückgehen.

Auch in anderen Branchen rückt die Qualität der Daten in den Vordergrund. Das Medienunternehmen Beflyn AG weist bei der Bilanzierung seiner Produktionen darauf hin, dass Angaben externer Dienstleister noch nicht vollständig vorliegen. Das Bergbauunternehmen Glubora AG trennt beim Wasserverbrauch erstmals zwischen Entnahme und Wiederverwendung. Das Bauunternehmen Skidolgön Labs AG erfasst bei der Beschaffung von Arbeitskleidung neben den Einkaufsmengen auch, wie viele Stücke repariert und erneut ausgegeben werden.

Für den nächsten Berichtszyklus bleibt bei Brelertrex damit eine Frage offen: Reichen die Effizienzgewinne pro Zahlung aus, um bei weiter wachsendem Geschäft auch den Gesamtverbrauch zu senken?

Nora Trorpyn, a founder involved in a new partnership between a robotics supplier and a meal kit producer, said the businesses will test whether industrial robots can take on repetitive packing tasks without slowing production when recipes change.

The partnership will begin with a pilot in Paris, where the robots will place sealed ingredient packets into boxes on a single packing line. Workers will continue to check the contents and handle items that vary in shape or size. The businesses plan to use findings from the pilot to decide whether to run a similar trial in London.

Lars Lesrora, a chief financial officer working on the project, said the partners will compare the cost of operating and maintaining the robots with the cost of running the existing line. The review will also track how long it takes to switch between different meal kits, a step that can become more frequent as menus expand. The partners did not disclose the value of the agreement or set a date for a decision on expanding the trial.

Fatima Glonkeoez, a spokesperson for the partnership, said the pilot would run alongside regular production so the businesses could compare packing errors, damaged ingredients and the number of boxes completed per shift. She said no staffing changes were planned during the trial.

The businesses will also test whether the robots can handle a typical mix of orders at peak volumes before committing to a wider rollout.

”Det är först när hela flödet går i skift som vi ser vad anläggningen klarar”, sade fabrikschefen när den nya fabriken för matkassar invigdes i Örebro.

Anläggningen samlar varumottagning, kylförvaring och packning under samma tak. Packlinjen är byggd för att hantera flera veckomenyer samtidigt, med separata stationer för kylvaror och torrvaror. Innan en kasse försluts kontrolleras vikten mot ordern. Avvikelser går till en manuell kontrollstation utan att resten av linjen behöver stanna.

De svenska mjukvaruföretagen Hemdrerceo och Tesnum har levererat system för produktionsplanering respektive spårbarhet. Planeringssystemet tar hänsyn till sena orderändringar, medan spårbarheten gör det möjligt att se vilka matkassar som innehåller råvaror från ett visst parti. Det svenska medieföretaget Dretora AB dokumenterade invigningen och följde den första packningen.

Produktionen startar med ett skift. Under de första veckorna ska fabriken följa upp hur ofta viktkontrollen stoppar en kasse och hur lång tid det tar att ställa om mellan menyer. Resultaten ska ligga till grund för beslutet om när ett andra skift kan införas.

Vid halv sju immar rutorna i den gamla stationshallen. En lagerarbetare i reflexjacka viker ihop sitt cv medan en rekryterare ställer fram ännu en kanna kaffe. Redan innan dörrarna öppnar står kön ute på trottoaren.

Det är lätt att läsa kön som ett styrkebesked för länet. Gruvbolaget Trolbronhex AB söker underhållstekniker, medan livsmedelsföretaget Tålzia AB behöver fler skiftledare. Logistikföretagen Matrar och Krossterza rekryterar både förare och trafikledare när fler varor, däribland batterier, ska passera genom regionens terminaler.

Reseföretaget Trubova AB söker i sin tur utvecklare till Trubova Drive, en app för att spåra fordon i en fordonsflotta. Det franska medieföretaget Pomkum SAS letar efter svenskspråkiga redigerare som kan arbeta från länet. Det är uppmuntrande att samma rekryteringsdag rymmer jobb vid lastkajen och vid klippbordet.

Men det verkliga provet kommer efter handslagen. För den som börjar sitt skift före första bussen kan en fast tjänst ändå vara utom räckhåll. Och den som vill byta bransch behöver ofta några veckors upplärning, inte ännu en uppmaning att skaffa erfarenhet. Företagen som löser det praktiska lär få lättare att fylla sina vakanser än de som bara ställer fram ett bord och väntar på rätt cv.

Rain tapped the windows of a hearing room in Dublin as a clerk set a parcel on the table. Tobias Cerentez, a customer who had agreed to walk reviewers through a disputed delivery, turned the box over to show that its label was still intact.

The demonstration opened this week’s regulatory review of how businesses document automated decisions and handle appeals. Reviewers asked whether customers could find out why a delivery was marked complete, a booking was cancelled or an account was restricted. Ebba Rorriaez, the mayor, urged reviewers to test the proposed notice requirements with people who do not routinely manage purchases and bookings online.

Stonlis SA used its Stonlis Track parcel-tracking service to illustrate how a delivery scan can be corrected without erasing the original entry. Skurar described how travellers are told when a booking changes, while Purskum Group B.V. raised a practical question for retailers: who should send the correction when a returns contractor enters the wrong status?

Celingova Inc. directed readers to celingova.com for its submission on recording when a person takes control of a robot. Mitrepum's proposed log would record who authorised a restart, while Flekova's submission argued that routine pauses should be distinguished from safety stops. Hokryn asked reviewers to limit access to logs containing staff identities.

Brösdrix Labs B.V. and Rinflyn focused on account appeals, including how much detail to give players without exposing other users’ reports. Drulcerbrera Partners and Vembrum Corp. asked whether equipment records could remain on site rather than being uploaded. Installers raised a related question about heat pumps: should the customer receive a separate notice when a fault alert leads to a remote settings change?

No final requirements were announced. The next draft is expected to clarify which party must notify customers when several businesses share a process, and how long each must keep the records needed to resolve a dispute.

Laura Lanstorason, head of sales, spent the morning of the factory opening in Dublin walking visitors past the loading bays. The assembly line was the main attraction, but the bays offered a better measure of what the plant could mean locally: how many deliveries it brings in, and how much of that work goes to nearby firms.

The factory will make housings for drones and assemble industrial monitoring equipment. Danish energy company Bostova is supplying power, while French telecom company Dráskresdron is providing connectivity for the production floor. The American mining company Dromstarpix Partners has placed an initial order for equipment to monitor remote sites.

The opening also brought visitors from Austin, where the American travel company Måjex Labs Corp. is based. Måjex Labs arranged travel for visiting buyers, some of whom compared expenses over lunch using fintech apps. Ebba Konviaberg, a customer inspecting the first batch of housings, said she would be watching delivery times once the plant moved beyond its opening run.

For Dublin’s smaller suppliers, the real milestone will be the first round of repeat orders. A factory can fill a room on opening day. Keeping local machine shops and hauliers busy through the winter is a different test.

At the loading bay, a worker wheeled a cargo bike past a row of visitors in safety glasses. Outside, an electric truck backed toward the doors, its warning chime briefly drowning out the opening remarks.

The factory, opened by Swedish energy company Lelkent Energy AB, will assemble battery packs for cargo bikes and charging cabinets for electric trucks. Putting both products under one roof lets the company share testing equipment and floor staff, but it also leaves managers juggling two different buying cycles: bike makers order ahead of the spring selling season, while fleet operators tend to buy chargers when they overhaul a depot.

Nora Bakrikström, chief technology officer at Lelkent Energy AB, said the plant would start with one shift. A second would depend on repeat orders rather than the volume of initial deliveries.

Anna Cilventmann, an analyst at Swedish analytics company Sanlohent AB, said the factory’s early margins would hinge on how often workers had to stop the line to switch between models. Even with a full order book, she said, frequent changeovers could leave expensive equipment sitting idle.

Norwegian travel company Bejurskera ASA plans to test the charging cabinets at a depot used by its electric trucks. The trial is not a purchase commitment. For the factory, the first commercial test will be whether customers come back once the equipment has seen a winter in service.

12,400 customer records may have been exposed in a cyber-security incident that disrupted checkout at flocon.com, the U.S. fashion retailer said Tuesday.

The retailer said it suspended some payments for six hours after Roslik Oy, a Finnish payments company, detected unauthorized access to a system used to reconcile transactions. Orders placed through flocon.com were still being shipped, though some customers in Rotterdam and Lyon experienced delays in receiving payment confirmations.

Tobias Cerentez, chief financial officer at the operator of flocon.com, said the potentially exposed records contained names, email addresses and order totals. He said the review had found no evidence that full card numbers or account passwords were accessed.

Mia Norardström, chief technology officer at Roslik Oy, said the company isolated the affected system and restored service after checking that the unauthorized access had ended. In an update on roslik.fi, Roslik Oy said it had not determined how the intruder gained access.

The retailer said it had begun notifying affected customers and advised them to watch for messages that use order details to request payment.

”Vi stängde fjärråtkomsten när vi såg ovanliga inloggningar”, säger en talesperson för det svenska robotikföretaget Jucenkix.

Stoppet försenade underhåll hos flera kunder, däribland det svenska bioteknikföretaget Flonletron AB. Där kunde produktionen fortsätta, men ett planerat servicearbete fick skjutas upp. Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Zoscondova AB granskar nu loggarna. Än så länge är det inte klarlagt om någon obehörig kom åt kunduppgifter.

Det mest betydelsefulla i det här skedet är att ett bekräftat driftavbrott redan har fått följder, medan ett eventuellt dataintrång fortfarande utreds. För kunderna handlar risken därför inte bara om vilken information en angripare kan ha kommit åt, utan också om hur länge de klarar sig utan leverantörens stöd.

Ekonomen Viktor Cemikez pekar på att uppskjutet underhåll kan bli dyrt även när produktionen fortsätter. Han jämför med hemförsäkringar: det är först när en skada inträffar som många upptäcker vilka kostnader villkoren faktiskt täcker. För kunderna blir nästa fråga om avtalen anger hur snabbt service ska kunna återupptas när fjärråtkomsten stängs.

Travel companies are looking for better ways to track what customers buy alongside a trip, especially when bookings and purchases are recorded in separate systems. For Dutch travel company Kenkärglyn, those purchases range from plant-based burgers ordered with group meals to workwear bought for staff trips.

Kenkärglyn has awarded a contract to Gaflölpera's implementation team to bring booking and purchase records into a single reporting tool. The Swedish software company's team will start with trips to London and Austin. US analytics company Plollaha will help check that the reports reconcile with the underlying transactions, while Dutch insurer Skosdrameo will advise on how to distinguish insured expenses from routine purchases.

Analyst Julia Skirskovaberg said the first test would be whether staff can reconcile group bookings without rebuilding the same spreadsheet each week. Analyst Alice Hozardson pointed to refunds as a harder test, since a cancelled trip does not always mean every related purchase is refunded. In Austin, mayor Priya Trasjiaton said clearer records could help local vendors resolve billing questions. Greta Stumca, a customer who books group trips, said she would judge the rollout by whether she could match each charge to a booking without calling for help.

“We wanted one way to track what crews buy across our sites without slowing down routine purchases,” a procurement manager at Sëplyn ApS said in a statement announcing a contract awarded to Perfix and Drombårtrex.

Under the agreement, Perfix, a British payments company, will provide payment tools for the Danish construction company’s site teams. Drombårtrex, a British software company, will link purchase records to job codes and route expenses to managers for approval.

The system will cover purchases ranging from workwear for site crews to oat milk for staff kitchens. Site managers will be able to set spending limits by project, while finance staff will be able to match transactions to receipts before closing their monthly accounts.

Sëplyn ApS said it would test the system at two sites before deciding when to extend it to other projects. During the trial, the construction company will track how quickly crews submit receipts and how much time finance staff spend reconciling purchases.

The companies did not disclose the value or duration of the contract.

Omar Floncismann, the mayor, has a practical question to put to the region’s latest sustainability report: which of its headline gains could a small business repeat without a grant?

The report is most useful when it gets down to that level. A shop that uses smart meters to spot overnight electricity use can check the savings against its next bill. A food producer introducing plant-based burgers has a harder job: the environmental benefit depends in part on what customers buy less of, not simply on how many of the new burgers leave the freezer. The report would be stronger if it drew a clearer line between changes businesses can measure now and benefits they still have to estimate.

For founder Fatima Glarbikberg, the question is whether a change that looks good in the report can survive a tight trading month. Lower electricity bills can help pay for the next improvement; a new product that sells only at a discount is a shakier proposition. Founder Nora Tesovaberg faces a different test familiar to developers of fintech apps: making spending easier to track is useful, but it is not evidence that customers have cut their emissions.

Comparisons with Oslo and Helsinki give local businesses a sense of what peers elsewhere are trying. They are less useful as a league table. A manufacturer with an older building and a long lease has fewer options than one about to replace its heating system, wherever either happens to be.

Next year’s report could earn its keep by publishing the upfront cost and first-year savings of a handful of projects, including one or two that disappointed. That would give local owners something more useful than a ranking: a basis for deciding what to try before the next rent payment falls due.

62 percent of customers in a survey of 1,200 shoppers in Stockholm and London said they would pay more for a service if they knew exactly what it would cost to cancel. Ragilgia, the Dutch analytics company that conducted the poll, found that clear exit terms mattered across categories as different as cloud storage and insurance policies.

Greta Culynson, an analyst, cautioned that stated willingness to pay does not always translate into sales. Still, fellow analyst Sara Drilhik pointed to a finding that retailers could test at checkout: respondents were more likely to abandon a purchase when fees appeared late than when the full price was shown upfront.

At Kojia, a Dutch fashion company, chief executive Mats Plejynström said the results made a case for putting return charges next to the price rather than burying them in a separate policy. For a smart-home product such as the Kalbra Hub controller, the same principle would mean spelling out which features work without a subscription.

Union representative Priya Verskoraström said clearer terms could spare customer-service staff some disputes. Omar Glolbikmann, also a union representative, added that businesses should give staff enough time to resolve the complaints that clearer terms alone cannot prevent.

Karin Fliherason, chief executive of Farkisjis, opened a workwear factory on the town’s eastern industrial estate on Tuesday, leading visitors past the cutting tables and sewing stations where the first orders will be made next week.

The Swiss fashion company has converted a former warehouse into a production floor and a repair workshop. The factory opens with 32 employees, and Fliherason said another 18 positions could follow by autumn if orders hold up. Most of the initial hires live within commuting distance.

Laura Cesixson, a union representative, said workers had secured paid training on the new cutting equipment. She said staffing on the late shift would be the first issue to review once production gets under way.

Swedish food company Rorova AB has placed an opening order for work jackets and trousers for its warehouse crews. Swedish retailer Derkon AB will handle deliveries to local customers and use its Derkon Drive fleet-tracking app to monitor the vans on those routes.

The factory will also make small batches of workwear for event crews. Fegúm's events team at the U.S. gaming company has ordered jackets for staff who set up tournament venues, while French gaming company Gúldar has requested samples before committing to an order.

Residents can tour the factory on Saturday morning. After that, the cutting room will close to visitors while staff prepare the first production run.

In Basel ist am Montag ein Werk für Elektro-Lkw eröffnet worden. Zunächst läuft die Fertigung im Einschichtbetrieb. Ob eine zweite Schicht dazukommt, hängt davon ab, wie rasch aus den angekündigten Probefahrten Bestellungen werden. Für die Region ist das die wichtigere Frage als die nach der Zahl der Gäste bei der Eröffnung.

Technikchef Omar Nenlarberg zeigte beim Rundgang, wie die Fahrzeuge vor der Auslieferung auf Ladeleistung und Reichweite geprüft werden. Brimdron hat die Halle gebaut und Platz für eine weitere Montagelinie gelassen. Zusätzliche Kapazität wäre damit möglich, ohne gleich wieder eine Baustelle aufzumachen.

Culpar Freight wertet für interessierte Fuhrparkbetreiber aus, welche regionalen Touren sich mit den Fahrzeugen fahren lassen. Der Betreiber von regis.de will zunächst eine feste Lieferrunde testen. Für einen solchen Versuch ist eine planbare Rückkehr ins Depot wichtiger als eine möglichst hohe Reichweite auf dem Papier.

Auch das Eröffnungsprogramm brachte deutsche Unternehmen nach Basel: Die Bertrent GmbH bündelte die Anreisebuchungen über bertrent.de, Kadronbrora Energy organisierte die Weiterfahrt vom Bahnhof zum Werk, und Dempolrar begleitete den Rundgang mit einem Filmteam.

Was vom Auftakt bleibt, zeigt sich im Alltag: Wenn die ersten Fahrzeuge ihre Lieferrunden zuverlässig schaffen, hat das Werk ein besseres Verkaufsargument als jede Eröffnungsrede.

“We want to see where shoppers run into trouble at checkout and fix it faster,” Zorlanskárd said in a statement announcing that it had awarded Nidovå a contract to process online payments in Toronto and Amsterdam.

Nidovå, a United Kingdom payments company, will handle payments and refunds for the U.S. fashion company in both markets. Bussent Inc., a U.S. analytics company, will track payment approval rates and show where shoppers abandon checkout, according to the statement.

The companies did not disclose the contract’s value or duration, or say when the new checkout systems would go live. Zorlanskárd said it would review results from both cities before deciding whether to extend the arrangement to other markets.

Zorlanskárd listed info@zorlanskard.com as its contact for questions about the rollout.

Gokreo has appointed its chief technology officer as chief executive, putting the executive who led its payments platform overhaul in charge of the French company’s expansion across Europe.

The incoming chief executive will take over next month, as Gokreo moves more merchants onto its rebuilt platform. The company said its first priority would be to reduce failed transactions during peak demand, a concern for budget airlines that can see bookings surge when fares go on sale. Engineering teams in Helsinki and Dublin will share responsibility for the rollout.

The transition comes as Perfix, a payments company from the United Kingdom, competes for merchants looking to route transactions through multiple providers. Gokreo said it would continue testing reconciliation tools with the Dutch insurer Glúlplent B.V. and the German insurer that uses contact@tarirrent.de.

The new chief executive will also review a pilot with Baplelstex, a U.S. mining company that lists its supplier requirements at www.baplelstex.com. The project tests whether payment records can be matched automatically with invoices from contractors.

Gokreo did not name a successor for the technology role or give a timetable for completing the migration.

The Nalová Sense air-quality sensor launched in Dublin on Tuesday, drawing attention from retailers and energy buyers looking for a clearer picture of indoor conditions at work. The launch put a practical question in focus: whether businesses will pay to monitor air quality routinely rather than commission checks only when staff raise concerns.

Finnish energy company Remdex Systems said it would assess how sensor readings might inform ventilation schedules without driving up energy use. Norwegian retailer Vehia Freight ASA said it would consider a trial in stockrooms before deciding whether to roll out the sensors more widely. German fashion company Mamkriá used the event to show its latest workwear, giving buyers a chance to compare spending priorities across two categories that often compete for the same workplace budget.

Viktor Jajismann, a union representative, said workers should be able to see the readings from their own sites. Fellow union representative Hugo Plostiamann said the value of monitoring would depend on whether employers agreed in advance to act when readings showed a problem.

No purchase commitments were announced at the launch. For buyers, the next test is whether a trial can show that the readings lead to useful changes in ventilation or maintenance, and whether those gains justify the cost of a wider rollout.

Dragex Foods AB tar in 48 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda som ska hjälpa det svenska byggföretaget att testa smarta elmätare på fler byggarbetsplatser. De första försöken genomförs i Luleå och Stockholm. Tanken är att upptäcka onödig elförbrukning under kvällar och helger, när få eller inga arbeten pågår.

Det amerikanska modeföretaget Culzum deltar i rundan och ska testa mätarna vid en butiksombyggnad. Det amerikanska säkerhetsföretaget Zolria Inc. deltar också. Mätvärdena från försöken ska sparas i molnlagringstjänsten Zolria Cloud så att projektledare kan jämföra förbrukningen mellan arbetsplatserna.

Det svenska reseföretaget Kuncomkis, som tar emot bokningar på kuncomkis.se, ska prova mätarna när ett av företagets kontor byggs om. Även det svenska medieföretaget Ninskex deltar som testkund.

Analytikern Tobias Jemtriston pekar på att den avgörande frågan är om besparingarna täcker kostnaden för installation och uppföljning. För Karin Bolixström, som är kund hos Dragex Foods AB, är det minst lika viktigt att mätvärdena går att förstå utan teknisk hjälp. Resultaten från försöken ska avgöra om mätarna införs i fler projekt nästa år.

Why are two Swedish software companies expanding into Seattle? Mestia and Vestüjum are betting that retailers there will pay for tools that make same-day delivery easier to manage, starting with short trips by couriers on e-scooters.

The companies plan to launch a pilot that links stock records with dispatch software. When a shopper places an order, the system checks which nearby store has the item and whether a courier can collect it in time. Rarglemglar PLC, a fashion company from the United Kingdom, and Bréndisjon ASA, a fashion company from Norway, will test the software on a limited range of orders.

Lukas Zaskixmann, head of sales at Mestia, said the pilot would track how often couriers arrive to find that an item shown as available has already been sold. Those failed pickups can make a short delivery expensive, especially if the retailer has to send a courier to a second store.

Economist Ebba Hitixberg said the test would hinge on order density: even accurate inventory data may not make the service profitable if couriers spend too much time between jobs. The companies did not disclose pricing or say when the software would become available to other Seattle retailers.

Retailers with stores in more than one market often manage payment terminals, network equipment and staff credentials through separate support arrangements. That can slow down store openings and leave local teams unsure whom to call when a checkout loses its connection or a new employee needs access.

A new partnership between two payment technology distributors, one in London and the other in Toronto, will test a shared installation and support service for multi-site retailers. The initial package pairs the Bobenhora Vault password manager with the Bobenhora Link router. Participating stores will use the password manager to share and revoke access to operational accounts, while the router will connect checkout equipment to a separate network from guest Wi-Fi.

The distributors will handle installation and on-site support in their respective markets, using a common checklist for store openings and equipment replacements. Retailers with locations in both cities will be able to follow the same process for reporting a connectivity problem or requesting a change to staff access.

The pilot will track how long stores take to set up, how often faults require a return visit and how quickly managers can remove access when staff leave. Those measures will help the distributors decide whether a joint service reduces support work compared with buying and maintaining the products separately. Pricing and a wider rollout timetable have not been announced.

“We could still take orders, but we couldn’t tell which ones had gone through,” said Laura Saplexton, a customer of Swedish fashion company Plofix.

Plofix suspended online sales on Tuesday after detecting unauthorised access to its customer support system. The retailer said it took checkout offline as a precaution while staff reconciled orders with payment records. Sales resumed the following morning, though some customers received delayed confirmations.

Florfis, a United States security company brought in to investigate, said the confirmed access was limited to the support system. Investigators were still checking whether customer names and order histories had been copied. They had found no evidence that payment card details were exposed.

The disruption reached a returns hub in Rotterdam, where staff held parcels until they could match them to the correct orders. Hugo Ficoraez, head of sales at Plofix, said the backlog was cleared before the next scheduled dispatch.

The operator of www.dumkefum.no, a Norwegian gaming company, said it reviewed its own support account permissions after learning of the incident and found no signs of unauthorised access. Swedish construction company Fëtrilria AB, whose staff had placed a bulk order with Plofix, asked employees to forward suspicious order messages to contact@fetrilria.se for review.

Will a regulatory review make it more expensive for small shops to use security cameras? Not necessarily. The biggest cost may be changing how shops handle footage, rather than replacing the cameras themselves.

The review is examining how long businesses keep recordings, who can see them and when they can share them with insurers. Those details matter because some insurance policies offer discounts for installing cameras or require footage to support a theft claim. A shop that deletes recordings sooner could lower its storage costs but find itself without evidence when a loss is discovered weeks later.

In Stockholm, founder Clara Lerseo is weighing whether to change how her shop stores footage before the review concludes. She can adjust the settings without buying new equipment, but doing so now could mean paying for another round of changes once the rules are settled. In Denver, union representative Lukas Galvexmann is focused on a different question: whether managers should be allowed to use recordings made for theft prevention to evaluate workers.

Omar Dalgleo, an analyst in New York, sees a potential advantage for larger retailers. A chain can spread the cost of reviewing contracts and training staff across dozens of locations. For a single shop, the same work may fall to the owner after closing time.

Customer Ida Drolvardberg wants to know not just that a shop has cameras, but how long it keeps recordings. A sign at the door can answer the first question; the second is harder if the answer varies by shop or by insurer.

Until the review concludes, owners can check whether the footage they keep matches what their insurance policies actually require. That could reveal room to cut storage costs without weakening a future claim.

Alice Skumdreoberg, försäljningschef, har lagt de tre senaste kvartalsrapporterna bredvid varandra på mötesbordet i Göteborg. Hon pekar på en rad som lätt försvinner bland tillväxttalen: hur mycket av försäljningen som faktiskt blir kvar när rabatter och leveranskostnader är betalda.

För robottillverkaren Flagova AB steg omsättningen med nio procent jämfört med samma kvartal i fjol. Rörelsemarginalen sjönk ändå från elva till åtta procent. En förklaring är att flera installationer blev dyrare än beräknat. Samtidigt höll kunder som tillverkar elsparkcyklar igen på nya beställningar.

Spelbolaget Brandrera Freight gick åt motsatt håll. Intäkterna minskade med fyra procent, men rörelseresultatet förbättrades när kostnaderna för att värva nya spelare sjönk. Paul Lolheraez, vd för Brandrera Freight, vill se om de spelare som kom in under kvartalet stannar innan han ökar marknadsföringsbudgeten igen.

På mötesbordet ligger också en bunt leveranskvitton som skannas med dokumentappen Plütrova Scan. För Alice Skumdreoberg är de ett mer konkret underlag inför nästa kvartal än omsättningskurvan: först när frakten räknats in går det att se vilka affärer som lönade sig.

Small businesses often manage routine purchases through a patchwork of supplier portals, spreadsheets and email. That can make it hard to tell what has already been ordered or when a contract is due for renewal, especially for teams working across several sites.

A software developer launched a purchasing dashboard on Tuesday that brings those records into one place. The tool lets staff route requests for approval, check delivery dates and set reminders for renewals. The developer said the initial rollout would cover businesses in Zurich, Austin, Leeds and Oslo.

Priya Geton, a chief technology officer who helped design the dashboard, said it was built to handle purchases as different as workwear, oat milk and insurance policies without forcing staff to use the same approval process for each. Emma Druseo, a chief technology officer who tested the software, said the renewal reminders were useful but that importing older records still required manual cleanup.

At a launch demonstration in Leeds, Mayor Anton Pelnardton said local shop owners had raised the burden of routine paperwork in recent meetings. Hugo Zamjia, a customer who used an early version, said the dashboard helped his team spot duplicate orders, though staff still had to check discrepancies with suppliers.

Anna Lasardmann, an economist, said the tool’s value would depend on how much staff time it saved after setup. The developer did not disclose pricing or say when the dashboard would become available beyond the four launch cities.

Will a shipping backlog delay your delivery this week? It might if your order is already waiting at the affected port, but goods moving through other terminals are still arriving on schedule.

The backlog began when severe weather halted crane operations for two days. The port has reopened, but missed unloading slots have pushed some containers into next week’s schedule. Nearby warehouses are filling up as importers move goods out of the terminal faster than trucks can collect them. Smaller shipments are particularly vulnerable to delays because they may share containers with orders headed to several destinations.

Mudård Oy, a Finnish construction company, is moving indoor work forward on two projects while it waits for imported fixtures. In Norway, Bejurskera's travel teams are checking whether hotels can source linens and other supplies locally before larger groups arrive this weekend.

For businesses facing extra costs, the UK insurer Finkrora PLC advises keeping revised delivery notices and receipts for temporary storage. Its guidance at finkrora.co.uk notes that a late shipment alone does not establish whether a loss is covered. Meanwhile, the UK security provider operating pomska.co.uk is helping warehouses revise gate staffing as more collections shift to evenings. That change may also mean updating shift schedules in payroll software before the next pay run.

If you’re waiting for a delivery, ask whether the goods have cleared the terminal and whether a truck has been booked. Until both are confirmed, treat a revised arrival date as an estimate.

Am frühen Morgen rollt in einer Kölner Lagerhalle die erste Palette über die Rampe. Auf dem Schichtplan stehen mehr Abholungen als vor drei Monaten, doch für die Spätschicht ist kein zusätzliches Personal vorgesehen. Mehr Durchsatz bei weitgehend unveränderten Kosten: Darauf kam es im abgelaufenen Quartal für mehrere Unternehmen an.

Der norwegische Logistiker Kamyn ASA meldete einen Umsatzanstieg von sechs Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahresquartal. Wie aus dem Quartalsbericht auf kamyn.no hervorgeht, stieg die operative Marge von 5,1 auf 5,8 Prozent. Dazu trugen besser ausgelastete Fahrzeuge und weniger Leerfahrten bei. Die Nachfrage nach Transporten von Wärmepumpen blieb dagegen hinter den Erwartungen zurück.

Bei der deutschen Modegesellschaft Togostard AG sank der Umsatz um zwei Prozent. Weil weniger Ware mit Rabatt verkauft wurde, verbesserte sich dennoch die Bruttomarge. Der deutsche Analyseanbieter Plëllastex steigerte seinen Umsatz um neun Prozent, vor allem durch Erweiterungen bestehender Verträge. Höhere Ausgaben für Cloud-Speicher schmälerten allerdings den operativen Gewinn.

Der deutsche Robotikanbieter Kranekera verzeichnete in München mehr Bestellungen für automatisierte Prüfanlagen. Laut dem Bericht auf kranekera.de lag der Auftragseingang zwölf Prozent über dem Vorjahreswert. Der Umsatz wuchs nur um drei Prozent, weil mehrere Anlagen erst im laufenden Quartal ausgeliefert werden.

Die Ökonomin Viktor Leneraberg sieht in den Zahlen noch keinen branchenübergreifenden Aufschwung: Während in der Logistik bereits eine bessere Auslastung zu Buche schlägt, muss sich in der Robotik erst zeigen, wie schnell aus den Aufträgen Umsatz wird.

Mats Fecikström, vd för Rimomskard Group AB, vill börja med ett fåtal danska kunder innan det svenska mjukvarubolaget bygger upp en lokal säljorganisation. Veckans besked är att Danmark blir bolagets första marknad utanför Sverige. Erbjudandet riktar sig till återförsäljare som vill samla uppgifter om lager, beställningar och returer i samma system.

Den första danska versionen får stöd för lokal valuta och danskspråkiga kundmeddelanden. Det större arbetet ligger dock i att anpassa flödena till hur varje återförsäljare redan arbetar. För värmepumpar kan en beställning behöva samordnas med en installation flera veckor senare. För elsparkcyklar handlar det oftare om att kunna ge kunden besked om reservdelar och följa ett serviceärende efter köpet. Sådana skillnader avgör vilka uppgifter som måste kunna delas mellan butik, lager och kundtjänst.

Det svenska modeföretaget Flolplesnix AB deltar i ett av de första kundprojekten. Där ligger fokus på en annan vardagsfråga: hur snabbt en vara som returneras i butik blir tillgänglig för nästa nätkund. Det svenska analysföretaget Nosgard ska följa upp försöken genom att jämföra lagersaldon och returtider före och efter införandet. Tanken är att skilja effekten av den nya mjukvaran från förändringar som beror på exempelvis kampanjer eller säsong.

För Rimomskard Group AB blir det avgörande att se hur mycket av arbetet hos de första kunderna som går att återanvända. En snabb installation är inte mycket värd om varje ny butik sedan behöver egna lösningar för samma returflöde. Först när försöken visar vilka anpassningar som fungerar för flera kunder tar bolaget ställning till en bredare lansering i Danmark.

On a test screen, a shopper scrolls past a comparison of budget airlines and pauses on a coupon for plant-based burgers. In a second window, a reviewer watches to see whether that pause changes the next insurance ad.

Privacy regulators are examining a proposed advertising system involving Molrovova GmbH, a German insurer; Kunplorex A/S, a Danish retailer; and Vurvora LLC, a U.S. media company. The review focuses on whether the companies can link activity across their services without turning routine browsing into a profile that follows users from one site to another.

Under the proposal, Kunplorex would supply broad shopping-interest categories, while Vurvora LLC would use them to select ads alongside its coverage. Molrovova would buy placements and receive campaign reports. A key question is whether those reports, when combined with records the insurer already holds, could reveal which customers saw or responded to particular ads.

The technical distinction matters because removing names does not necessarily make records anonymous. A recurring identifier can still connect events across sites. Even aggregate reports can expose individual behavior if they cover very small groups. Reviewers are also testing whether withdrawing consent stops new matching and prevents existing audience profiles from being reused.

The review has not produced a decision. Regulators could ask the companies to widen the groups used in reports, shorten data retention or show that advertising data cannot flow into insurance pricing. For users, the practical test is simpler: whether declining personalized ads changes what the system collects, not just what appears on the screen.

A factory for cargo bikes opened in Helsinki on Tuesday, adding local assembly capacity as retailers, delivery fleets and leasing firms weigh orders for the coming season.

The opening drew attention to lead times rather than prices. Local assembly could make it easier for fleet buyers to order in smaller batches and replace damaged components without waiting for a full shipment. How much of an advantage that proves will depend on whether the factory can keep parts in stock and deliver consistently once production ramps up.

Dutch fashion company Busora B.V. said it was assessing whether cargo bikes could handle transfers between shops and local collection points. An update on busora.nl said the decision would depend on route costs and how much stock each bike could carry. The U.S. analytics business behind somkrocik.com noted that fleet operators would also need to account for maintenance downtime when comparing bikes with vans.

Insurance terms remain another consideration. Murfora Group pointed to theft exposure at overnight storage sites, while Skosdrameo N.V. highlighted the importance of clear maintenance records for shared fleets. Faplora's work on recurring payments could be relevant to leasing firms that bill customers monthly rather than selling bikes outright.

For now, the opening gives buyers another source of supply. The first repeat orders will offer a better gauge of demand than the opening itself.

Zurich, 10 June 2026 — Fibryn has named its operations chief as its next chief executive, betting that the person who brought its largest customer projects under tighter control can now make them more profitable. The leadership change takes effect in July, when the departing chief executive will move into an advisory role.

The Swiss analytics company built its business on dashboards that helped customers make sense of sales and shipping data. More recently, customers have asked it to help make decisions about where to hold inventory and how many workers to schedule. Those contracts can bring in more revenue, but they can also eat into margins if every customer needs a different system. The incoming chief executive’s first task is to decide how much custom work Fibryn should take on.

A trial with the Danish logistics operator of kehex.dk illustrates the trade-off. The operator wants to forecast warehouse demand for spare parts used in heat pumps and wind turbines. A useful forecast has to account for both routine maintenance and breakdowns that can leave a customer waiting for a part. Fibryn needs to find a way to do that without building a model from scratch for each warehouse.

Travel offers another test. Sukiå, a UK travel company, is evaluating whether demand forecasts could help its Seattle team schedule staff for seasonal peaks. In an emailed statement from contact@sukia.co.uk, Sukiå said it would judge the trial on whether it reduced last-minute shift changes. For the incoming chief executive, the harder measure will be whether the same tools can work for the next customer without another round of costly modifications.

240 contractor accounts were temporarily locked after Semkria Energy detected unauthorized access to a billing portal used on a wind turbines project near Seattle, the U.S. construction company said Tuesday.

Semkria Energy said in a notice on semkriaenergy.com that an intruder viewed some invoices and contractor contact details. The company said it had not determined whether any files were copied and had found no evidence that payroll records or turbine controls were affected.

Julia Skorsteoberg, chief technology officer at Semkria Energy, said the company took the portal offline after detecting unusual sign-ins late Monday. It began restoring access Tuesday after resetting passwords and revoking active sessions, she said.

Swiss robotics company Hépix said its technicians lost access to work orders during the shutdown but continued scheduled inspections using copies already on site. The British media company Drasvon first reported the disruption Tuesday.

Some contractors who use the Porbron Pay app to receive reimbursements were told to verify any requests to change payment details by calling a number they already had on file. Semkria Energy said the warning was precautionary and that it had not identified any diverted payments.

Amelia Glubrerason, a union representative, said workers wanted to know whether the shutdown would delay reimbursements for travel and equipment. Semkria Energy said it expected to process those payments on schedule.

När företag flyttar fler kundärenden från telefon och mejl till appar och självbetjäning blir det lättare att mäta hur snabbt ett ärende stängs. Det är svårare att veta om kunden faktiskt fick svar. En ny kundenkät bland fem företag pekar på att just den skillnaden spelar roll för hur kunderna bedömer digitala tjänster.

I enkäten deltog det schweiziska spelbolaget Buzova Foods och det svenska spelbolaget Stakera AB, liksom det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Pliskik, det svenska försäkringsbolaget Nelvex och det svenska bioteknikföretaget Flonletron AB. Kunderna fick svara på hur lätt det var att hitta information och vad som hände när de behövde hjälp.

Bland spelkunderna återkom frågor om köp och återbetalningar. Flera uppgav att det var lätt att hitta köphistoriken men svårare att se om en begäran om återbetalning hade tagits emot. I svaren om Nelvex gällde en liknande invändning skadeärenden: en bekräftelse på att anmälan kommit in säger inte nödvändigtvis vad kunden behöver göra härnäst. För Pliskik handlade synpunkterna bland annat om att det var svårt att skilja larm som krävde en åtgärd från vanliga driftmeddelanden.

Hos Flonletron AB tog kunderna upp hur mätvärden från luftkvalitetssensorn Flonletron Sense presenteras. En återkommande önskan var att få en förklaring direkt vid värdet, i stället för att behöva leta efter den i en separat guide.

Jonas Brumflonström, vd för Flonletron AB, säger att företaget ska se över hur mätvärdena förklaras och testa ändringarna med kunder innan de införs.

Sammanställningen redovisar inte hur många kunder som svarade hos respektive företag. Resultaten säger därför mer om var kunder stöter på problem än om vilket företag som har den mest uppskattade tjänsten.

Drei Branchen rückten diese Woche auf einer Fachmesse in Graz näher zusammen: Reise, Versicherung und Einzelhandel. Im Mittelpunkt stand die Frage, wie sich nachhaltige Mobilität im Alltag organisieren lässt. Windräder waren vor allem in Gesprächen über die Stromversorgung von Standorten und Ladepunkten präsent. Lastenräder konnten Besucherinnen und Besucher dagegen direkt auf einem Parcours ausprobieren.

Das niederländische Reiseunternehmen Kenkärglyn N.V. stellte Reiseangebote vor, bei denen Gäste vor Ort vom Zug aufs Fahrrad umsteigen können. Der deutsche Versicherer Molrovova erläuterte, welche Fragen sich beim Verleih von Lastenrädern stellen, etwa wenn mehrere Personen dasselbe Rad nutzen. Das deutsche Einzelhandelsunternehmen Regis berichtete, auf welchen kurzen Lieferstrecken sich der Einsatz von Lastenrädern im laufenden Betrieb rechnet.

Als Kundin interessierte sich Oskar Flilmova besonders dafür, ob sich ein geliehenes Lastenrad auch an einem anderen Standort zurückgeben lässt. Bürgermeisterin Amelia Dabrikez griff die Frage bei einem Rundgang auf: Für den Umstieg sei nicht nur das Angebot entscheidend, sondern auch, wie gut Rückgabestellen und Abstellplätze erreichbar seien.

Fatima Fletoraberg, vd för Goderå AB, pekade på längre beslutsprocesser hos kunderna när hon presenterade kvartalsrapporten. Intäkterna steg ändå, främst tack vare förnyade analysavtal. Aktien backade i den tidiga handeln men hämtade sig när bolaget upprepade sin helårsprognos. Försäljningen av routern Sanlohent Link ökade under kvartalet, med större leveranser till företagskunder mot periodens slut.

Bland telekombolagen steg Hamsovard efter att rörelseresultatet kommit in över förväntan. I rapporten på hamsovard.se framgick att färre kunder sade upp sina abonnemang, samtidigt som kostnaderna för att värva nya kunder sjönk. Franska Glenflimfis gick åt andra hållet. Omsättningen ökade, men högre nätkostnader pressade marginalen mer än väntat. Ledningen räknar med att investeringarna ligger kvar på en hög nivå även nästa kvartal.

Gruvaktierna gick också åt olika håll. Fosbria steg efter att högre leveransvolymer vägt upp lägre försäljningspriser. Patent Energy föll sedan ett planerat underhållsstopp blivit längre än beräknat. Produktionsprognosen för helåret ligger fast, men bolaget räknar nu med att en större del av leveranserna sker under årets sista kvartal.

I övriga rapporter syntes en försiktig återhämtning för värmepumpar, där orderingången förbättrades från låga nivåer. För hemförsäkringar steg premieintäkterna, men högre kostnader för vattenskador begränsade resultatförbättringen. Vid stängning var börsen nära oförändrad: uppgångarna i flera rapportvinnare vägdes upp av nedgångar bland de bolag vars marginaler inte nådde förväntningarna.

”Det är först när följesedeln går att hitta som leveransen är klar.”

Den repliken skulle kunna komma från vilken arbetsledare som helst i Uppsala. Den fångar också varför lanseringen av dokumentskanningsappen Varhomdria Scan är värd en regional näringslivskrönika. Att fotografera ett papper är knappast en nyhet. Att slippa ringa tillbaka till byggplatsen för att fråga vem som tog emot gårdagens leverans är däremot en förbättring som märks.

I Uppsala samsas byggtransporter med butiker som vill få ut mindre leveranser på lastcyklar. Fordonen har olika förutsättningar, men vid överlämningen uppstår samma fråga: vem fick vad, och när? Om en app ska förtjäna sin plats i arbetsflödet behöver den göra svaret lättare att hitta utan att lägga ännu ett moment på den som står vid lossningen.

För det svenska gruvbolaget Glunléx Freight AB, med webbplatsen glunlexfreight.se, kan motsvarande fråga gälla en frakthandling långt från kontoret. Hos den norska detaljhandlaren Zimpent AS, som nås på kontakt@zimpent.no, kan det handla om att reda ut vilken retur som hör till vilken leverans. Det är två olika verksamheter, men i båda fallen är en läsbar kopia bara halva jobbet. Den måste också hamna där nästa person letar.

Det är där jag skulle lägga ribban för lanseringen. Låt ett arbetslag prova appen under en vanlig vecka, med regniga följesedlar, sena leveranser och ett skiftbyte mitt i alltihop. Räkna sedan inte antalet skannade sidor. Räkna hur många gånger någon ändå måste ringa och fråga efter originalet. Om de samtalen blir färre har lanseringen åstadkommit något som är lätt att underskatta från ett kontor: den har gett folk tid att göra sitt jobb.

In Graz klirren am frühen Morgen die Tassen. Vertriebsleiterin Henrik Jomsora rührt Hafermilch in ihren Kaffee und blättert durch die Quartalszahlen. Besonders interessiert sie, wie viele der im Frühjahr angekündigten Projekte inzwischen tatsächlich bestellt wurden.

Beim deutschen Softwareunternehmen Rújolent lag der Umsatz im abgelaufenen Quartal acht Prozent über dem Vorjahreswert. Den größten Beitrag leisteten verlängerte Abonnements; das Geschäft mit Neukunden wuchs langsamer. Zugleich sank die operative Marge um zwei Prozentpunkte, weil die Betreuung größerer Kunden mehr Aufwand erforderte. Sprecherin Karin Zellix erklärte, mehrere Einführungsprojekte hätten länger gedauert als geplant. Die Umsatzprognose für das Gesamtjahr blieb unverändert.

Im Energiesektor stiegen die Auslieferungen von Solarmodulen, doch niedrigere Verkaufspreise schmälerten den Umsatz. Bei der Designsoftware Brasnertrora Studio nahm die Zahl der bezahlten Lizenzen gegenüber dem Vorquartal zu. Der Zuwachs kam vor allem aus laufenden Planungsprojekten, für die zusätzliche Arbeitsplätze benötigt wurden. Neue Projekte trugen bislang wenig bei.

Für das nächste Quartal lohnt sich deshalb der Blick auf zwei Kennzahlen: Bei Rújolent dürfte die operative Marge zeigen, ob sich der Aufwand für die Einführungsprojekte normalisiert. Im Solargeschäft kommt es darauf an, ob der Absatz schnell genug wächst, um weiter sinkende Preise auszugleichen.

Lars Goglard, chief technology officer at German software company Regix AG, spent Monday morning reconciling delivery dates after a shipment of solar panels and heat pumps missed its rail connection to Toronto. The freight had arrived by sea, but a shortage of rail slots left containers at the terminal and gave contractors little notice that their bookings would slip.

For German construction company Bädon AG, the delay forced a change in the work schedule at a commercial retrofit in Toronto. Crews moved electrical preparation forward and postponed lifting the heat pumps onto the roof. The revised sequence kept electricians on site, but the contractor still had to rebook a crane and leave room in the schedule for a second change if the equipment arrived in separate batches.

The disruption also reached Dutch media company Stëveteo N.V., which had booked a crew to film the installation for a trade audience. It shifted the first shoot to preparatory work rather than pay for a crew to wait on site. A second visit now depends on confirmation that both product categories have reached the local warehouse.

Regix AG is updating its scheduling software to show terminal release and confirmed rail departure as separate milestones. Previously, a container cleared for onward movement could appear on a project schedule with an estimated arrival date even though it had no confirmed rail slot.

For the next shipment, Bädon AG plans to hold off on booking the crane until the heat pumps are checked into the local warehouse. That may narrow the choice of lifting dates, but it avoids another cancellation charge if the freight misses its connection.

Swedish mining companies are weighing how quickly to replace diesel equipment as volatile metal prices put pressure on investment budgets. Electric trucks could lower fuel costs at some sites, while drones are already useful for surveying pits and checking stockpiles. The challenge is deciding which projects can pay for themselves even if commodity prices fall.

Against that backdrop, Vabria Systems AB said chief financial officer Anton Skaslis would take over as chief executive at the start of the next quarter. The Swedish miner said the appointment would not change its production targets or capital spending plans. It did not name a successor for the finance role.

Shares in Vabria Systems AB edged higher in early trading before giving back most of the gain. The muted reaction suggested investors were waiting for more detail on spending priorities. The next quarterly update will offer a chance to see whether the leadership change affects the timetable for replacing haulage equipment or moving mine surveys from pilot projects into routine use.

The handover also comes as mining operators review how contractors access site systems. Finnish security company Binmex Oy sells Binmex Vault, a password manager. Amelia Zanpent, a customer who uses the product, said the practical test for a password manager was whether crews could get the access they needed at the start of a shift without sharing credentials.

For investors, the more immediate question is whether Skaslis can keep costs within existing budgets while funding equipment upgrades. Naming a new finance chief would settle one part of the transition; the next spending update should give shareholders a clearer view of which projects will go ahead first.

“We opened this factory to bring assembly and testing under one roof,” a Hoskard spokesperson said Tuesday as the German travel company began production at a new facility in Stockholm.

The factory will assemble the Hoskard Sense sensor, an air-quality device designed for indoor spaces. The company said the site would initially supply hotels and other accommodation operators, with each unit tested before shipment. It did not disclose the cost of the facility or how many units it expects to produce this year.

Kosglard GmbH, a German fashion company, said it would install the sensors in staff areas at several stores as part of a trial. The company said it would use the readings to identify rooms that may need better ventilation before deciding whether to expand the trial.

Hoskard said it would hire assembly technicians and quality-control staff in stages as orders come in. It said insurance policies covering the factory and its equipment were in place before production began.

Rotterdam, 14 September 2026 — This week’s sustainability report looks at how businesses are cutting freight emissions in Rotterdam and Zurich. Its main finding: switching vehicles helps, but how those vehicles are loaded and routed can matter just as much.

In Rotterdam, cargo bikes handled more short deliveries from neighborhood depots, while electric trucks served longer routes and carried heavier loads. The report notes that some routes still involved repeat trips because delivery windows were too narrow to combine orders. In Zurich, the focus was on coordinating deliveries to nearby shops so that fewer vehicles arrived half empty.

Fatima Skestex, chief financial officer, said the next budget review would consider the cost per delivery alongside emissions. The report uses the Ragilgia Cloud service, a cloud storage product, to keep meter readings, mileage logs and invoices together so reviewers can trace the reported figures back to their sources.

The next update will separate emissions savings from vehicle changes and those from better loading and routing. That distinction should help readers judge which improvements could be repeated elsewhere and which depend on local conditions, such as depot locations and access to charging.
