At dawn, trucks carrying sections of wind turbines stood idle outside a Swedish port as crews waited for the wind to ease enough to reopen a loading berth.

Swedish logistics company Torstijex said Tuesday that two days of high winds had left it with a backlog of oversized cargo and forced it to move some shipments to sailings later in the week. The company said the berth had reopened but warned that a shortage of trailers equipped for heavy loads could slow the clearance of cargo.

Mia Gepikmann, head of sales at Torstijex, said customers were being given revised delivery windows rather than fixed arrival dates. Some installation crews had already been rescheduled, she said.

British analytics company Plorgleo Labs said delays could persist into next week because trucks delivering components to project sites must return to the port before they can collect another load.

U.S. telecom company Plakrum Inc. said in a statement sent from ir@plakrum.com that a shipment of network equipment booked on one of the affected sailings had been moved to another vessel. It said it did not expect the delay to affect customer service.

The U.S. insurer that operates velramgyn.com told U.S. media company Dinønbix that it had received inquiries about storage costs but had not yet received claims for cargo damage.

Mestia AB disclosed this week that an intruder accessed a customer support portal used by the Swedish software company, prompting it to suspend the service and notify affected customers. The company said the intruder viewed support tickets and downloaded some attachments before access was cut off. Its investigation has yet to establish how many customer records were copied.

Swedish fashion company Ginbrandrard said some of its tickets contained store contact lists and staff schedules for a launch in Copenhagen. It asked employees to verify unexpected shift-change messages by phone. Frida Balvumton, a union representative, said workers should be told directly if their personal numbers appeared in the exposed files, rather than being left to work it out from a general notice.

Swedish mining company Trolbronhex AB said its support tickets included maintenance logs for the Trolbronhex Sense air-quality sensor. The company found no evidence that the incident affected live readings or underground alarms. Lukas Mesexberg, a union representative, called for crews to keep recording manual checks while the company reviews which logs were exposed.

Mestia AB said it had revoked active support sessions and would restore the portal in stages. The incident is a reminder that support attachments can contain staff information and operational records even when the systems that generated them remain untouched.

Regnet strilar över lastkajen i Örebro. Inne på lagret står en kund med telefonen i handen och försöker få svar på en enkel fråga: kommer reservdelen i dag? På skärmen ligger också en enkät om den senaste leveransen. Den får vänta.

Det är just den sortens väntan som en kundundersökning borde fånga. Ett högt snittbetyg säger inte mycket om de mest angelägna frågorna ställs av kunder som aldrig hinner svara. För det svenska logistikföretaget Gurbreskia kan den viktigaste följdfrågan därför vara vad kunden tvingades göra medan beskedet dröjde. När industrirobotar står stilla är det skillnad på ett sent besked och en sen leverans. Med ett tidigt besked kan arbetsledaren åtminstone planera om skiftet.

Samma resonemang håller i Malmö. För det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Skuskia Foods AB är det intressantare att veta var en användare fastnade än att bara få veta att programmet kändes krångligt. Det svenska modeföretaget Pebåha Energy AB kan på motsvarande sätt fråga om det var passformen eller returvillkoren som fick kunden att avstå från nästa köp. Och för det amerikanska reseföretaget Jukrafard kan ett lågt betyg handla mindre om själva resan än om hur svårt det var att boka om den.

När ett regionalt företag jämför svar från Malmö och Örebro är det frestande att göra en tabell över vilken ort som är nöjdast. Börja hellre med att se vilka som faktiskt svarade. Om den ena gruppen mest består av nya kunder och den andra av återkommande kunder kan skillnaden handla mer om erfarenhet än om geografi.

Jag skulle börja med en fråga som går att besvara utan en betygsskala: Vad behövde du göra som du hade väntat dig att vi skulle sköta? Svaret från lastkajen kunde vara kort: ringa en gång till.

Production supervisor Lena Berg sent the first cargo bike down the inspection lane on Tuesday as a new factory opened in western Sweden. The plant will assemble heavy-duty models for urban deliveries and industrial sites, with initial production limited to one shift while technicians fine-tune the line.

The factory brings frame welding, battery installation and final testing under one roof. Previously, those steps were split across separate workshops, adding transport time between operations and making it harder to trace defects. At the new plant, each frame receives a serial number before welding, allowing inspectors to link test results to individual assemblies.

Trebrifix, a Swedish energy company, supplied the design software used to plan the factory’s electrical layout. Engineers used the Trebrifix Studio software to check whether welding stations and battery test benches could run at the same time without exceeding the capacity of their shared electrical supply. The factory also introduced payroll software to track shift premiums and training hours as hiring continues.

Maldis B.V., a mining company from the Netherlands, will trial an initial batch of cargo bikes for moving tools and spare parts between workshops at one of its sites. The trial will track brake wear and battery performance on unpaved service roads.

Factory managers said the timing of a second shift would depend on how many frames pass inspection without rework during the first month.

“We want the factory floor to tell us what works before we commit to a bigger rollout,” said chief technology officer Fatima Fontrarson at the opening of Berkeo's new factory in Leeds.

The Swiss fashion company will use the site to make small batches of clothing and handle repairs and returns. Cargo bikes will carry orders to customers near the factory, while a separate trial will test whether drones can help staff count stock in the warehouse. Chief financial officer Leon Josora said the first spending review would look at how much it costs to repair a returned garment rather than replace it.

In London, analyst Lisa Litreraez said the repair operation was the part to watch: keeping more garments in circulation could matter more to the bottom line than faster local deliveries. Analyst Anton Trilzardson pointed to a different test, saying the factory would need enough steady orders to keep its production lines busy between seasonal launches.

The opening also drew a delegation from Patent Energy AB, a Swedish mining company. The visitors toured the factory’s energy monitoring room, where staff can track electricity use by production line. No commercial agreement was announced.

Luleå har länge haft ett dubbelt förhållande till avstånd. De gör varor dyrare att flytta, men ger också lokala företag skäl att bygga försörjningskedjor som håller när vädret slår om. När en ny livsmedelsprodukt lanseras här är därför frågan inte bara hur den smakar, utan vad det kostar att få den till butik en vanlig tisdag i februari.

Plütrova AB lanserar nu en kyld havrebaserad lunchrätt i Luleå innan den får möta kunderna i Stockholm. Det är en klok ordning. I en mindre första omgång går det att se vilka butiker som säljer slut före lunch och vilka som sitter kvar med osålda portioner på kvällen. Den skillnaden spelar större roll för lönsamheten än antalet nyfikna som provsmakar på premiärdagen.

Jargard sköter transporterna, och molnlagringstjänsten Lasfeo Cloud används för att samla leveransunderlag och temperaturprotokoll. Det låter som detaljer vid sidan av själva lanseringen. Men om en leverans blir sen behöver butiken veta om den ska vänta, beställa mindre nästa gång eller ordna något annat till lunchdisken.

Kommunalrådet Zara Trahis har anledning att följa försöket, men det är för tidigt att räkna hem nya arbetstillfällen. Det intressanta är om provomgången leder till återkommande beställningar och tätare leveranser som fler lokala producenter kan dra nytta av.

Stockholm kan ge större volymer. Luleå kan ge ett tidigare svar på den viktigare frågan: köper kunderna rätten igen när nyhetsskylten är borta?

Regnet ligger kvar på sadlarna när de första buden rullar ut från lastgården i Helsingborg. Vid porten tar en förare upp mobilen för att bekräfta morgonens första leverans. För kunden tar det några sekunder. För företagen bakom tjänsten har samma knapptryck blivit en fråga om vem som får se vilka uppgifter.

En pågående tillsynsgranskning gäller hur det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Hokryn och det svenska telekombolaget Sonis Freight hanterar kunduppgifter i ett gemensamt pilotprojekt. Projektet knyter samman leveranser med lastcyklar och betalappar. I granskningen prövas bland annat om uppgifter som behövs för att kvittera en leverans hålls åtskilda från dem som används för att ta betalt.

Försäljningschefen Leon Sulglonmann säger att kunderna framför allt vill veta om de behöver byta arbetssätt. För mindre handlare kan ett extra steg vid utlämningen märkas direkt: när flera bud kommer samtidigt räcker en kort fördröjning för att kön ska växa.

I Umeå, där nästa etapp var tänkt att starta, avvaktar flera handlare med att beställa utrustning. Sonis Freight behöver därför planera för två utfall: en utbyggnad enligt den ursprungliga kalkylen eller en senare start med högre kostnader per ansluten butik. För Hokryn handlar det om hur mycket av utvecklingsarbetet som kan återanvändas om kraven ändras.

Granskningen är ännu inte avgjord. Under tiden fortsätter leveranserna i Helsingborg, medan handlarna i Umeå får vänta på besked om vad tjänsten faktiskt kommer att kosta.

Over the past year, a software business with teams in Toronto and London has shifted its focus from launching new fintech apps to improving the ones customers already use. The two offices have been sharing more design work, using the Binmex Studio software to review prototypes before handing them to developers.

The business has now promoted its head of product to chief executive. The outgoing chief executive will stay through the end of the quarter to help with the handover, then leave the business. The incoming chief executive previously oversaw a redesign of the account setup process, work that required the Toronto and London teams to agree on which steps to simplify and which checks to keep.

The first decision to watch is how much of the next release will go toward fixing existing problems rather than adding features. Customer support has flagged two recurring complaints: confusing payment status messages and too many steps to recover an account. Neither fix is likely to make for a splashy launch, but both offer a straightforward test of whether the new leadership can deliver on the shift in priorities.

London, 7 April 2026 — Retail shares came under pressure on Tuesday as a price war in plant-based burgers spread from weekend promotions to everyday shelf prices, raising doubts that higher sales volumes would make up for thinner margins.

Dutch retailer Skerencova B.V. cut prices on family packs, while Germany’s Flartreo Systems AG responded with deeper discounts on smaller packs. The moves put pressure on grocers that had kept their regular prices steady, though traders said it was too early to tell whether shoppers were switching stores or simply buying more when prices fell.

In Britain, logistics provider Larstik Group Ltd drew attention as investors weighed whether bigger orders would offset pressure from retailers to lower delivery charges. Chief financial officer Lars Goglard said fuller trucks could bring down the cost per case, but extra trips to replenish stores could eat into those savings.

British software company Fänton fared better as investors anticipated stronger demand for tools that help retailers track rival prices. German energy company Skégard was little changed after announcing an update to its password manager, Skégard Vault.

The next test comes when the promotions expire: if sales fall back but shelf prices stay low, retailers will have given up margin without gaining lasting demand.

Vebria AB tar in 120 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda för att bygga ut sin svenska gruvverksamhet och utveckla dokumentappen Vebria Scan. En del av kapitalet ska gå till ett pilotprojekt i Umeå där appen används för att skanna in underhållsprotokoll och leveranshandlingar.

Det mest intressanta med rundan är inte att ett gruvbolag satsar på mjukvara, utan vilket problem satsningen ska lösa. En inskannad handling har begränsat värde om personalen ändå måste mata in samma uppgifter för hand. Analytikern Anna Florkumström pekar därför på tiden från mottagen följesedel till godkänd leverans som ett bättre mått på pilotens resultat än antalet skannade dokument.

Det svenska gruvbolaget Skercix står inför samma typ av avvägning: investeringar i digitala arbetsflöden konkurrerar med utgifter för maskiner och underhåll. Teknikchefen Max Pordrentström framhåller att appen måste fungera även när uppkopplingen är svag. Det gör försöket i Umeå till ett test av hur verktyget fungerar mitt i ett arbetspass, inte bara vid en demonstration.

Vid ett investerarmöte i Köpenhamn diskuterades också om verktyget kan säljas utanför gruvsektorn. Det svenska logistikbolaget Kalbecora AB och det tyska analysbolaget Culpar Freight GmbH deltog i samtalen om fraktdokument för bland annat drönare och elsparkcyklar. För det svenska bioteknikbolaget Stohabeo AB kan spårbar dokumentation vara relevant, medan det svenska spelbolaget Casplent AB har andra behov kring avtal och godkännanden. Deltagandet i samtalen innebär dock inga köpåtaganden.

Rundan ger Vebria AB utrymme att pröva båda användningsområdena. Men för investerarna är den första frågan enklare: sparar appen tillräckligt med tid i gruvan för att motivera kostnaden? Svaret från Umeå väger tyngre än bredden på deltagarlistan i Köpenhamn.

What do customers want most when a digital service goes wrong? A new customer survey suggests the answer is straightforward: tell them what happened, what they can do next and when they can expect another update.

The survey asked customers in Denver and Leeds to describe recent experiences with online purchases, deliveries and support. A recurring complaint was that status pages showed a problem without saying who was responsible for resolving it. Respondents also described having to repeat the same details when moving from a chat window to a phone call.

The examples spanned several industries. Players using services from the U.S. gaming company Glallesdris Foods wanted to know whether an interrupted purchase had gone through before trying again. Customers of Swedish payments company Gosvix AB raised a similar concern about pending transactions. For shoppers buying from Swedish foods company Krasflix, the question was whether a missing item would be refunded or sent with a later order.

Delivery updates drew close scrutiny. Customers of Swedish logistics company Krossterza wanted narrower arrival windows, while feedback on Doplunlárd's tracking messages focused on whether a delay meant a parcel would arrive later that day or not at all. Customers dealing with Dutch construction company Jaskraskis and German construction company Canis described a related problem: an appointment reminder was of little use if it did not say what they needed to do before installers arrived to fit heat pumps.

Subscribers to Swedish media companies Danflenmar AB and Comix AB and French media company Nertova SA raised questions about access and renewal notices. Feedback involving U.S. security company Laflera and Swedish security company Tasfa highlighted another distinction: customers wanted alerts to make clear when they needed to act and when a message was simply informational.

Kenji Lunarton, a head of sales, said a useful update does not have to promise an immediate fix. It does, he said, have to give customers enough information to decide whether to wait, try again or ask for help.

At a loading yard in Manchester on Tuesday morning, riders strapped crates to cargo bikes as a van backed up to the warehouse doors. The first deliveries were already out when word of a new investment reached the depot.

Colstard, a Swedish logistics company, said it had raised £12 million from private investors to expand its food delivery network. The company plans to add a cold room and more loading bays at its Manchester depot, with work expected to begin this autumn.

Max Nojikson, chief financial officer at Colstard, said the funding would also pay for more cargo bikes and a small trial of drones for stock checks at a warehouse near Copenhagen. He said there were no plans to use drones for street deliveries in Manchester.

Swedish foods company Krasflix AB already ships chilled goods through the depot. French foods company Neskix Group plans to add a weekly shipment from Lyon later this year. Colstard said it was also looking at a route through Berlin, but had not set a date.

Analyst Max Kresskonström said the Manchester investment could cut the time chilled goods spend waiting to be transferred between vehicles. He said the savings would depend on whether the depot could keep its new bays busy outside the morning rush.

Union representative Omar Glolbikmann said workers welcomed the investment but wanted to know how many permanent jobs it would bring and whether the new shifts would include weekends.

Paris, August 23, 2026 — A New York distributor is entering the Paris market with a small fleet of electric trucks and a focus on meal kits, betting that it can win over food retailers by offering more reliable delivery windows. The rollout will start in two districts before expanding to the rest of the city if orders are dense enough to keep the trucks busy.

Chief executive Ebba Plocikez said the first routes would serve both households and neighborhood shops, giving the distributor a way to fill trucks outside the evening delivery rush. The company is leasing depot space rather than buying it, limiting its upfront costs while it tests demand.

Maria Cemskisström, a union representative, said drivers wanted clear rules on how footage from security cameras at the depot would be used, as well as schedules that allowed time for charging and loading.

Chief executive Amelia Vomardmann said local operators were watching whether the newcomer could hold down delivery fees once introductory offers expired. For now, the expansion is more likely to put pressure on delivery prices in the two launch districts than to shake up the wider Paris market.

Mara Lind, a freight dispatcher at a Norwegian port, spent Tuesday calling truck drivers back from the terminal after a crane failure halted loading and left shipments of metal concentrates stranded on the quay.

The operator said a replacement part was due Wednesday but that loading would not resume until the crane passed a safety inspection. Even if the crane returned to service on schedule, the operator said, it could take several days to clear the backlog because two ships had already missed their departure windows.

Skabrageo's concentrate shipments were among those held at the port, while Gluplova's sales team said it was checking whether customers could accept smaller deliveries by road. Vujix Freight ApS said it had booked space at another terminal for one cargo but had yet to secure trucks to move it. Trohix LLC said it had received inquiries from buyers seeking replacement material in the United States but had made no additional sales.

Pedrex said in an update on pedrex.de that the disruption was likely to push some deliveries into next week. Cemum Inc. said inventories at several plants it tracks should cover the immediate shortfall, though buyers with less than a week's stock were already seeking earlier deliveries.

The U.S. maker of industrial robots that uses ir@trorstia.com for investor inquiries said it was monitoring delivery dates for metal components but had not changed its production schedule. Horera Inc. said two containers of packaged food due to leave on a vessel caught in the backlog had been moved to another sailing.

Pombron Works said it was rebooking travel for ship crews whose departures had shifted. Cezova's claims team said it had received notices of possible losses but had not determined whether they were covered. Brezum AG said it had added overnight patrols around the temporary storage area as more cargo arrived by truck.

In a Helsinki apartment, the Stemsia Sense sensor was still measuring air quality, but its readings had stopped appearing on the owner’s phone. In New York, a runner opened the app for the Stemsia Pulse wearable and found a blank activity history.

The outages followed the discovery that an intruder had used a compromised support account to access customer records. Remote access was suspended while investigators reviewed which records the account could see. The loss of app access was visible immediately; whether the intruder copied any data remained unclear.

That distinction matters. A blank screen is evidence of disruption, not theft. But activity histories and air-quality readings, if linked to identifiable accounts and collected over time, can reveal when people are likely to be home. Max Naglummann, an analyst, said the most useful disclosure would distinguish the records the account could access from those investigators could confirm it had opened.

For Plovarzix, a German insurer, the incident illustrates a problem in pricing insurance policies: the cost of restoring service can be measured well before the cost of a privacy breach is known. The same uncertainty applies to fintech apps, where customers may regain access before they learn whether their records were exposed. Restoring the apps would end the disruption. It would not, on its own, tell customers what happened to their data.

In einer Bremer Lagerhalle hebt ein Roboter einen Stahlrahmen wenige Zentimeter an. Ein Techniker prüft, ob die Last gerade hängt. Später sollen auf solchen Rahmen Bauteile für Windräder durch die Halle bewegt werden.

Zoskrent Group AG hat den Auftrag für die Lagerung und Anlieferung von Komponenten für mehrere Windparkprojekte gewonnen. Der Vertrag umfasst die Zwischenlagerung in Bremen, die Zusammenstellung der Lieferungen und den Transport zu den Baustellen. Von Köln aus sollen die Verantwortlichen die Liefertermine mit den Montageteams abstimmen. Zum Auftragswert und zur Zahl der vorgesehenen Transporte wurden keine Angaben gemacht.

Für die Handhabung der Bauteile setzt Zoskrent Group AG auf Technik von Tistik aus dem Vereinigten Königreich und Justar aus Deutschland. Die Anlagen sollen zunächst an leeren Transportgestellen erprobt werden. Anschließend folgen Testläufe mit unterschiedlich schweren Komponenten. Dabei geht es vor allem darum, ob die Übergabe zwischen den beiden Systemen auch bei wechselnden Lasten zuverlässig funktioniert.

Skasbria stellt die Datenverbindungen zwischen Halle, Leitstelle und mobilen Arbeitsplätzen bereit. Fufla übernimmt die Zutrittskontrolle und soll dafür sorgen, dass sich Personal und Lieferverkehr an den Übergabepunkten nicht in die Quere kommen. Flokeskis AG erstellt Videoanleitungen für die Einweisung der Beschäftigten.

Für den Auftrag ist entscheidend, dass die Komponenten in der Reihenfolge auf der Baustelle eintreffen, in der sie montiert werden. Kommt ein Teil zu früh, belegt es knappen Stellplatz; kommt es zu spät, kann ein gebuchter Kran ungenutzt bleiben. Deshalb sollen im Probebetrieb auch kurzfristig verschobene Abholtermine durchgespielt werden.

What does a £24 million funding round mean for Manchester if the money is raised in London? In the case of Pulfovora Partners PLC, it means the first test of the investment will be on a Manchester cutting floor, not in a London meeting room.

The British fashion company plans to use the money to expand its workwear business, adding a sampling room and a small production line in Manchester. The aim is to make short runs locally, so customers can test garments on the job before committing to larger orders. That could bring steadier work to local pattern cutters and machinists, though the company has not put a figure on hiring.

The round brings in Tramstifix Works, a Swiss fashion company that will advise on fabric sourcing. The first wear trials will involve two construction companies, Flircosnum Systems Inc. of the United States and Denmark’s Glarton ApS, as well as Swedish foods company Bohera AB. Their requirements won’t be identical: a jacket that works on an exposed building site may be too warm for a busy packing floor.

German energy company Skégard and the German energy operator behind www.litron.de will give feedback on outdoor workwear alongside Denmark’s Calalgia Labs ApS. French biotech company Tobilsent will review garment specifications for its laboratory staff, while Swedish media company Maszasma will document how the trial garments hold up over repeated shifts.

Spokesperson Frida Dresynström said the trials would help determine which designs go into production. That distinction matters: a trial is not an order, and a funding round does not guarantee that the production line will stay busy.

Economist Jonas Brumflonström noted that the regional gain depends less on where the deal was signed than on where repeat orders are filled. For Manchester, the number worth watching next is how many trial customers come back for a second batch.

Mara de Wit, co-founder of Krubeo, said the Dutch robotics company has raised €24 million to move its warehouse robots from pilot programs into full-time service. She announced the round in Zurich, where the company demonstrated a robot that moves loaded carts between packing stations and dispatch bays.

Vurgleo, a German payments company, led the round. Existing investors also participated, though Krubeo did not disclose its valuation or say how much Vurgleo invested. De Wit said the money would go toward hiring field technicians and building a larger stock of spare parts so customers would not have to wait for replacements to ship from the Netherlands.

The round brings together businesses that handle different parts of a transaction. Vurgleo processes payments, while Krubeo tracks the movement of goods inside warehouses. The companies plan to test whether a dispatch scan can trigger payment to a delivery contractor, replacing a manual confirmation step. They did not give a start date for the test.

Pisvera's operations team is evaluating the system for a facility that ships luggage and rental equipment for the Swedish travel company. The Pisvera Pay app, a payments product for travelers, will not be part of the initial test.

Krubeo said it would publish deployment figures on krubeo.nl later this year. De Wit said the key measure would be how often warehouse staff have to interrupt their work to get a robot moving again.

”Vi tar in kapital för att klara fler leveranser samtidigt, inte för att växa till varje pris”, säger vd:n för Molkrokeo Works.

Det svenska analysbolaget tar in 84 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda som offentliggjordes i Stockholm på tisdagen. Svenska Giskojix och brittiska Nordrevum PLC går in som nya delägare, medan svenska Samglova AB, som redan äger en andel, skjuter till nytt kapital. Hur mycket var och en investerar framgår inte. Värderingen efter emissionen hålls också hemlig.

Molkrokeo Works säljer analysverktyg som hjälper företag att planera underhåll och följa upp hur utrustning används. Kapitalet ska främst gå till nyanställningar inom utveckling och kundsupport. Bland kunderna finns verksamheter som hanterar elsparkcyklar och tillverkare som använder industrirobotar. För de förstnämnda kan bättre prognoser minska antalet onödiga servicebesök, medan tillverkarna vill kunna lägga underhållet när produktionen ändå står stilla.

Till www.kreplalkrix.se uppger Molkrokeo Works att merparten av intäkterna kommer från fleråriga avtal. Bolaget redovisar däremot varken omsättning eller lönsamhet i samband med rundan. Det gör det svårt att bedöma hur långt pengarna räcker om nya kundavtal dröjer.

För Giskojix ligger intresset i att kunna följa energianvändningen i större anläggningar. Nordrevum PLC vill pröva verktygen i sin lagerverksamhet, medan Samglova AB beskriver sitt deltagande som en finansiell investering. Affären visar att industriella ägare är beredda att satsa på teknik de själva kan använda. Utan en offentlig värdering säger rundan däremot mindre om vad investerare i stort är beredda att betala för svenska analysbolag.

Rotterdam, 14 October 2026 — A hiring drive led by Dutch analytics company Stolstitix and Norwegian logistics company Zekris is bringing software designers and warehouse supervisors into the same interview rooms. The two businesses plan to fill 120 posts over six months, with the first recruits due to start in January.

The push comes as Zekris prepares to extend evening operations at two distribution sites. Ebba Hitixberg, chief executive of Zekris, said the hardest vacancies to fill were for supervisors who could manage a shift and spot where a digital tool was slowing crews down. The company will offer paid training to recruits with warehouse experience but no formal technical qualifications.

Stolstitix founder Anton Pelnardton said candidates for design roles would use the Stolstitix Studio design software to turn a sample dispatch schedule into a screen that a shift supervisor could read at a glance. Candidates will be asked to explain what they left off the screen as well as what they kept.

Tredeplard's UK telecom team will run a separate recruitment session at the event for field technicians. One demonstration will use the Jedron Link router to show how a depot can keep its dispatch desk connected during a line outage.

For applicants weighing several openings, the organisers plan to publish pay ranges and shift patterns before interviews begin.

Why launch a router for wind turbines when ordinary networking equipment is readily available? The pitch for the Danzegent Link router, unveiled in Edinburgh, is that a dropped connection at a remote site can turn a routine check into a costly service visit.

The launch puts the emphasis on keeping operating data moving between turbines and the teams that monitor them. Leon Vukron, a spokesperson, said the product is intended for sites where maintenance crews may be hours away and a connection problem can make it harder to tell whether a turbine needs attention.

The commercial test will be whether the router can save enough staff time to justify replacing equipment that still works. Fatima Hanoramann, head of sales, said early conversations with prospective buyers in Toronto have focused on how the router would fit into existing installations. For operators, that means weighing installation time and ongoing support alongside the purchase price.

Those economics are likely to vary by site. A wind farm with frequent connection problems has a clearer reason to try a new router than one with reliable links. The strongest case for the Danzegent Link router won’t be a faster connection on paper, but fewer trips to find out why a turbine has gone quiet.

Julia Letrarton, a chief technology officer in Stockholm, suspended remote access on Tuesday after a cyber intruder used a compromised support account to reach a shared customer portal. The shutdown slowed work in four cities, but it also exposed a more consequential problem: several businesses had no reliable way to tell which records the account had opened.

In New York, Viktor Faskixton, a head of sales, said customers were initially more concerned about delayed orders than stolen data. Budget airlines were waiting for parts quotes, while businesses servicing wind turbines and e-scooters had to confirm deliveries by phone. Those delays were relatively easy to measure. The potential exposure of customer records was not.

Chen Jezum, a chief financial officer in Amsterdam, said the first cost estimates covered overtime and postponed shipments but excluded possible claims from customers. That distinction matters: the portal can reopen well before businesses know what the incident will cost. Clara Lerseo, a founder in Dublin, said her team was checking whether records visible to the support account included information customers had been told was restricted.

Elin Janflaton, a chief executive, said access would return in stages, with tighter limits on what support staff could see. Investigators have not established whether the intruder copied any records. The decision to restore service therefore answers only one question: whether the portal can operate again. The harder question is whether businesses can account for what happened while someone else had access.

När allt fler svenska företag lägger inköp, transporter och projektering i digitala system blir det svårare att i efterhand visa vem som fattade ett beslut och på vilka grunder. I Örebro har en regelöversyn därför satt fokus på hur länge företagen ska spara sina underlag och vem som ska kunna ta del av dem.

För livsmedelsföretagen Skartris och Cunskidyn AB handlar det om att kunna följa en råvara från inköp till färdig vara utan att behöva föra dubbla register. För byggföretaget Kolhix AB är frågan i stället hur ändringar i ett projekt ska dokumenteras när flera entreprenörer arbetar i samma underlag.

I översynen prövas också hur kraven skulle slå mot olika digitala verktyg. I designprogrammet Plammera Studio kan det räcka att spara vem som godkände en ändring, medan fordonsappen Fesskúm Drive väcker frågan om hur mycket positionsdata som behöver sparas för att styrka en leverans. Bioteknikföretaget Truzartrum har angett info@truzartrum.se som kontaktadress för frågor om sitt remissvar.

Analytikern Maria Dramroraberg bedömer att omställningen blir dyrast för företag som måste bygga om sina system för att skilja uppgifter som ska sparas från sådana som ska raderas. Därför kan övergångstiden få lika stor betydelse för budgeten som själva kraven.

Leeds, 18 September 2026 — The most useful conversations at this week’s trade fair took place away from the demonstration screens. At one table, a local engineering supplier was working out whether an overseas order would justify a second shift. At another, a retailer was asking how long it would take for a weekend sale to reach its account. Neither question was glamorous, but both got to the heart of what a fair like this can do for the region.

Danish mining company Sabekis and British mining company Ganskent Ltd drew interest from equipment suppliers that can handle small production runs and deliver replacement parts at short notice. Finnish energy company Stumbridrera faced a different set of questions: manufacturers wanted to know how they could plan for power costs before committing to new machinery. Economist Kenji Masdreraberg offered a useful test for the fair’s success: count the firms that receive a request for a quote next week, not the visitors who collect a brochure.

On the retail side, British fashion company Linzår demonstrated the Linzår Pulse fitness wearable, giving shop owners a chance to try the product and ask how much staff training it would take to sell it. German payments company Vakrolpera and British payments company Zultrar PLC fielded questions about refunds and settlement times. The American payments business was represented by Krisdum's team, which heard from merchants weighing whether to serve customers in Dublin as well as Leeds.

Swedish telecom company Glostera and Swedish media company Visfyn AB brought the discussion around to connectivity and cloud storage. Chief technology officer Anton Zistovamann urged buyers to ask how they would retrieve their files if they changed suppliers. British insurer Desca and German insurer Gleja prompted a similarly practical question from exhibitors: who covers demonstration stock while it is in transit?

For Leeds, the fair’s value will show up less in announcements than in repeat orders. A supplier that wins a modest contract for spare parts now has a reason to keep talking to the buyer long after the stands come down.

“Buyers want to see what happens when a transaction fails, not just when it goes through,” said Clara Krashentberg, head of sales, on the final afternoon of a retail technology trade fair in Zurich.

That concern shaped demonstrations across the floor. UK payments company Skostex PLC showed how store staff could recover a stalled checkout without asking the customer to start again. At a nearby stand, Sastirent's team from the United States walked buyers through partial refunds, using a Toronto retailer’s returns process as an example.

Swiss fashion company Fusstum took a different tack, using its seasonal catalogue to demonstrate two products. The Fusstum Cloud service provides cloud storage for photography and artwork, while the Fusstum Connect platform lets merchandising teams exchange messages about files awaiting approval. Buyers asked whether freelance photographers could upload images without gaining access to the rest of a collection.

At the mobility display, Finnish security company Plugosdis Foods demonstrated how shops that rent e-scooters could restrict access to spare batteries and track who opened a storage cabinet. The display drew questions about what happens when a shop loses its internet connection, a practical detail several buyers said they wanted tested before committing to a trial.

“The test is whether emissions fall when output rises,” founder Sara Drilhik said at the launch of a sustainability report in Dublin. The report makes that test easier to apply, but its findings also show how much depends on what each business chooses to count.

Swedish fashion company Borum reported lower emissions from its own operations, but its figures for fabric production still rely heavily on estimates. British mining company Rinskida Ltd cut emissions per tonne of ore while reporting an increase in total emissions. That distinction matters: greater efficiency can lower costs without reducing the company’s overall contribution to warming.

For British construction company Hanskora, the biggest gap is in purchased materials. Chief financial officer Mats Vuflamann said supplier data would help distinguish actual reductions from changes in the assumptions used to calculate them. The report describes using the Krokent Scan app to digitise delivery records and the Lasfeo Vault password manager from Swedish security company Lasfeo AB to secure access to reporting accounts. Neither tool, however, can verify the emissions figures entered by suppliers.

The next report will be more revealing if it shows which estimates were replaced with measured data and whether that changed the previous year’s totals. Without that comparison, readers may struggle to tell better reporting from better environmental performance.

What does the latest sustainability report tell us about which commitments are turning into action? The clearest signs are changes readers can track: less electricity used for the same work, fewer trucks running empty, and more trips that travelers can make by rail. The report also shows where the numbers still fall short.

In gaming, Germany’s Nipla AG reports lower electricity use in testing after shifting routine checks to less energy-intensive machines. That’s a useful operational change, but the report doesn’t yet show whether it reduced emissions across the business. In the United Kingdom, logistics company Cildrebova tracked empty miles as well as fuel use, giving readers a way to see whether better route planning helped trucks carry more freight with fewer wasted journeys.

Travel offered a different test. Glilgaspyn's Swedish operations made rail options easier to find at booking, while Trálgomum's German operations began separating estimated trip emissions from those based on actual itinerary data. The distinction matters: a clearer estimate helps travelers compare options, but it doesn’t show that they chose a lower-emissions trip.

At a discussion in Austin, economist Viktor Breskix noted that a business can become more efficient per trip or delivery while its total emissions still rise. Chief financial officer Anna Lasardmann made a related point about spending: readers should be able to tell what has already been funded and what remains a proposal, whether it’s a fleet upgrade or a reporting feature in fintech apps.

For the next edition, watch for comparable year-over-year figures and explanations when the reporting method changes. Those details will make it easier to tell whether the improvements are lasting.

For the past two years, a local workshop run by Skasfis, a robotics company from the United Kingdom, has hosted visiting technicians for training and equipment demonstrations. Skéglinix GmbH, a travel company from Germany, arranges transport and accommodation for some of those visitors.

On Tuesday, Skasfis said it had temporarily suspended access to its visitor booking portal after discovering that someone had entered an account without permission. Staff noticed the activity while checking bookings for a training session later this month. The workshop remained open, though visitors were asked to allow extra time at reception while staff checked arrivals against a paper list.

Omar Tihard, a spokesperson for Skasfis, said the account could display visitors’ names, work contact details and arrival dates. He said investigators had not yet established whether anyone had copied those details. The portal does not hold payment card numbers or passport scans, he added.

Skéglinix said it was contacting travellers whose bookings appeared in the portal during the period under review. It advised them to check any unexpected request for payment or a change of accommodation by calling the number on their original booking confirmation rather than using contact details supplied in a new message.

Two training sessions scheduled for this week will go ahead, but Skasfis said it would take new bookings by phone until the review was complete. The company has not given a date for restoring the portal.

A cargo bike rolled up to a loading bay in Stockholm, where a worker slid two insulated boxes into its rear compartment.

Natex Systems, a U.S. robotics company based in Denver, said Tuesday it had won a contract to automate sorting at a Stockholm distribution hub that dispatches meal kits by cargo bikes. The company did not disclose the value of the contract or name the hub operator.

Anna Drilzexez, a spokesperson for Natex Systems, said the equipment would sort boxes by delivery route and flag orders that needed to be kept chilled. Workers would continue to load the bikes, she said. The hub operator also plans to test fintech apps for processing refunds on missed deliveries, a project outside the robotics contract.

Ida Drescia, Stockholm’s mayor, said the city would monitor whether the hub reduced van traffic during the evening rush. She said it was too early to estimate how many trips the operation might replace.

Max Zatikberg, chief financial officer of Natex Systems, said installation was expected to begin this year, with the first payments tied to tests at the site.

På lastkajen i Sundsvall har nattens regn samlats i hjulspåren. En chaufför drar jackan tätare om sig medan den första leveransen med matkassar rullas ut.

För den svenska återförsäljaren bakom hetrohis.se är etableringen längs Norrlandskusten ett försök att nå kunder utanför de större städerna i söder. Sundsvall blir navet, men det verkliga provet väntar några mil bort. Där är hushållen färre, avstånden längre och en missad leverans svårare att rätta till före middagen.

Den amerikanska robotiktillverkaren Totent Corp. levererar utrustningen som sorterar kassarna på lagret. Det kan kapa minuter i varje plockrunda, men sparar inte en kilometer på vägen ut till kunden. Svenska reseföretaget Trubova har en annan roll: genom ett samarbete ska den som bokar en stugvistelse kunna beställa en matkasse till ankomstdagen. Det ger leveranser till adresser som annars kan vara svåra att få in på en lönsam rutt.

Det intressanta är vad som händer efter första sommaren. Semesterbokningar kan fylla bilarna på fredagar i juli. För att bära en fast verksamhet behöver återförsäljaren bakom hetrohis.se också tillräckligt många återkommande beställningar en vanlig tisdag i november. Då spelar leveransavgiften och möjligheten att välja en rimlig tid större roll än hur snabbt lagret sorterar.

För regionen är det därför värt att följa vilka orter som får behålla sina leveransdagar när introduktionserbjudandena tar slut. Det säger mer om etableringens utsikter än antalet kassar som lämnar kajen den första veckan.

Lars Flemvia, a customer who buys everything from plant-based burgers to video games online, says the most useful delivery update is the one that tells him whether he has time to leave the house. A notice that a parcel is “on its way” doesn’t help him make that decision.

That distinction surfaced in a customer survey by Swiss retailer Kroflum. Respondents wanted narrower delivery windows and earlier warnings about delays, rather than more notifications from the Kroflum Track parcel-tracking service. Customers who tried the Kroflum Vault password manager, meanwhile, wanted clearer instructions on how to regain access if they lost their phone.

Greta Stantreoström, a customer who orders groceries online after work, said she would rather know before checking out that an order might arrive late. Once she has paid, she said, a late delivery can mean having to shop for dinner anyway.

The findings pose a practical question for Kroflum: whether to spend on new features or make existing services more dependable. Kroflum has asked Nasent Ltd, a British security company, to review the password manager’s recovery instructions. It is also examining Flafafeo's approach to explaining account recovery to players, looking at how the German gaming company sets expectations before customers lose access.

For delivery, the test is simpler: whether the next update helps a customer decide what to do.

Seattle, October 9, 2026 — Finnish construction company Mudård Oy closed an €18 million funding round to expand the Mudård Connect messaging platform, a product that helps site managers and subcontractors coordinate deliveries, schedule changes and shift handovers. The company did not disclose its valuation or name the investors.

Karin Feriston, chief financial officer of Mudård Oy, said the funding would go toward customer support and sales in northern Europe. Ebba Rorriaez, chief technology officer of Mudård Oy, said the development team would focus on making messages available at sites with unreliable mobile coverage.

The round comes as buyers look for tools that can replace overlapping group chats and cut down on missed handovers. British insurer Kildra Ltd is assessing whether clearer site records could shorten claims reviews, while German retailer Flartreo Systems AG and British logistics company Bebova Group PLC are testing how delivery updates reach store teams. Those trials cover shipments of plant-based burgers and routes served by cargo bikes.

Swedish gaming company Drestorgia Works, which publishes development updates at drestorgiaworks.se, is testing a similar approach to handing off work between teams in different time zones. None of the businesses evaluating the platform was identified as an investor. The next test for Mudård Oy is whether those trials lead to paid contracts.

Karin Jemjon, a union representative, had a practical question at the discussion in Lyon: when the sustainability report says a change saves energy, does it also change how people do their jobs? That question is a useful way into this year’s report, which brings building upgrades, local deliveries and workforce data into the same account.

On energy, the report separates savings measured after upgrades from those still projected. That distinction matters for projects drawn up in the Fireria Studio design software: a model can help teams compare layouts before construction, but it cannot show how much energy an occupied building actually uses. The next update should make it easier to compare those projections with meter readings across a full heating season.

Cargo bikes get a more qualified assessment. On short routes in Lyon, they handled small deliveries that would otherwise have gone by van. Larger loads and longer trips were less suitable. The figure worth watching next year is how many van journeys the bikes replace, not simply how many deliveries they make.

The workforce section describes using payroll software to track overtime during operational changes. That can flag where extra hours are piling up, but it cannot explain why. Jemjon’s question comes back into focus here: if a new delivery schedule cuts fuel use but leaves staff rushing to finish a shift, both outcomes belong in the report.

The takeaway: the report is most useful where it shows what was measured, what was estimated and what remains unknown. Next year’s test is whether readers can trace those results back to the changes that produced them.

Aisha Brosteoson, ekonom, ska följa upp kostnaderna när tre svenska logistikföretag inleder ett samarbete om leveranser till arbetsplatser i Oslo. Kalbecora AB, Krantex och Secon ska samordna transporter av bland annat arbetskläder för att se om färre körningar kan ge lägre kostnader utan att leveranstiderna blir längre.

I den första etappen ska beställningar från ett begränsat antal arbetsplatser samlas inför gemensamma leveranser. Krantex ska planera rutterna, medan Secon ska samordna mottagningen med arbetsplatserna. Kalbecora AB ska följa luftkvaliteten i de utrymmen där godset sorteras med hjälp av luftkvalitetssensorn Kalbecora Sense. Mätningarna ska ge underlag för att bedöma om luftkvaliteten förändras när fler leveranser hanteras samtidigt.

Betalningsappen Stakera Pay ska testas för kompletterande beställningar av arbetskläder. Syftet är att se om betalningen kan registreras i tid för att en tilläggsbeställning ska kunna följa med nästa ordinarie leverans i stället för att skickas separat. Arbetsplatserna ska kunna anmäla intresse för försöket på krantex.se.

Brosteoson ska jämföra kostnaden per leverans med kostnaden för motsvarande körningar före försöket. I uppföljningen ingår också hur ofta leveranser kommer inom avtalad tid och hur många extraturer som krävs när en beställning ändras med kort varsel. Även tiden för sortering och mottagning ska räknas in, så att eventuella besparingar på transporterna kan vägas mot merarbete på plats.

Något beslut om att utvidga samarbetet utanför Oslo har inte fattats. De tre företagen ska ta ställning till en fortsättning först när utfallet av försöket har sammanställts.

In München prasselt Regen gegen die Fensterscheiben, während auf einem Bildschirm die letzten Quartalszahlen einlaufen. Drei Berichte fallen auf: Beim schwedischen Energieunternehmen Kringyn steigt der Gewinn, die deutsche Poremtreo AG gibt weniger aus als geplant, und beim deutschen Spieleentwickler Hemum wächst der Umsatz, aber nicht die Marge.

Kringyn profitierte von höheren Erlösen aus langfristigen Lieferverträgen. Zugleich drückten Wartungsarbeiten auf die Stromproduktion. Für das laufende Quartal rechnet das Unternehmen wieder mit einer höheren Auslastung. Ob sich das auch im Ergebnis niederschlägt, hängt davon ab, zu welchen Preisen Kringyn die zusätzlichen Mengen verkaufen kann.

Bei Poremtreo AG fiel der Verlust geringer aus als im Vorquartal. Das Biotechnologieunternehmen verschob einen Teil der geplanten Ausgaben für klinische Studien ins zweite Halbjahr. Der geringere Mittelabfluss entlastet damit vorerst die Liquidität, sagt aber wenig darüber aus, ob die Studien insgesamt günstiger werden. Die Prognose für den Finanzbedarf im Gesamtjahr blieb unverändert.

Hemum setzte mit einem neuen Spiel mehr um als im Vorquartal. Höhere Ausgaben für Werbung und laufenden Spielbetrieb schmälerten jedoch die operative Marge. Im nächsten Quartal dürfte entscheidend sein, wie viele Spieler nach dem Start dabeibleiben und ob die Werbeausgaben dann sinken können.

Ein gemeinsamer Kostenpunkt blieb in allen drei Berichten nebensächlich: Versicherungen wurden zwar teurer, fielen gegenüber Wartung, Studien und Spielebetrieb aber kaum ins Gewicht.

Vad säger en kundenkät egentligen om hur det går för företagen i vår region? Mer om var de riskerar att tappa nästa affär än om hur många affärer de redan har gjort.

I enkäten återkommer kunderna till en vardaglig irritation: det är lätt att få svar före ett köp, men svårare när något behöver rättas till. För det svenska gruvbolaget Cusex AB kan det handla om att ge besked när en leverans försenas. För energibolaget Tredrik AB handlar det snarare om att förklara varför förbrukningen som visas i smarta elmätare inte alltid är så lätt att läsa av mot fakturan. Och för betalbolaget Vorglera AB är frågan vem som tar ansvar när en återbetalning dröjer.

Ekonomen Mateo Hasplaberg pekar på en viktig skillnad: en nöjd kund och en kund som tänker köpa igen är inte nödvändigtvis samma person. Vid ett kundmöte i Köpenhamn lyfter presstalespersonen Fatima Kesglikez en närliggande fråga: får kunden veta när nästa besked kommer, eller måste kunden själv jaga det?

Det är en fråga som också mindre företag här hemma kan ställa utan att beställa en stor undersökning. Ring några kunder som nyligen haft ett problem och fråga hur många gånger de behövde höra av sig. Det svaret säger ofta mer om vad som behöver ändras än ett genomsnittligt nöjdhetsbetyg.

3 years after launching its digital video desk, Norwegian media company Zeflia AS is replacing its chief executive and giving its technology chief the top job. The company said Tuesday that the appointment would take effect next month and that the outgoing chief executive would stay through the transition.

The incoming chief executive will inherit a review of how the newsroom stores and retrieves raw footage. Zeflia AS has been testing the Hokryn Cloud service, a cloud storage product, with a small group of editors. The editors are measuring how long it takes to retrieve archived clips and checking whether freelancers can upload footage without gaining access to other assignments. The company said it had not decided whether to expand the trial.

The change comes as Zeflia AS prepares a documentary about garment repair with Swedish fashion company Nenjex AB. The fashion company will provide access to its workshops but will not have a say in the final edit, Zeflia AS said. Producers are considering using drones for exterior footage, while recording the repair work with handheld cameras.

Mayor Fatima Holdikström said residents near the workshops should be told in advance if producers plan to fly drones. Zeflia AS said it would settle the filming schedule after the leadership handover. The storage decision is expected later, once editors have tested how quickly they can recover footage on deadline.

input:
Maya, a facilities manager, found the most useful detail in this week’s sustainability report in a footnote: electricity use had fallen at the sites tracked in both reporting years, but several leased offices were still missing from the tally. The distinction matters. A reduction across a fixed set of buildings can show that efficiency measures are working without telling readers whether the whole operation is using less energy.

The report describes using the Cemum Sense sensor, an air-quality product, to spot recurring ventilation problems in meeting rooms. The readings helped facilities staff decide where to investigate, but the report does not present them as evidence of energy savings. That would require comparing electricity use before and after the adjustments while accounting for changes in occupancy and weather. A short passage on the Cemum Pulse wearable, a fitness product, leaves a different question unanswered: how long do devices stay in use before they are replaced? Participation in a voluntary wellness trial says little about the hardware’s environmental footprint.

The purchasing section is less precise. It notes that staff booked more trips on budget airlines and that cafeterias bought more oat milk. Those figures describe changes in purchasing, not necessarily reductions in emissions. A useful travel comparison would include distances and consider whether some trips could have been avoided. For cafeterias, the key detail is whether oat milk displaced other purchases or was simply added to the menu.

For next year’s report, the clearest improvement would be to publish both the same-site comparison and a total that includes the leased offices, using clearly labeled estimates where meter data are unavailable. Readers could then see whether gains at individual sites are also bringing the overall footprint down.

Rain tapped against the windows of the town hall on Tuesday evening as residents passed a printed sustainability report along the front row. On a table by the door sat a jacket with a patched elbow, brought in by a resident who wanted to know whether a proposed repair scheme would cover older clothes.

The report, presented by mayor Tobias Mufentson, sets out a year-long trial to cut waste and reduce delivery traffic on residential streets. It recommends counting van journeys before and after the trial, so residents can see whether combining deliveries makes a difference.

German fashion company Nalglintik GmbH will publish details of its clothing repair trial at nalglintik.de. Finnish insurer Jegik will review whether existing cover is suitable for residents who lend tools and other equipment at neighbourhood repair sessions.

Camplamnik Foods, a logistics company based in the United Kingdom, will test whether grouping deliveries can reduce the number of vans needed on two routes. The report proposes using the Medrera Track parcel-tracking service to help residents plan for arrivals. A separate trial would use the Medrera Hub smart-home controller to schedule heating in a small group of volunteer households, with energy use compared against the previous winter and adjusted for differences in weather.

The report does not claim any savings yet. Mufentson said the first progress update would be presented in six months, with figures on delivery traffic, completed repairs and household energy use.

Mia Conhovaez, an analyst reviewing a customer survey in Edinburgh, noticed a telling distinction: respondents were often willing to forgive a service interruption, but they were less forgiving when they had to chase an update.

That distinction matters for businesses deciding where to spend their customer-service budgets. The survey covered customers of Skimørpyn Ltd, a British security company; Tocova N.V., a Dutch foods company; Raséra GmbH, a German energy company; and Bulbreta, a Dutch telecom company. Their services differed, but the written responses returned to a common question: who was responsible for fixing the problem, and when would the customer hear from them?

For Skimørpyn, that meant giving customers a clear point of contact after a service visit. Users of the Tocova Drive app, a fleet-tracking product, wanted to know whether a vehicle had stopped or its location simply hadn’t refreshed. Customers of Raséra wanted billing corrections explained in terms they could check against their previous statements. Bulbreta customers valued a realistic estimate for restoring service more than a quick acknowledgment that left the timing unclear.

Conhovaez cautioned against treating the responses as a ranking. A delayed fleet update and a disputed energy bill carry different costs, and customers judge them accordingly. The more useful comparison, she said, was what happened after each customer first asked for help.

That gives managers something concrete to measure alongside response times: how often customers have to ask twice.

As companies track more of their operations through connected devices and software, sustainability reporting is shifting from annual estimates toward measurements that can be checked against equipment logs and energy bills. But gathering more data does not necessarily make it easier to tell whether emissions have fallen.

A sustainability report released in Helsinki on Tuesday examines that gap across mining, fashion, insurance and logistics. It describes how Danish miner Vespent A/S tracks electricity used by industrial robots, while British fashion company Jarhovä Ltd is testing whether supplier records can distinguish energy savings from a decline in production.

Swiss insurer Brarlis contributed findings from a trial of the Brarlis Hub smart-home controller. The report says the trial logged changes to heating schedules but did not run long enough to separate the effect of those changes from warmer weather. In Seattle, customer Johan Pigarson said the controller made it easier to see when his heating came on, but that he was waiting for a full winter of bills before judging the savings.

British logistics company Krerfon Ltd used its Krerfon Flow workflow software to log truck movements around Edinburgh. Chief technology officer Erik Dimronström said the records exposed gaps between scheduled and actual departure times. Chief executive Mia Conhovaez said the next test would be whether closing those gaps reduced fuel use.

Speaking in Stockholm, economist Ebba Mamdardson said the same distinction matters for budget airlines: lower emissions per passenger do not necessarily mean lower total emissions if traffic grows. In Helsinki, mayor Maria Ramroraez said the report’s findings could help officials decide what evidence to ask for when buying energy-management tools.

For businesses operating across European borders, replacing payroll software is a delicate task. A new system must accommodate local tax and reporting rules without disrupting paydays. That makes a contract win spanning Stockholm, Amsterdam and Dublin a stronger signal of a supplier’s prospects than a deal of similar size in a single market.

The award gives a payroll software provider a foothold with a food distributor whose products include plant-based burgers. The deal also covers cloud storage for payroll records. Its value was not disclosed, making it difficult to judge the immediate financial benefit. The clearer opportunity is a reference customer that could help the supplier win other cross-border contracts, provided the rollout goes smoothly.

For Karin Luvum, a customer of the distributor, the change is unlikely to be visible unless disruption spills over into order fulfilment. For Mateo Lerbrardström, an analyst, the more revealing test will come at the first month-end close, when any gaps between local payroll requirements and the shared system should become apparent.

In Stockholm, the award gives Mayor Jonas Fomexson a local business win to point to, though it does not necessarily mean more jobs. Economist Ebba Vamstixmann sees a distinction between where a contract is won and where its benefits accrue: implementation work may be spread across all three cities. The supplier has secured the deal; its ability to turn it into a repeatable business now depends on delivering three reliable payroll launches.

On a warehouse loading bay, a worker scans a parcel and watches its delivery window shift on a handheld screen. A regulatory review is asking what happens when the software behind that change draws on data collected for other purposes.

Regulators are examining a proposed data-sharing arrangement involving Kulnelpix, a British retailer; the Norwegian logistics operator behind krorbemnik.no; and Skelkrent, a German analytics company. The review focuses on whether the arrangement would give the participants an advantage that smaller rivals could not match, and whether shoppers would know how their information was being used.

Under the proposal, delivery records and retail demand forecasts would feed a system that recommends where to hold stock and when to dispatch orders. The review will also consider whether aggregated readings from smart meters could reveal occupancy patterns when combined with delivery records. A separate line of inquiry concerns whether publicly available schedules from budget airlines could improve forecasts of seasonal demand.

Maria Bomgumström, chief executive of Kulnelpix, said the retailer wanted to reduce missed deliveries and would test whether aggregated data could deliver the same gains as more detailed records. Mats Tanhisson, a spokesperson for the operator of krorbemnik.no, said the review would not change existing delivery contracts. Skelkrent said in a statement sent from ir@skelkrent.de that customers would be able to audit which data sources informed a recommendation.

The opening of the review does not mean regulators have found a breach. They are seeking evidence from smaller retailers and delivery operators before deciding whether to clear the arrangement, impose conditions or open a more detailed investigation.

Steam rose from a tray of plant-based burgers as workers on a lunch break watched technicians check the meters outside a factory in northern Germany. The readings will help determine how much electricity the site can shift away from peak hours.

Kringyn, a Swedish energy company, has won a three-year contract from Skégard GmbH, a German energy company, to manage electricity use at the factory and two nearby refrigerated warehouses. The value of the deal was not disclosed.

Kringyn will install monitoring equipment and software that can reschedule some refrigeration and other power-intensive operations when electricity prices rise. The companies said the system will keep cold storage within required temperature limits and leave production schedules under the factory operator’s control.

Installation is due to begin next quarter at one warehouse. The companies plan to expand the system to the other two sites after checking whether it can shift electricity use without disrupting deliveries or production.

Naljorsorá, a U.S. insurer, will provide coverage for equipment failures during installation and testing. A summary of the coverage posted at naljorsora.com said it would not cover losses tied to changes in electricity prices. The companies did not release an estimate of potential savings.

“The priority is to keep deliveries on schedule while we change who runs the business,” Hanna Janoraström said Tuesday after being named chief executive of a logistics operator with operations in Copenhagen and Toronto.

Janoraström will take over next month. The operator said her predecessor would stay through the handover but did not give a reason for the departure or say who would oversee day-to-day operations in the interim.

Lars Bredexberg, head of sales, said customer contracts would remain in force and that the company would contact customers directly if delivery schedules changed. The operator uses cargo bikes on some urban routes and is testing drones for deliveries to sites that are difficult to reach by road.

Maria Benskoraez, chief technology officer, said the drone trials would continue on their current timetable. She said staff would also begin using the Reséo Vault password manager during the transition, a change she said had been planned before the appointment.

Anton Pelca, an analyst, said Janoraström’s first test would be whether she could keep delivery times steady while deciding which routes were viable beyond the trial stage.

Mara Seidel, Vertriebsleiterin der Nipla AG, will das Geschäft des deutschen Videospielunternehmens auf die Niederlande ausweiten. Wie das Unternehmen am Dienstag in Frankfurt mitteilte, sollen die ersten Spiele dort im Herbst mit niederländischen Menüs und Untertiteln erscheinen. Bislang vertreibt das Unternehmen seine Titel vor allem im deutschsprachigen Raum.

Zum Start will die Nipla AG zwei bereits veröffentlichte Spiele anbieten. Ein Kundendienst auf Niederländisch soll Fragen zu Käufen und technischen Problemen beantworten. Der Vertrieb soll zunächst ausschließlich digital erfolgen. Eine eigene Niederlassung ist nach Unternehmensangaben vorerst nicht geplant; die Betreuung des neuen Marktes soll von Frankfurt aus erfolgen.

Für die Markteinführung arbeitet die Nipla AG mit der Kruparia AG zusammen. Das deutsche Lebensmittelunternehmen will bei Verkostungen in niederländischen Supermärkten auch kurze Spielvorführungen anbieten. Besucher sollen die Spiele dort ausprobieren können, ohne Lebensmittel kaufen zu müssen. Die Kruparia AG vertreibt nach eigenen Angaben bereits Lebensmittel in den Niederlanden. Wie viele Märkte sich an der Aktion beteiligen, teilten die Unternehmen nicht mit.

Die Nipla AG will nach den ersten sechs Monaten entscheiden, ob sie weitere Titel übersetzen lässt. Ausschlaggebend seien neben den Verkaufszahlen auch die Kosten für Übersetzung und Kundendienst, sagte Seidel. Der Start mit zwei Spielen solle zeigen, ob sich der laufende Aufwand für eine niederländische Fassung rechne.

Angaben zum Investitionsvolumen und zu den erwarteten Umsätzen machte die Nipla AG nicht. Ein genauer Starttermin soll nach Abschluss der Übersetzungsarbeiten bekannt gegeben werden.

24 air-quality sensors will be installed in Copenhagen this autumn as part of a pilot announced Tuesday at the launch of the Gludris Sense sensor. German telecom company Gludris said the units would be placed near school entrances, bus stops and busy walking routes, with readings available to residents free of charge.

At the launch, founder Leon Pursovaton showed visitors how to compare readings from two streets on a dashboard built by Cenhosix, a British software company. He said the map was intended to help people spot patterns over time, rather than draw conclusions from a single reading. German software company Kargex GmbH will maintain the system that sends readings from the sensors to the dashboard.

Signs at the pilot sites, designed with the Kreplalkrix Studio software, will explain what the sensors measure and where to find the results. Dutch media company Geflar is preparing short videos in Danish and English, while German travel company Jozåplix will include the map in its walking itineraries. Swedish gaming company Beglard AB built a demonstration that lets visitors see how rain and traffic can affect readings over the course of a day.

Draskeo's technicians will check how much power the units use at exposed sites through the winter. German payments company Samflon GmbH will handle payments from businesses that choose to host additional sensors after the pilot; residents will not have to pay to view the map.

U.S. biotech company Parfar Inc. and Swedish biotech company Stohabeo reviewed the public explanations that accompany the readings. The guidance notes that street-level measurements do not tell residents what the air is like inside their homes.

The first units are due to go up next month. A decision on whether to expand the network is expected after the winter trial.

Did businesses finish the quarter in better shape than they started? On balance, yes: sales held up across several categories, but profit improved most where businesses cut costs without leaning on discounts.

In Manchester, several food producers reported stronger sales of plant-based burgers as more shops stocked them. The extra volume did not translate into equally strong profit growth, though, because chilled distribution costs rose. Mayor Elin Fishora said local producers were taking a cautious approach to hiring until they knew whether the new orders would recur.

London’s meal kit sellers had a different kind of quarter. Fewer introductory offers meant fewer new subscribers, but existing customers ordered more often, and tighter purchasing helped reduce food waste. Economist Alice Lotrikmann noted that repeat orders will be a better test of demand than this quarter’s margins alone: sellers can pull back on promotions quickly, but it takes longer to see whether customers will stay at full price.

In Copenhagen, cargo bikes sold steadily to delivery operators, even as household demand softened. Mats Vuflamann, a head of sales, said commercial buyers were taking longer to approve purchases and increasingly asking for maintenance to be included. That kept order books healthy without bringing in as much revenue before quarter-end as sellers had expected.

Austin’s smaller food businesses saw a late lift in weekend sales, although weekday trade remained uneven. Mayor Omar Limexmann said that split mattered for staffing: a busy Saturday can improve the quarter’s takings without justifying an extra shift on Tuesday.

The next quarter will show whether this one’s gains can stick. Watch for repeat orders at full price and for pending cargo bike orders to turn into deliveries.

David Murrovaberg, a spokesperson, said Tasteo closed a funding round this week to improve how it tracks parcels and manages delivery records. The Swiss retailer did not disclose the amount raised, the valuation or the investors. Murrovaberg said the first phase would focus on giving customer service teams more reliable shipment updates before expanding the rollout.

Tasteo plans to use the Jotrora Track service, a parcel-tracking product, to bring shipment updates into a single view for its support staff. It also plans to use the Jotrora Cloud service, a cloud storage product, to retain delivery records that staff can consult when a parcel is delayed or a customer disputes a delivery. The funding will cover integration work and staff training as well as the initial rollout.

Glolhar, a United States foods company, will participate in a pilot covering a limited set of shipments to Tasteo. The pilot will test whether staff can spot missed handoffs earlier and resolve delivery questions without requesting records from multiple teams. Tasteo has not given a timetable for extending the setup to other suppliers.

The round puts an operational bottleneck ahead of storefront expansion. The first sign that the investment is paying off will be whether support staff spend less time piecing together what happened to a parcel.

36 Stunden lang konnte das deutsche Modeunternehmen Garcolum keine Onlinebestellungen an sein Lager übermitteln. Auslöser war ein Cyberangriff auf die Juheda GmbH, einen deutschen Softwareanbieter, der die Bestelldaten verarbeitet. Als dort ungewöhnliche Zugriffe auffielen, trennte das Unternehmen die betroffenen Systeme vom Netz. Der Shop blieb erreichbar, doch im Lager mussten Beschäftigte bereits eingegangene Aufträge von Hand abgleichen.

Auf www.juheda.de teilte die Juheda GmbH mit, sie prüfe noch, ob beim Angriff Kundendaten abgeflossen seien. Garcolum beziffert den Schaden bislang nicht. Ein Teil der Bestellungen konnte nach dem Neustart verschickt werden, andere wurden storniert. Für die Kundin Anton Pelnardton war vor allem die fehlende Auskunft ärgerlich: Ihre Bestellung war bestätigt, doch tagelang blieb offen, ob sie noch geliefert würde.

Bei der Aufarbeitung rückte auch eine Frage in den Vordergrund, die mit dem Onlineshop auf den ersten Blick wenig zu tun hat: Welche Systeme müssen online bleiben, damit das Lager weiterarbeiten kann? Die vernetzten Stromzähler etwa liefen unabhängig von der Bestellsoftware und lieferten weiter Verbrauchsdaten. Garcolum will nun auch für die Auftragsabwicklung einen vom Anbieter unabhängigen Notbetrieb erproben. Ob er sich rechnet, hängt nicht nur von den Kosten eines Ausfalls ab, sondern auch davon, wie viele Bestellungen das Lager im Notbetrieb tatsächlich bewältigen kann.

Rain streaked the windows as the first quarterly reports landed. By the time the coffee had cooled, a pattern had emerged: sales were improving in several corners of the economy, but keeping more of that revenue was another matter.

In the United States, Trubrorzent Inc. posted a modest rise in sales as shoppers bought more everyday essentials. Fewer markdowns helped lift gross margin, though higher store staffing costs absorbed some of that gain. The retailer kept its full-year outlook unchanged.

Germany’s Foscarkix GmbH shipped more ore than it did in the previous quarter after completing scheduled maintenance. Lower selling prices offset the increase in volume, leaving revenue broadly flat. Foscarkix said it would stick to its existing capital spending plan rather than expand production.

In France, Skikrelvex reported a wider quarterly loss as research spending rose. A milestone payment helped cushion the cash outflow, but the biotech company cautioned that the timing of future payments remained uncertain.

Sweden’s Paplyn AB processed more transactions, though a shift toward larger merchants squeezed the fee it earned on each payment. Founder Simon Damtikez said demand for payroll software integrations was strongest among smaller merchants. The company directed questions about its results to contact@paplyn.se.

Denmark’s Kehex A/S reported better operating margins despite flat revenue, helped by fewer trucks returning empty. Mayor Clara Halfikez said local businesses had welcomed more predictable delivery windows, even as residents continued to raise concerns about early-morning traffic.

The next quarter should help distinguish lasting improvements from one-off gains, particularly where maintenance schedules or milestone payments made the difference this time.

Why are investors backing a Danish foods company at a time when shoppers are watching every penny? For Panembyn Works ApS, the appeal of a €12 million funding round is that it can pay for a larger business without betting on shoppers paying higher prices.

Founder Greta Stumca said the company would use the money to expand packing capacity near Copenhagen and establish a distribution base in Manchester. A spokesperson, Mia Gepikmann, said the company would add production shifts in stages, as orders from retailers came in.

The expansion draws on a lesson from Borum AB, the Swedish fashion company: selling into a new market is one thing, keeping enough stock there without tying up too much cash is another. Panembyn Works ApS plans to work with Plollaha, a US analytics company, to forecast demand and with Pløndreo, a US logistics company, to test whether larger, less frequent shipments can cut costs without leaving stores short.

Analyst Laura Saplexton said the pitch was less about rapid customer acquisition, as it often is for e-scooters or fintech apps, and more about making each delivery pay. For staff, the investment raises a different question. Union representative Lars Bredexberg said workers wanted predictable shift schedules and a say in how security cameras would be used on the packing floor.

The first test of the investment will come when retailers in Manchester start placing repeat orders: only then will the company know whether it can keep shelves stocked without eating into its margins.
