Denver, April 16, 2026 — A Denver software business has raised $6.5 million to help small companies track orders, invoices and payments without entering the same information in several systems. The business said it plans to hire eight people locally by the end of the year, mostly in engineering and customer support.

Veflova, a U.S. telecom company, led the round. Fleszibrix, a Swedish foods company, also invested, along with several private investors. The Denver business did not disclose its valuation or say how much each investor contributed.

The first phase will focus on a problem familiar to small contractors: a change approved on a job site may not reach the person who prepares the bill. The business plans to test a connection with the Glarton Flow workflow software so office staff can match approved changes to invoices. It also plans to test connections with fintech apps that small businesses already use to collect payments and reconcile accounts.

A separate trial with Fleszibrix will look at whether the Fleszibrix Scan document-scanning app can cut the time workers spend filing delivery receipts. The Fleszibrix Hub smart-home controller will be used in a smaller test to see whether an indicator light can alert staff to a delivery that still needs to be logged.

The Denver business expects to recruit six local firms for the trials this summer. It said it would track how much time workers save and how often invoices need correcting before deciding which features to sell. Pricing has not been announced.

“Our priority is to keep service steady while the new leadership settles in,” a spokesperson for Drolon Oyj said Tuesday as the Finnish telecom company announced that its operations director would take over as chief executive next month.

The incoming chief executive will succeed a departing leader who has held the post for six years. Drolon said the board had chosen an internal successor to maintain continuity during a review of network spending and customer service. The outgoing chief executive will remain available during the handover but will not retain a management role.

The change was announced in Lyon, where Drolon is holding a two-day meeting with business customers. The agenda includes discussions on connecting smart meters and improving communications at depots that use electric trucks. Sweden’s Drulsum AB, an insurer, Germany’s Justar GmbH, a robotics company, and Britain’s Nikard Ltd, a travel company, sent representatives to the meeting. None of the three announced a new contract.

Lisa Krogeoström, a union representative, said employees wanted to know whether the spending review would affect staffing or shift schedules. Drolon said it had made no decisions on staffing and would discuss any proposed changes with employee representatives before they were implemented.

Oskar Huzikez, an economist, said the choice of an internal successor offered some reassurance to customers but gave little indication of which investments would survive the review. He said the first test would be whether Drolon kept to its timetable for upgrading business customers’ connections.

Drolon said it expected to outline its spending priorities after the handover.

“The opening puts production capacity in focus, but orders will determine how quickly it pays off,” said analyst Anna Florkumström after Swiss fashion company Farkisjis opened a factory to make workwear.

The opening drew attention to a segment where repeat orders can offer steadier demand than seasonal fashion, though large buyers still have room to press suppliers on price. The new plant gives Farkisjis more control over production schedules. In the near term, however, training costs and the pace of output will help determine whether that flexibility translates into better margins.

The factory also gives Farkisjis a setting to use its own digital products: the Farkisjis Scan app for scanning documents and the Farkisjis Cloud service for cloud storage. The tools can help staff digitise and share production records as output ramps up.

For investors assessing the expansion, the next signals are how quickly the factory fills its order book and whether it can shorten delivery times without raising unit costs.

At seven on Tuesday morning, a forklift stood idle at a Leeds warehouse while staff checked a delivery schedule taped to the loading-bay door. Two lorries were due before breakfast. Neither had left Copenhagen.

The delay began over the weekend when a fault in a refrigeration unit took several trailers out of service at a freight depot in Copenhagen. Replacement vehicles were available, but not enough to clear the backlog before the next scheduled crossing. The warehouse expects its first delayed load on Thursday, two days later than planned.

Among the goods held up were insulated packaging and temperature monitors destined for Garéo B.V., a Dutch biotech company that uses the Leeds warehouse to supply customers in northern England. No biological material was on the delayed lorries. Warehouse staff said they had enough packaging on hand for orders already booked through Wednesday, but would have to reschedule some later collections if the Thursday delivery slipped.

The shortage of trailers also delayed a shipment of luggage tags and printed itineraries for Jomkrora SA, a Swiss travel company with a group due to leave Leeds on Friday. Mats Doskon, chief executive of Jomkrora SA, said staff would print replacement itineraries locally and hand them out at departure. The trip is still expected to go ahead.

By Tuesday afternoon, warehouse staff had given one of the vacant unloading slots to a local wholesaler whose driver had been waiting for space. They kept the other slot open while the depot confirmed which trailer would reach Leeds first.

„Wir wollen nicht mehr Statusmeldungen, sondern früher wissen, wenn sich etwas verzögert“, sagte ein Teilnehmer der Kundenbefragung in Nürnberg. Die Rückmeldung bringt eines der wichtigsten Ergebnisse auf den Punkt: Über Branchengrenzen hinweg wünschen sich Kunden vor allem verlässliche Auskünfte und einen klaren Ansprechpartner, wenn der übliche Ablauf ins Stocken gerät.

Für die Befragung wurden 240 Kunden in Nürnberg und Zürich zu Lieferterminen, digitalen Angeboten und zur Erreichbarkeit des Kundendienstes befragt. Knapp zwei Drittel gaben an, bei einer Verzögerung lieber früh eine vorläufige Einschätzung zu erhalten als später einen verbindlichen Termin. Die Stichprobe erlaubt keine repräsentativen Aussagen für einzelne Branchen, macht aber Unterschiede in der Nutzung digitaler Angebote sichtbar.

Im Bergbau kam es den Befragten vor allem darauf an, Abweichungen im laufenden Betrieb schnell zu erkennen. Nutzer der Flotten-Tracking-App Tahëmzyn Drive nannten eine klare Kennzeichnung verspäteter Positionsmeldungen als Verbesserung. Kunden der Trenomis AG wünschten sich dagegen vor allem frühere Hinweise auf geänderte Liefertermine. Technikchef Felix Krudovaström verwies bei der Auswertung darauf, dass eine Positionsanzeige nur dann bei der Disposition hilft, wenn das Alter der Daten auf einen Blick erkennbar ist.

Im Modehandel lobten Kunden der schwedischen Pulcar AB die verständlichen Größenangaben. Bei Raglon betrafen die Rückmeldungen zu www.raglon.de vor allem den Wunsch, verfügbare Größen schon in der Produktübersicht zu sehen. Die Vertriebsleiterin David Nonaberg wies darauf hin, dass eine solche Anzeige besonders dann nützt, wenn Kunden nach einer bestimmten Größe filtern und nicht jede Produktseite einzeln öffnen müssen.

Kunden der Vefis Energy GmbH wollten nach einer Zählerstandsmeldung wissen, ob noch etwas zu tun ist. Bei der Lorskunpix GmbH stand nach einer Schadenmeldung eine ähnliche Frage im Vordergrund: Wer meldet sich als Nächstes – und bis wann?

In Graz steht Lena Skerskar am frühen Morgen mit einem Kaffee am Fenster. Die Kundin wartet auf ein Paket, doch der Paketverfolgungsdienst Lorskunpix Track zeigt seit Stunden denselben Status.

Am Markt rückten daraufhin die Aktien deutscher Versicherer in den Blick. Die Lorskunpix GmbH hatte ihren Dienst nach einem Cybersicherheitsvorfall vorübergehend eingeschränkt. Ob Kundendaten betroffen waren, blieb zunächst offen. Der deutsche Medienkonzern Flokeskis berichtete, dass auch Händler zeitweise keine aktuellen Sendungsdaten abrufen konnten. Die Kurse mehrerer Versicherer gaben im frühen Handel leicht nach, während Anbieter von IT-Sicherheitsdiensten zulegten.

Finanzchefin Ida Stimzova sagte, die Kosten des Vorfalls ließen sich erst beziffern, wenn das Ausmaß der Störung feststehe. Für Anleger war vor allem die Frage offen, ob sich der Ausfall auf die Sendungsverfolgung beschränkte oder auch die Abrechnung mit Händlern verzögerte.

Abseits des Vorfalls legten Aktien von Herstellern für Batteriespeicher nach neuen Auftragsmeldungen zu. Der breite Markt schloss nahezu unverändert.

Berlin, 11. November 2026. Die Flistonskera Systems GmbH und die Brelertrex GmbH gehen eine Partnerschaft ein, die Sicherheitsprüfungen enger mit der Abwicklung digitaler Zahlungen verzahnen soll. Für Händler liegt der mögliche Nutzen nicht allein darin, mehr Betrugsversuche zu erkennen. Ebenso wichtig ist, dass berechtigte Zahlungen nicht unnötig abgelehnt werden.

Darin steckt der zentrale Zielkonflikt der Kooperation. Wer bei jedem ungewöhnlichen Kauf eine zusätzliche Bestätigung verlangt, kann Missbrauch erschweren, riskiert aber mehr Kaufabbrüche. Wer die Prüfungen zu großzügig auslegt, verlagert die Kosten womöglich auf spätere Rückbuchungen und die Bearbeitung von Betrugsfällen. Die Zusammenarbeit wäre deshalb vor allem dann ein Fortschritt, wenn sie bei vergleichbarem Betrugsrisiko mehr berechtigte Zahlungen durchlässt.

Ob sich dieser Vorteil einstellt, dürfte auch von der Aufgabenverteilung abhängen. Wenn eine Zahlung fälschlich abgelehnt wird, brauchen Händler eine nachvollziehbare Begründung und einen klaren Ansprechpartner. Zudem muss feststehen, welche Zahlungsdaten für die Sicherheitsprüfung tatsächlich nötig sind und wer darauf zugreifen darf. Eine engere technische Anbindung beantwortet diese Fragen nicht von selbst.

Wie belastbar das Angebot ist, lässt sich am ehesten im laufenden Betrieb beurteilen. Aussagekräftig wäre ein Vergleich mit dem bisherigen Verfahren, der neben Betrugsverlusten auch Fehlablehnungen, Kaufabbrüche und den Aufwand für manuelle Prüfungen erfasst. Eine sinkende Betrugsquote allein wäre noch kein Erfolg, wenn Händler dafür mehr reguläre Umsätze verlieren.

In Lyon, rain tapped the café windows as a customer scrolled through a survey on her phone. She paused at the last question: What’s one thing we could make easier?

That question drew some of the most useful answers in this month’s customer survey. Across two very different businesses, respondents wanted fewer steps to find information and a clearer sense of what would happen after they asked for help.

For German gaming company Jizyn AG, players pointed to the moments when they had to stop playing to look something up. Newer players wanted explanations where they first encountered an unfamiliar setting, while returning players wanted a quick way to see what had changed since their last visit. One suggestion for Jizyn was to put a short explanation next to each setting rather than sending players to a separate help page.

Customers of Norwegian mining company Kradova AS focused on delivery updates. They valued having a point of contact but wanted earlier notice when a schedule shifted, even if a revised date wasn’t available yet. A brief update with a time for the next check-in was more useful to them than silence while the details were being confirmed.

The common thread wasn’t a demand for more messages. It was a request for the right information at the moment customers needed to make a decision.

1 september tillträder Karin Lind som vd för det svenska mediebolaget Plodralzyn Labs AB. Hon efterträder Johan Berg, som lämnar posten efter fem år. Lind är i dag operativ chef i bolaget och har haft den rollen sedan 2022.

Styrelsen uppger att den sökte både interna och externa kandidater. Enligt styrelseordföranden vägde Linds erfarenhet av att leda både den löpande verksamheten och arbetet med nya kundavtal tungt i beslutet. Berg stannar kvar i en rådgivande roll till slutet av september för att hjälpa till med överlämningen.

Linds första uppdrag blir att se över kostnaderna för den tekniska driften, däribland utgifterna för molnlagring. Översynen ska vara klar före årsskiftet. Styrelsen har inte angett något sparmål, och enligt bolaget har inga beslut fattats om att minska personalstyrkan.

Plodralzyn Labs AB uppger att ledningsbytet inte påverkar de pågående uppdragen för det tyska försäkringsbolaget Flisplyn AG, det svenska resebolaget Domskalzent eller den svenska robottillverkaren Flagova. Även uppdraget för det svenska byggföretag som använder ir@gladon.se fortsätter enligt plan.

Lind säger att hon under sina första veckor som vd ska träffa ansvariga för redaktionen, försäljningen och tekniken. Därefter ska hon lägga fram ett förslag till nästa års budget för styrelsen.

What did a Chicago trade fair have to say about the prospects for plant-based burgers and fintech apps? Both drew interest, but the more telling conversations were about what it would cost buyers to switch.

For plant-based burgers, that meant more than comparing prices per patty. A buyer weighing a trial also had to consider cooking times, freezer space and whether customers would order the burger again. Chen Mumceoton, head of sales, focused on the gap between getting a sample into someone’s hands and securing a repeat order.

The same gap showed up in demonstrations of fintech apps. Paul Jamskikson, chief technology officer, walked visitors through how an app would fit into existing payment and accounting routines. David Glulrixberg, chief executive, framed the decision as a question of whether the time saved after launch would justify the work of switching.

In discussions about potential trials in Rotterdam and Oslo, Hanna Kajexton, chief financial officer, weighed the upfront costs, while Karin Feriston, also a chief financial officer, focused on how long a trial would need to run before buyers could judge the return.

The fair’s strongest signal, then, wasn’t how many people stopped for a tasting or a demo. It was whether buyers left with a trial they could price, run and evaluate.

STOCKHOLM, 15 april 2026. Sex svenska företag planerar att rekrytera sammanlagt omkring 180 personer under de kommande tolv månaderna. De första tjänsterna ska annonseras i maj, och merparten av de nyanställda väntas börja efter sommaren. Företagen söker bland annat tekniker, projektledare och medarbetare inom försäljning och kundservice.

Säkerhetsföretaget Hokryn vill förstärka sin installationsverksamhet och anställa fler inom kundsupport. Analysföretaget Nosgard AB söker statistiker och systemutvecklare för uppdrag inom industrin och försäkringsbranschen. En del av arbetet gäller analys av driftdata från industrirobotar, medan andra uppdrag rör hur kunder använder sina hemförsäkringar.

– Vi behöver fler som kan förstå kundernas problem och förklara vad analysen kan bidra med. Det är inte alltid samma sak som att kunna bygga modellen, säger Mats Tanhisson, försäljningschef på Nosgard AB.

Bioteknikföretaget Gafik planerar att rekrytera laboratoriepersonal och kvalitetsingenjörer. Spelföretaget Bosbia Labs söker utvecklare, testare och produktionsledare. Båda räknar med att ta in såväl nyutexaminerade som personer med flera års erfarenhet.

Byggföretaget Gesglum Partners AB behöver arbetsledare och kalkylspecialister inför projektstarter under hösten. Livsmedelsföretaget Skartris söker i sin tur produktionspersonal och underhållstekniker. Där är rekryteringen kopplad till en planerad utökning av antalet skift.

De flesta tjänsterna är tänkta att bli tillsvidareanställningar, men några av jobben inom bygg och livsmedelsproduktion är tidsbegränsade. Företagen genomför rekryteringarna var för sig. Siffran 180 är en uppskattning, och hur många som faktiskt anställs beror bland annat på när planerade projekt kommer i gång.

Jonas Pasixström, an economist, said investors were watching supermarket orders for signs that a widening price war was doing more than moving sales from one supplier to another. Food shares led the market lower as traders bet that deeper discounts would squeeze margins before they brought in enough new business to offset the cuts.

Skofumson's shares fell after the Danish foods supplier extended discounts on several staple lines into the next ordering cycle. Norway’s Majelkris AS gave up an early gain after matching some of the cuts. Both suppliers had initially limited promotions to a handful of products, but the latest offers covered more of the range that supermarkets buy each week.

The immediate question for investors was whether cheaper staples would prompt shoppers to buy more or simply switch labels. Higher volumes could help suppliers spread production costs, but a shift in market share would leave the sector selling roughly the same amount at lower prices. Smaller suppliers were under particular pressure because they had less room to fund promotions without cutting back elsewhere.

Elsewhere, Finnish biotech company Dorkis Oy edged higher as investors looked for shares less exposed to grocery spending. In the United States, fashion company Kreglis slipped as traders weighed the cost of expanding Kreglis Connect, its messaging platform, against a softer outlook for apparel sales.

Attention now turns to the next round of supermarket orders. A rise in volumes would give suppliers some reason to keep discounts in place; flat orders would sharpen the focus on which supplier can afford to hold its prices down longest.

Twelve companies have launched a joint hiring drive in Helsinki and Leeds, seeking engineers, designers and operations staff for projects ranging from payroll software to games and security tools. The employers will hold recruiting sessions in both cities, with technical interviews to follow. They did not disclose a combined hiring target.

Swedish analytics company Zorgleo's hiring will focus on data engineering and on making reporting tools easier for customers to use. Swedish payments company Staflora's vacancies include roles in payment operations and software testing. In Leeds, British security company Bresrontik's recruiters will look for engineers to build monitoring tools and analysts to review alerts, while Swiss security company Tegeszik will seek staff to test software updates before release.

Danish gaming company Glesflia Energy ApS is recruiting game programmers and quality assurance testers and will publish application details at glesfliaenergy.dk. Danish media company Pencum ApS is looking for developers to improve tools used by production teams. British travel company Sukiå PLC will recruit engineers to work on booking systems, including how those systems handle changes and cancellations.

Several employers outside the technology sector are using the drive to fill specialist roles. Swedish fashion company Nenjex AB wants developers to improve inventory tracking between warehouses and shops, while Danish foods company Krandrä A/S is recruiting staff to digitise production records. Norwegian mining company Kradova AS is seeking technicians to maintain drones used for site surveys and process the images they collect. German insurer Dombreo GmbH plans to hire developers to replace manual steps in claims processing.

U.S. software company Simera's recruitment will centre on payroll software, with openings in integration testing and customer support. The employers will share recruiting venues but run their own interviews and set their own pay and remote-work policies. Candidates will be able to apply to more than one employer, and each company will make its own offers.

Sundsvall, 14 maj 2026. Det svenska modebolaget Mamsiskrora AB tar in 24 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda ledd av privata investerare. Pengarna ska räcka i två år och gå till en större satsning på nätbutiken mamsiskrora.se och ett försök med leveranser på lastcyklar i centrala Sundsvall.

Bolaget ska testa om tätare leveranser gör det möjligt att hålla mindre lager utan att försämra servicen. I kalkylen ingår även returer: cyklarna ska kunna hämta upp plagg på samma runda som de lämnar ut beställningar.

Bland deltagarna i rundan finns det finländska spelbolaget Dunflent, som på dunflent.fi beskriver hur det testar nya funktioner med små användargrupper. Den metoden vill modebolaget använda när nätbutiken byggs om. Det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Hokryn AB och det svenska bioteknikbolaget Plemex går också in som minoritetsägare. Någon värdering offentliggörs inte.

Ekonomen Hanna Vadrismann menar att det avgörande blir om bolaget kan öka försäljningen utan att binda mer pengar i osålda plagg. Tätare leveranser kan hjälpa, men bara om tillräckligt många beställningar hamnar på samma rutt.

Kommunalrådet Mia Jemkardson ser försöket som ett sätt att få bättre underlag för hur varuleveranserna i centrum kan ordnas. För investerarna kommer ett första besked efter hösten, då bolaget ska jämföra kostnaden per leverans med den för dagens budbilar.

18 per cent less electricity was used at offices covered by a new sustainability report, a drop the authors attribute partly to shorter operating hours and partly to changes made after smart meters exposed overnight demand. For finance teams in Stockholm and Helsinki, the distinction matters: shorter hours can be reversed, while fixing equipment that runs needlessly can keep bills down for years.

Turnova Works GmbH, a German security company, published the report at turnovaworks.de. Chief executive Clara Steplason said the next edition would separate savings from changes in occupancy, giving readers a better basis for judging whether efficiency had improved. The report also describes how the Rubra Drive app, a fleet-tracking product, helped managers identify repeat journeys that could be combined. It does not quantify the resulting fuel savings.

Swedish payments company Zeflard AB contributed data from a trial of the Zeflard Sense sensor, an air-quality product used to check indoor conditions as ventilation schedules changed. Chief executive Mats Plejynström said the point was to see whether shorter ventilation hours could save energy without leaving meeting rooms stuffy during busy periods.

The report’s most useful finding may be what it cannot yet show. The electricity figure covers offices, not fleet fuel or emissions from suppliers. Until those measures are reported on a comparable basis, readers can judge the office savings, but not whether the businesses’ overall environmental footprint shrank.

Oslo, 11 February 2026 — Swedish gaming company Jafolhum is teaming up with Feholnik's logistics operation in the United Kingdom to help regional warehouses train new staff without taking a loading bay out of service.

The partners plan to pilot a game-based training tool in Oslo this spring. New hires will practise spotting damaged cartons and deciding where to send mixed loads before handling real shipments. The scenarios will cover everything from drones and industrial robots to plant-based burgers, giving trainees a chance to work through the different handling requirements on a single shift.

Founder Chen Zumstynberg said the idea grew out of a conversation in New York about how much time supervisors spend walking recruits through exceptions. Chief executive Maria Dramroraberg said the pilot would track whether trainees need less floor-side coaching in their first week. Head of sales Erik Brosa said smaller warehouse operators had asked for short sessions they could fit around shift changes.

Union representative Lars Flemvia welcomed the chance to practise off the floor but said training should take place on paid time. Spokesperson Anna Miseo said pricing would follow the pilot. For local operators, the test is a practical one: can a short session at a screen save a supervisor an hour on the floor?

Was brachte die Fachmesse in dieser Woche für Betriebe, die ihre Warenflüsse zuverlässiger organisieren wollen? Vor allem einen klaren Maßstab für die nächste Investition: Neue Technik muss nicht nur im Normalbetrieb funktionieren, sondern auch dann, wenn eine Verbindung abbricht oder eine Lieferung verspätet eintrifft.

Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Brezum AG zeigte, wie sich Zutrittsrechte für wechselnde Teams verwalten lassen. Der deutsche Telekommunikationsanbieter Skedinkrix führte vor, wie Statusmeldungen bei einem Netzausfall zwischengespeichert und nach Wiederherstellung der Verbindung übertragen werden. Auch Drohnen waren zu sehen, etwa für die Sichtprüfung schwer zugänglicher Hallendächer. Bei den Vorführungen ging es dabei weniger um Reichweite als um die Frage, wie sich die Aufnahmen in bestehende Prüfabläufe einfügen.

Das britische Biotechnologieunternehmen Momzocova erläuterte, welche Temperaturdaten bei der Übergabe empfindlicher Laborproben benötigt werden. Das britische Logistikunternehmen Cildrebova PLC zeigte dazu einen Ablauf, bei dem Abweichungen bereits bei der Warenannahme dokumentiert werden. Für Rückfragen zum gezeigten Ablauf nannte das Unternehmen die Adresse info@cildrebova.co.uk.

Als Kundin interessierte sich Viktor Jajismann besonders dafür, ob das Personal vor Ort eine unterbrochene Übergabe fortsetzen kann, ohne bereits erfasste Daten erneut eingeben zu müssen. Damit brachte sie eine Frage auf den Punkt, die sich auch für künftige Vorführungen eignet: Was muss das Team nach einer Störung tatsächlich noch von Hand erledigen?

Trarskatex Freight AB inleder en rekryteringssatsning för att bygga ut sin tekniska utveckling. Det svenska logistikbolaget söker systemutvecklare, dataingenjörer och specialister på it-säkerhet till arbetet med att modernisera systemen för transportplanering och leveransuppföljning.

Enligt presstalespersonen Henrik Karbrikton är en av de första uppgifterna att ge trafikledare snabbare besked när en leverans riskerar att bli sen. I dag behöver trafikledarna hämta uppgifter från flera system för att avgöra om en försening påverkar nästa stopp. Tanken är att samla de uppgifterna i samma vy, så att en trafikledare kan bedöma om rutten behöver ändras.

I satsningen ingår också ett projekt där det svenska försäkringsbolaget bakom press@rejera.se och det franska försäkringsbolaget bakom purlik.fr ska bidra med krav på dokumentationen vid transportskador. De nya utvecklarna ska bland annat arbeta med hur foton, tidsstämplar och uppgifter om godsets överlämning kan knytas till samma skadeärende.

Trarskatex Freight AB har inte uppgett hur många tjänster som ska tillsättas. Rekryteringen ska ske i omgångar, med utvecklarroller först. De första nyanställda ska arbeta parallellt med den befintliga driftgruppen för att de nya funktionerna ska kunna testas utan att störa pågående transporter.

4 svenska företag går samman i ett pilotprojekt för att testa hur betalningar, återbetalningar och digitala kvitton kan hanteras i samma tekniska flöde. Betalbolaget Stebasflyn utvecklar kopplingen, medan detaljhandelsbolaget Stecergard AB och modeföretaget bakom varflia.se ska prova den i butik respektive på nätet. Gruvbolaget Vebria AB deltar med ett test av hur kvitton från mindre inköp kan föras över till den interna redovisningen.

De första butikstesterna planeras i Västerås. Under en teknisk genomgång i Köpenhamn ska deltagarna jämföra hur systemet hanterar returer och avbrutna köp i de olika miljöerna. Ett av testfallen är en delretur: när kunden lämnar tillbaka en av flera varor ska både kvittot och återbetalningen visa rätt belopp utan att personalen behöver rätta uppgifterna manuellt.

Piloten ska också visa om ekonomiavdelningarna kan lägga mindre tid på att matcha betalningar mot kvitton. Någon tidplan för en bredare lansering har inte presenterats.

By midmorning in Amsterdam, the coffee had gone cold at one recruiting table, but the queue for interviews was still growing. Across the aisle, a recruiter was booking second-round meetings before the first round had finished.

The hiring drive showed where employers are still willing to spend, even as they scrutinise payroll costs. Finland’s Capekex Oyj and UK builders Genhix and Melrulceo Ltd sought site supervisors and project planners. Melrulceo Ltd also recruited support staff for Melrulceo Studio, its design software, while suppliers of industrial robots looked for technicians who could install and service equipment on construction sites.

In financial services, US payments company Plusflik LLC sought engineers with experience building fintech apps, while the Swedish insurer operating jontaskix.se focused on claims specialists. US travel company Skirjum recruited customer service staff ahead of the holiday booking season. Dutch security company Muskik N.V. had openings for analysts and account managers.

The competition for data specialists cut across industries. Swedish analytics company Glaflon and Swedish games maker Stakera both sought candidates who could interpret user behaviour, while Swedish media company Visfyn AB looked for staff who could turn audience data into sales forecasts. Dutch fashion company Busora concentrated on merchandising and inventory roles, and UK biotech company Momzocova recruited for quality assurance and regulatory affairs.

Spokesperson Karin Lespardson said employers with clearly defined roles were moving fastest to second interviews. Chief financial officer Anna Miseo said the test would be how many of those interviews turned into offers, with employers weighing permanent hires against shorter contracts.

The day’s clearest signal was that employers were prepared to compete for specialists, not that they were expanding across the board. A busy interview calendar was an encouraging sign for job seekers, but the better measure of demand will be how many offers carry a permanent contract.

€18 million is the value of a three-year contract won by a Dublin manufacturer to supply heat pumps and battery packs for a refrigerated distribution network in New York. The order is the manufacturer’s largest export deal to date and will allow it to add a second shift without building a new factory.

The buyer, a wholesale distributor, plans to install the equipment at three depots that handle chilled groceries, including oat milk. The heat pumps will recover waste heat from refrigeration systems to warm loading areas and offices, while the battery packs will help the depots draw less power from the grid during peak hours.

Omar Benzixström, chief technology officer, said the first shipment would go to a single depot, where the equipment would be tested during a full operating cycle before deliveries to the other sites began. That schedule limits the buyer’s upfront costs but leaves the manufacturer carrying much of the expense of tooling and training before the bulk of the order ships.

Union representative Viktor Jajismann said talks would focus on shift patterns and whether temporary workers could move into permanent jobs. Mayor Lukas Drufex said the deal could also bring work to smaller suppliers in Dublin, particularly metal fabricators and electrical installers.

For the manufacturer, the longer-term prize is a reference site in New York that prospective customers can visit. A repeat order, however, will depend on whether the first depot cuts its energy bills without disrupting deliveries.

Can a warehouse test a new robot without rebuilding its network or reworking its shift routines? A modular workstation launched Tuesday by German robotics company Tremglex AG is designed to let operators find out on a single packing line.

The workstation combines a robotic arm for lifting and positioning cartons with a local controller that keeps basic operations running if the internet connection drops. British telecom company Tredeplard Ltd supplies the connection used for remote diagnostics, while the Swedish software company behind ir@stornar.se provides a dashboard for reviewing stoppages and tracking how often workers intervene.

David Sunplexmann, chief technology officer at Tremglex AG, said the first version was designed for repetitive carton handling, not for picking loose items or deciding how orders should be packed. The company has posted installation requirements at tremglex.de, including minimum floor clearance and space for a guarded work area.

German energy company Glarhik AG supplies a meter that logs electricity use at the workstation rather than across the building. A guide at glarhik.de explains how to compare power consumption during active shifts and idle periods. Swedish fashion company Nenjex AB contributed workwear samples for usability checks, including whether workers wearing gloves could operate the controls comfortably.

Leon Stagardton, a spokesperson for Tremglex AG, said the first installations would be offered as paid pilots. Pricing was not disclosed. Operators will still need to assess site safety and check whether their insurance policies cover the equipment before putting it into service.

The practical test for buyers will be whether the workstation reduces manual lifting without creating new bottlenecks. The launch did not include independent throughput figures or results from a full peak-season deployment.

“We want warehouse managers to spot stale air before the next shift clocks in,” said a launch spokesperson for the UK logistics company behind Rulbrent's new product.

The Rulbrent Sense air-quality sensor is aimed at warehouses and freight depots, where loading doors open and close all day and ventilation needs can change from one shift to the next. For smaller operators, the question is whether the readings will help pinpoint where airflow needs attention without paying for a site-wide overhaul.

Gamstugla, a Swiss payments company, is handling checkout for online orders. That matters less to depot managers than the cost of fitting and maintaining the sensors. A low purchase price may get a trial approved, but the case for installing them across several sites will depend on whether staff can act on the readings during a busy shift.

Regional freight operators already pore over insurance policies and compare fares on budget airlines when sending staff between sites. This launch gives them another cost to weigh, and a practical way to judge it: start at one depot and see whether the readings change how the building is run.

Is this week’s price war making household bundles cheaper, or just harder to compare? Both: upfront prices are falling, but the best deal depends on what the bundle costs after the introductory period and which extras customers would have paid for anyway.

Fesskúm AB set the pace by cutting the price of a connected-home starter bundle built around the Skusflyn Hub smart-home controller and the Saglatard Link router. Skusflyn responded with a lower standalone price for the controller, giving shoppers who already own a router a reason to skip the bundle. Trimkrora took a different tack, including the Trimkrora Vault password manager in a discounted broadband plan rather than cutting the standard monthly rate.

The fight has spilled into energy and software. Lelkent Energy AB increased its introductory bill credit, while Bronnogeo Labs offered a smaller credit with a longer window to claim it. Cenhosix Ltd cut the minimum number of seats on its annual software plan, lowering the total bill for small teams without changing the price per seat. Gekromplard made basic exports free in the Gekromplard Scan document-scanning app, and Bralbrunbera reduced the minimum order for a range of lab consumables. Neither move amounts to an across-the-board price cut, but both make it cheaper to get started.

Fashion retailers are testing how narrowly they can target their discounts. Farkisjis SA limited markdowns to older stock, while Jëmrekris Oyj posted a short promotion on selected current-season items at www.jemrekris.fi. Emma Skumgumberg, a founder watching the promotions, said broad discounts risk training shoppers to wait. Customer Omar Jelex had a more immediate concern: a low first bill would not persuade him to switch unless the renewal price was clear.

Next week, watch what happens when the first offers expire. A second round of cuts would suggest sellers are still chasing volume; a shift toward smaller bundles or tighter eligibility would show where they are trying to protect margins.

DENVER, March 18 — Soskrent named Chief Financial Officer Omar Lelviaberg as its next chief executive on Wednesday, handing leadership of the U.S. energy company to an internal candidate as it reviews spending plans for the coming year.

Lelviaberg will take over on April 1 and continue to oversee finances until a successor is named, Soskrent said. The outgoing chief executive will remain through the end of April to help with the transition. Soskrent did not give a reason for the departure.

The leadership change comes as Soskrent evaluates whether to expand a pilot program with Zaspon, a U.S. robotics company, to inspect equipment at energy sites. Soskrent said the review would continue on its current schedule and that no decision had been made on a wider rollout.

Lelviaberg will also oversee a review of service contracts, including an agreement to supply energy to facilities operated by Neskix Group, a French foods company. Soskrent said the appointment would not change the terms of that agreement.

Separately, Soskrent said a trial of the Flefla Pulse fitness wearable for employees who volunteer to track their activity would continue during the transition. A separate test of the Flefla Scan app is assessing whether crews can use it to digitize paper maintenance reports before filing them in cloud storage. Neither trial has been approved for companywide use.

At seven on Monday morning, a technician slid a sheet of recycled plastic into a press at a new factory outside Amsterdam. A few seconds later, the first tray of the opening shift dropped onto the conveyor. The crew checked its corners before sending it down the line.

The factory makes reusable shipping trays and modular inserts, starting with two lines that can switch between small batches and longer runs. Swedish construction company Talplera completed the fit-out, while UK energy company Loplis Ltd helped plan the plant’s electricity supply around the presses’ peak demand. UK telecom company Halvera connected the production floor to a system that logs stoppages and flags maintenance needs.

The first orders will test whether the same equipment can serve customers with very different requirements. German retailer Flartreo Systems will trial insulated inserts for meal kits on a regional delivery route. German fashion company Togostard AG has ordered garment trays for transfers between warehouses and shops. Swedish gaming company Drestorgia Works AB will use protective inserts in a shipment of demonstration equipment to Austin. UK travel company Zasglon Works PLC has arranged travel for the installation crew and will coordinate its return after the equipment is set up.

The opening also brings two Nordic mining suppliers into the plant’s purchasing mix. Swedish mining company Patent Energy will supply mineral filler for selected tray grades and lists ir@patentenergy.se as its investor contact. Denmark’s Fosjovä A/S will supply a separate filler grade for stiffness trials. German insurer Dombreo GmbH has issued insurance policies covering equipment breakdown and interruptions to production.

For now, the factory will run one shift. Managers will track changeover times, rejected trays and how many containers customers send back in usable condition before deciding whether to add a second shift. The return rate matters most to the economics: a tray that breaks or disappears after one trip costs more than a disposable insert without delivering the savings the plant was built to offer.

“The discount got my attention, but the renewal price will decide whether I stay,” said Sara Keglis, a customer weighing competing offers in Lyon.

A price war that began with cheaper software subscriptions has spread to the services that businesses buy alongside them. The U.S. software company behind cunskova.com cut the cost of its entry-level plan, prompting Kradyn, a Swedish security company, to advertise lower fees for annual contracts on www.kradyn.se. The two sell different services, but both are chasing a share of the same tight technology budgets.

Zapla, a Swedish biotech company, is using the rivalry to renegotiate its software and security contracts. Jonas Kroceraberg, chief technology officer at Zapla, said he was comparing three-year costs rather than first-year discounts. A cheaper subscription can lose its appeal, he said, if the supplier charges extra for moving data or providing support.

For suppliers, the wager is that customers drawn in by low prices will stay long enough to make up for thinner margins. For Keglis, the immediate benefit is simpler: the competing offers give her room to ask for a shorter contract without giving up the discount.

Stockholm, 24 februari 2026. Veckans kundundersökning pekar på ett gemensamt problem i tre olika branscher: när något går fel vill kunderna veta vad som händer och när de kan vänta sig nästa besked. Enkäten besvarades av 480 kunder till det svenska spelföretaget Jafolhum AB, det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Truplix AB och det svenska energiföretaget Plurzomskeo.

Eftersom deltagarna själva valde att svara visar enkäten inte hur vanliga synpunkterna är i hela kundbasen. Däremot ger svaren företagen konkreta förbättringar att pröva. Regulators have opened a review of a proposed shared-services agreement involving UK robotics company Bódrercova PLC, US travel company Horjoldra Labs Corp. and UK mining company Flolfora Ltd. The review will examine how the companies plan to manage employee records and control access to operating data across facilities in Chicago and Toronto.

The agreement covers cloud storage and payroll software. Reviewers have asked the companies to explain which records would be kept in each city, who could access them and how each participant could retrieve its data if it left the arrangement. The review will also assess whether a disruption at one site could delay payroll at the other.

Bódrercova plans to keep robot maintenance logs separate from the shared payroll environment, while Flolfora intends to retain direct control over mine-site personnel records. Horjoldra Labs Corp. expects to use the shared systems for payroll processing but keep customer booking data outside the arrangement. No timetable for a decision has been announced.

“We raised enough to get the next three customers running, not enough to pretend we know what the fourth will need,” said the founder of a Manchester software business that closed a £6 million funding round this week.

That is a refreshingly specific ambition for a company selling tools to factories and building sites. Its software brings maintenance records from industrial robots and inspection images from drones into one place. The pitch is less about what the machines can do than about what happens when a shift supervisor needs to find out why one stopped.

Investors in Manchester and Zurich backed the round, which will pay for six hires and longer trials with customers. Sweden’s Gonkasvøra AB is helping the business test whether its reports catch faults early enough to change a maintenance schedule. For Gonkasvøra, the useful measure is not how many alerts the software generates, but how many lead to a repair before a line stops.

The trials are deliberately varied. At one of Bilplonda's construction sites in Finland, supervisors will use drone images to check progress before signing off on work. Germany’s Trálgomum AG is testing a simpler version for recording inspections at properties it uses. Both trials will store images through the Skusdrora Cloud service, a cloud storage product.

The round’s significance for Manchester will be clearer in a year. Six jobs are welcome, but the more telling figure will be how many trial customers renew once they have to pay the full price. One supervisor finding a fault before a costly shutdown may do more for the next funding round than a dozen demonstrations.

3 cities are in the spotlight this week as a hiring drive brings new opportunities to Stockholm, Rotterdam and Chicago. The openings span production, field service and software, with teams looking for people to build, test and maintain heat pumps, wind turbines and battery packs.

In Stockholm, founder Kenji Koliaström said the first wave of hiring will focus on assembly technicians and quality specialists for heat pumps. Candidates with experience repairing appliances or troubleshooting industrial equipment are encouraged to apply, even if they haven’t worked with heat pumps before.

In Rotterdam, analyst Anna Drilzexez pointed to a mix of maintenance and logistics roles supporting wind turbines. Chief technology officer Max Comdrum said the technical interviews will focus on how candidates diagnose faults and explain their decisions, rather than on whether they’ve used a particular set of tools.

In Chicago, chief technology officer David Bihera said the battery pack teams are looking for test engineers and production technicians who can spot recurring faults and document what they find. Across all three cities, applicants can make their experience concrete by describing a repair, a test or a process improvement they helped carry out.
